For arbitrary binary relations, we show that singleton closures coincide with reachable sets and that the common intersection of all singleton closures consists exactly of the globally reachable points. In the Goldbach setting, this yields a topological characterization of the conjecture in terms of the distinguished point \(6\). In particular, the strong Goldbach conjecture is equivalent to the associated relational space being non-\(wR_0\) and connected. We also obtain compactness and supercompactness criteria in terms of the set of possible Goldbach exceptions.

papers.title: Elliptic closed geodesics on non-negatively curved Finsler manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a compact simply-connected manifold $(M,F)$ with a bumpy irreversible Finsler metric $F$ whose flag curvature $K$ satisfies $K\ge 0$ and $H^*(M;\Q)\cong T_{d,n+1}(x)$ for some $d\in2\N$ and $n\in\N$ carries exactly $\frac{dn(n+1)}{2}$ (the number of closed geodesics in Katok's example) closed geodesics, then there are at least $2$ irrationally elliptic closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

papers.title: Integrable distortion I: Weil--Petersson circle homeomorphisms and the Schoen conjecture
papers.abstract:
A circle homeomorphism $\beta:\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is Weil--Petersson if it has a quasiconformal disk extension whose Beltrami coefficient is square integrable for hyperbolic area. We minimise the hyperbolic anti-holomorphic energy \[ E_2(h)=\int_\mathbb{D}\eta(h)|h_{\bar w}|^2,dA, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \int_\mathbb{D}\frac{|\mu_f|^2}{1-|\mu_f|^2},dA_\eta,\quad f=h^{-1}, \] over all monotone Sobolev maps with boundary values $\beta$. For Weil--Petersson data, the unique minimiser is a real analytic hyperbolic harmonic diffeomorphism, globally quasiconformal and asymptotically conformal, with an explicit dilatation bound in terms of any admissible barrier's energy. We prove that a circle homeomorphism is Weil--Petersson if and only if it admits a finite-distortion homeomorphic extension satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{K}_F-1),dA_\eta<\infty. \] For every $p>1$, the boundary values of a finite-distortion homeomorphism satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}|\mu_F|^p(1-|\mu_F|^2)^{-p_*/2},dA_\eta<\infty \] lie in Guo's $p$-integrable Teichm"uller space $T^p$. A capacity estimate for boundary moduli for the quasisymmetric ratio yields a derivative-free characterisation of $T^p$, essentially Bishop's theorem when $p=2$. The minimum defines a M"obius-invariant boundary energy, quantitatively comparable to the weighted square norm of the minimiser's Hopf differential.
  For arbitrary quasisymmetric data, we prove Markovi'c's theorem (the Schoen conjecture) by approximation with our smooth quadratic minimisers. Mori's theorem and the mean-value property of a logarithm verify the averaged-distance hypothesis in Riestenberg--Smillie's interior comparison, giving explicit displacement, energy-density and dilatation bounds in terms of the quasisymmetry constant. The nonquadratic ($p\neq2$) theory is developed in Part~II.

papers.title: Infinitesimally polar Killing foliations via geometric resolutions
papers.authors: Francisco C. Caramello Jr., Laura Ribeiro dos Santos
papers.abstract: We establish the strong Molino conjecture for complete infinitesimally polar singular Riemannian foliations and identify their Molino sheaves with those of their geometric resolutions. The resolution preserves basic and equivariant basic cohomology and transverse curvature bounds. These comparisons yield orbifold models and approximations of leaf-closure spaces, Euler localization, closed-leaf existence and Euler positivity under positive curvature, and transverse sphere theorems. Maximal defect gives a closed-ball leaf-closure space. Further applications include fundamental-group growth bounds and closedness under nonpositive transverse Ricci curvature that is negative definite at one regular point.

papers.title: Two Generalizations of the G_0 Dichotomy
papers.abstract: We give classical proofs of the generalizations of the $\mathbb{G}_0$ dichotomy to $\kappa$-Souslin digraphs and uniformly analytic sequences of digraphs indexed by $\kappa^{\mathbb{N}}$.

papers.title: Equivariant deformation theory and deformations of homogeneous varieties
papers.abstract: We show that, in characteristic $p$, almost all projective homogeneous varieties under a reductive group and with non-reduced stabilizer do not lift to characteristic $p^2$. To this end, first we develop a general framework for equivariant deformation theory, leading to practical criteria ensuring that the deformations of a scheme come with deformations of a group scheme action. Second, we establish a formula to compute the cohomology of equivariant vector bundles over projective homogeneous varieties with non-reduced stabilizer, enabling us to determine the $G$-module structure of the first cohomology groups of their tangent bundles.

papers.title: Minimal immersions by first eigenfunctions of Riemann surfaces with large conformal automorphism groups. The Klein quartic
papers.abstract:
Minimal immersions of closed surfaces into spheres by first eigenfunctions play an important role in both the theory of minimal surfaces and spectral geometry. In this paper, we establish the existence of equivariant conformal minimal immersions of this type for Hurwitz surfaces and other families of %Riemann surfaces with large automorphism group.
  Finally, we explicitly construct a conformal minimal equivariant immersion of the Klein quartic into the unit sphere $S^{7}$ by first eigenfunctions. Ths immersion is a natural candidate for maximizing the normalized $\lambda_1$ among closed genus-3 surfaces.

papers.title: Biquandle Image Quivers
papers.authors: Geunyoung Kim, Sam Nelson, Puttipong Pongtanapaisan
papers.abstract: We introduce a new family of weighted quiver-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and link, surface-knots and surface-links, and immersed surface-knots and surface-links associated to finite biquandles. We derive several polynomial invariants from these quivers via decategorification. We provide examples to illustrate the computation of the invariant as well as toy examples showing tables of invariant values for small biquandles.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
papers.abstract: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

papers.title: Mixed Unfitted finite element approximation of band structures in photonic crystals
papers.authors: Yuyan Zou, Luke G. Bennetts, Hailong Guo
papers.abstract: Photonic crystals are periodic dielectric structures whose optical properties are characterized by Maxwell eigenvalue problems with discontinuous material coefficients. For arbitrarily shaped inclusions, their numerical solution remains challenging due to costly mesh generation and remeshing as the geometry changes. In this paper, we address this challenge by developing a mixed unfitted finite element method based on the Floquet-Bloch transform. Our method uses a uniform background mesh independent of the inclusion geometry, thereby avoiding interface-fitted meshing and allowing us to impose the periodic boundary condition through a direct identification of degrees of freedom. A key feature of our construction is that the resulting finite element pairs preserve the de Rham commuting relation for the shifted operator. This structure enables us to establish an inf-sup condition uniformly with respect to the cut position and, in particular, to rule out spurious modes. We further establish optimal convergence of the eigenvalues and eigenspaces, with constants independent of both the mesh size and the position of the interface. Finally, we present extensive numerical experiments in two and three dimensions to validate our theoretical results and demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method.

papers.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
papers.authors: Omid Amini, Matthieu Piquerez, Lyuhui Wu
papers.abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.

papers.title: Negative Values of Wahl's Second Chern Number for Normal Surface Singularities
papers.abstract: We disprove Wahl's 1993 vanishing conjecture, open for more than thirty years, which asserts that $c_2^w(X)=0$ for every nonquotient normal surface singularity. Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve with a nontrivial involution having $r>0$ fixed points, and put $d=2g(C)-2$. If $d>r$, the union of the diagonal and the graph of the involution in $C\times C$ has negative definite intersection matrix and can be analytically contracted to a normal surface singularity $(X,o)$. A direct relative Chern-class computation and Wahl's residue formula give $c_2^w(X)=-r(d+r)/(d-r)$. An explicit curve of genus four gives $c_2^w(X)=-4$. Branched double covers of a fixed curve of genus two yield examples with $c_2^w(X_m)=-2m(m+1)$, so these values are unbounded below. We give the construction and intersection calculations in detail, as well as a line-bundle filtration realizing the negative value.

papers.title: Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.

papers.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-D\"oring combustion equations
papers.abstract: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-D\"oring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.

papers.title: Non-existence of negative weight derivations on Jacobian algebras
papers.authors: Bingyi Chen, Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Huaiqing Zuo
papers.abstract: Let $S=\mathbb K[x_1,\cdots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables with positive integer weights over a field $\mathbb K$ of characteristic zero. Let $f\in S$ be a weighted homogeneous polynomial such that the Jacobian algebra $$A=\left.S \middle/ \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1},\cdots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\right)\right.$$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K$-vector space. We prove that $A$ has no nonzero negative weight derivation, which confirms a conjecture of the third author. An immediate consequence of this conjecture is the micro-local characterization of quasi-homogeneous singularities.

papers.title: Which Immersions into Euclidean Space are Boundary Immersions?
papers.abstract: Here we study the problem of whether a given codimension one immersion $f$ of a closed and connected manifold into Euclidean space can be extended to an equidimensional immersion $F$ of some compact manifold $M$ whose restriction to the boundary parameterizes the image $S$ of $f$. Such an extension $F$ exists if and only if (i) simple conditions on orientations and wrapping numbers are satisfied and (ii) a distinguished finite subset of the first cohomology of $S$ with coefficients in a certain sheaf of finite groups contains the preferred point.

papers.title: Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1
papers.abstract: We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.

papers.title: Cohomology and Representation Theory for Lie Superalgebras
papers.abstract:
In this paper the authors describe two general frameworks for studying algebraic supergroup and Lie superalgebra representations. These encompass the well-known rational representations for a reductive algebraic group and the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}$ for semisimple Lie algebras. Many of the important developments will be surveyed and a blueprint for these new approaches will be provided.
  The existence of odd elements simply add an additional layer of difficulty. The authors prove that the calculation of the sheaf cohomology in the super setting for the rational category is equivalent to understanding the Lie superalgebra cohomology. This generalizes the well-known fact that the classical Bott-Borel-Weil theorem is equivalent to Kostant's theorem. Furthermore, for the parabolic Category ${\mathcal O}^{\mathfrak p}$ where ${\mathfrak p}$ is a principal parabolic, the authors show that the characters of simple modules can be obtained by looking at natural generalizations of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials given by extensions between simple modules and costandard modules arising from the underlying costandardly stratified category.

papers.title: PMR-Aided Shifted-Pruning SCL-Flip Decoding for CRC-Aided Polar Codes
papers.authors: Niloufar Hosseinzadeh, Mohammad Morsali, Mohsen Moradi, Hessam Mahdavifar
papers.abstract: We propose a posterior-mass rescue (PMR)-aided shifted-pruning SCL-flip decoder for CRC-aided polar codes. After CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) and differential-metric shifted-pruning recovery fail to find a CRC-valid candidate, PMR locally continues discarded prefixes stored during the initial CA-SCL pass, ranked by estimated posterior mass, without increasing the shifted-pruning retry budget. Simulation results for a (128, 64) code with the Reed-Muller (RM) rate profile and a (256, 128) code with the polarization-weight (PW) rate profile, both using an 11-bit CRC, show lower observed FER than SCLF-Diff (T = 15) and the considered literature baselines under the evaluated recovery budgets, with observed FER close to that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20). At the reported moderate and high SNRs, the average reconstruction-aware path-step count is within a few percent of that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20), while at 2.0 dB it is 9.4% and 4.3% higher for the two codes, respectively. The proposed decoder also has a larger worst-case path-step bound.

papers.title: Phase diagram and fluctuations in the cubic mean field Ising model
papers.authors: Van Hao Can, Viet Tinh Dang
papers.abstract: We study the cubic mean field Ising model with three body and two body interactions and an external field. Our main result is a complete classification of the global maximizers of the variational pressure in the full three-parameter region $(K,J,h)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$. We identify a coexistence surface with two nondegenerate global maximizers and a critical curve with a unique quartically degenerate maximizer; elsewhere the maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. This extends the phase diagrams previously obtained on two-parameter subfamilies \cite{CMO24,O24}. As applications of the general results in \cite{CR}, we give explicit magnetization fluctuation theorems and asymptotic distributions for one-parameter maximum likelihood estimators in the resulting regimes.

papers.title: The classification of taut surface singularities via representations from logarithmic vector fields
papers.abstract: We study logarithmic vector fields on exceptional cycles through finite-dimensional representations and recover Laufer's classification of taut normal complex surface singularities. For graphs with two nodes, restriction maps define representations of a fixed quiver, with dimensions bounded independently of the number of components and their self-intersections. We identify restriction cohomology with an extension group and use interval decomposition to reduce its vanishing to interpolation on a rational chain. These calculations determine the classification conditions, and vanishing on every analytic realization proves sufficiency, including the nonrational cases. The obstruction cycles also give a uniform criterion: a graph is taut if and only if $H^1(5E,S_X|_{5E})=0$ for every analytic realization, where $S_X$ is the ambient logarithmic tangent bundle. We prove that five is the smallest positive integer for which this criterion holds for all graphs.

papers.title: The factorial separation conjecture
papers.abstract: We propose the Factorial Separation Conjecture (FSC), a strict strengthening of earlier factorial gap conjectures: \[ |n!-m^k|>n \] for all integers $n\ge8$ and $m,k\ge2$. The inequality excludes every displacement up to and including the factorial index. We prove the conjecture unconditionally for exponents divisible by three, for even exponents at least four, and for every exponent at least two when the largest prime divisor of the base is at most $n+2$. For exponents divisible by five, we prove the finite interval $8\le n\le1100$ and all sufficiently large indices, with an effective but uncomputed threshold. The conclusion for every $n\ge8$ and every exponent divisible by five is proved under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for a specified family of Dedekind zeta functions. Here GRH asserts that their nontrivial zeros have real part $1/2$. The arguments combine valuations, cyclotomic factorizations, cubic reciprocity, character estimates and explicit formulas. All finite comparisons are justified in the text. The general conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Blow-up of damped semilinear wave equation with short range potential and critical power nonlinearity
papers.authors: Ikeda Masahiro, Tu Ziheng, Wang Chengbo
papers.abstract: The present paper is devoted to the study of a semilinear wave equation with spatially dependent scattering damping and a short-range potential, with particular focus on determining the critical exponent for the power-type nonlinearity. By employing the test function method, we establish wave-type blow-up results and derive lifespan estimates at the critical level. The main contribution of this work lies in providing a uniform asymptotic analysis for a family of test functions, which is achieved through a detailed investigation of a parametric second-order elliptic equation. As a further novelty, we relax the radial symmetry condition conventionally imposed on the coefficients $D$ and $V$ by resorting to the comparison principle in conjunction with a monotone exhaustion argument.

papers.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study optimization over a finite composition of implicit response maps generated by smooth potentials with strongly monotone signed gradients. This class includes chains mixing strongly convex minimization and strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses. We propose a fully first-order method based on recursively perturbed response solves. The central issue is stability under inexact response solves: a downstream adjoint error changes the perturbation vector of the next upstream perturbed problem. We establish coupled bounds for the forward response errors and backward errors in the scaled response differences whose coefficients remain bounded as the perturbation parameter $\delta$ decreases. A triangular Lyapunov construction combines these bounds with the $O(\delta)$ bias of the exact perturbation estimator. For the warm-started method with finitely many inner iterations, this gives $\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla\Phi(x^k)\|^2 \leq O(K^{-1})+O(\delta^2).$ Thus, for fixed problem data and finite depth, $\delta=O(\epsilon)$ yields an $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ outer-iteration dependence. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.authors: Zhuoni Chi, Shurui Liu, Ping Nie
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: On the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of some residual intersections
papers.authors: Manav Batavia, Vaibhav Pandey, Uli Walther
papers.abstract:
We determine the arithmetic rank and cohomological dimension of each generic residual intersection of the ideal of submaximal Pfaffians of an alternating matrix of variables. This ideal fails to be a set-theoretic complete intersection. Our methods yield several structural results: in characteristic zero, we compute the $D$-module length of the top local cohomology module supported at this ideal and show that over the integers, it admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space structure. In particular, the top local cohomology module has no integer torsion. We also establish the $F$-regularity of the generic residual intersection rings considered here.
  Further, for each admissible height $s$, we construct $s$-residual intersections of complete intersection ideals and height three Gorenstein ideals that are set-theoretic complete intersections in any characteristic. Finally, we pose a general question of independent interest concerning the behaviour of arithmetic rank.

papers.title: A Unifying View of Distributionally Robust Optimization for Probability Smoothing via Maximum Entropy
papers.authors: Kota Kurihara, Yuya Yamakawa, Yoichi Izunaga
papers.abstract: The probability smoothing problem seeks estimators that assign positive probability to all categories, including those unobserved in a finite sample. In our previous work, we established that the estimator derived from distributionally robust optimization (DRO) with a $q$-norm ambiguity set ($q$-DRO) satisfies the axioms of Positivity, Symmetry, and Order Preservation, while relaxing the rigid Ratio Preservation axiom characterizing Laplace smoothing. In this paper, we observe that Symmetry itself imposes a strong constraint: it forces all unobserved categories to receive identical probability regardless of their relation to observed categories. Motivated by this observation, we study DRO with an optimal transport ambiguity set (OT-DRO), which incorporates inter-category dissimilarities through a cost matrix and thereby enables structure-respecting smoothing. We derive a tractable dual reformulation of OT-DRO as an empirical cross-entropy minimization with a Lipschitz-type penalty on the log-probability vector, and we identify an explicit threshold on the robustness radius at which the optimal estimator reduces to the uniform distribution, paralleling the threshold established for $q$-DRO. We then show, through Sion's minimax theorem, that DRO for probability smoothing over any compact convex ambiguity set that contains a strictly positive distribution is equivalent to entropy maximization over that set. This unifying perspective explains the parallel threshold structure in $q$-DRO and OT-DRO.

papers.title: On the effects of rotation on stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the half spaces in scale-critical spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier--Stokes equations with the Coriolis force in the half space with the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We show the existence of a unique small solution in the scale-critical Besov spaces. In particular, for any boundary data with only the normal component assumed to be sufficiently small, and for any external forces, we establish the well-posedness of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary value problem when the speed of rotation is sufficiently large. In the proof, to exploit the stabilizing effect of the Coriolis term, we employ two explicit formulas depending on the relation between the horizontal frequency and the magnitude of the rotation speed.

papers.title: Global hydrodynamic limit of the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system with large data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we aim to investigate the global-in-time hydrodynamic limit of the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system for light particles. With a modified micro-macro decomposition yielding uniform a priori estimates with respect to the Deborah number $\varepsilon$, we prove that the solution of the original system tends to that of the target system, i.e., the incompressible Navier-Stokes/Kramers-Smoluchowski system, as Deborah number goes to zero, and that quantitative convergence rates are obtained in the $L_{x,v,t}^\infty$ norm. Compared with the existing results that the convergence is from ``weak solution" to ``strong solution", the convergence results in the present work are further developed globally in time from ``strong solution" to ``strong solution" with vacuum (i.e., the macroscopic particle density may vanish at far field or at any point) and large initial data for both the original system and the target system. In addition, the ill-prepared initial data for the microscopic component of the kinetic quantity are allowed.

papers.title: Geometric and measure-theoretic characterizations of the measure-determining property of balls in metric spaces
papers.abstract: The question of what structural properties drive the collection of open or closed balls to uniquely determine Borel probability measures on a metric space, the ball property, has a long history in measure theory. While various sufficient conditions have been known since the 1970s, and it was shown by Preiss and Ti\v{s}er (1991) that it holds for all separable Banach spaces, Davies (1971) constructed a famous counterexample that shows it can fail on compact metric spaces. It was only recently established in van Delft (2026) that metric spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding must possess the ball property. This article provides a comprehensive structural and measure-theoretic characterization of the ball property. First, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the ball property to fail: the collection of balls must possess sufficient combinatorial capacity, which we define as charged dyadic shattering. Second, by characterizing the ball property via $\lambda$-systems, we place classical vector space results within a unified context. Building on this to understand spaces that have the topological capacity but lack linear or geometric rigidity required to force ball-annihilating measures to zero, we relate the metric outer measure to the cylinder outer measure on countable products of Polish spaces, deriving necessary and sufficient measure-theoretic conditions for the ball property to hold. This allows us to derive a structural taxonomy on the decoupling of the metric outer measure from the cylinder outer measure. This is subsequently used to deconstruct Davies' counterexample. Finally, we introduce a minimal combinatorial generalization of the ball property, the $n$th order ball property, and show that such classes can fully recover measure determination in highly pathological constructions like Davies' counterexample.

papers.title: Sharp Holder regularity for autonomous Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a domain and let $\mathcal H:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be Lipschitz with constant $0<k<1$. We prove that every weak $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solution of the autonomous Beltrami equation $f_{\bar z}=\mathcal H(f_z)$ belongs to $C^{1,\gamma}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, where $\gamma=3/(2K+1)$ and $K=(1+k)/(1-k)$. The exponent is optimal, resolving the conjecture of Astala, Clop, Faraco, J\"a\"askel\"ainen and Koski.

papers.title: Rational Points on Drinfeld Modular Curves of Prime Level
papers.abstract: Let $q \ge 3$ be a prime power and let $\mathfrak{p} \subset \mathbf{F}_q[T]$ be a nonzero prime ideal of degree $d$. We prove that $Y_0(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T))=\emptyset$ if $d \ge 4$ is even or $d>q$, and that $Y_1(\mathfrak{p})(\mathbf{F}_q(T)) = \emptyset $ for every $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: Big Ramsey degrees and structures in relational languages
papers.abstract: We establish a precompact transfer theorem for big Ramsey structures and a uniform envelope theorem for valuation hypergraphs. These yield big Ramsey structures for generic injective relational structures in languages with finitely many symbols of each positive arity, answering the existence part of Problem~6.3.2 of Balko et al.\ [M.~Balko et al., J.~Eur.~Math.~Soc.\ 28, 2101--2150 (2026)], and refute Conjecture~4.7 of Braunfeld et al.\ [S.~Braunfeld et al., Adv.~Comb., Paper No.~4 (2024)]. We also construct a finitely constrained free amalgamation class in a finite language of maximum arity three whose Fra\"iss\'e limit has infinite singleton big Ramsey degree, giving a negative answer to the existence question in Problem~6.3.3 of Balko et al.

papers.title: The Eighth-Order Evolution Model for Closed Planar Curves
papers.abstract: We consider the $L^2(ds)$ gradient flow of $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$ for smooth closed immersed planar curves. The stationary curves are precisely the multiply covered circles. We give an explicit sufficient condition under which the elastic energy is non-increasing and for each nonzero turning number, explicit small initial scale-invariant energy yields a global smooth solution with bounded positive length and exponential convergence to a fixed multiply covered circle, after reparametrisation. We note that that the qualitative rigidity and convergence results are already contained in the generalised ideal flow theory of McCoy and Wheeler. The present paper gives quantitative measure of small initial data, corrected evolution identities, and a complete argument in the case of the curvature energy $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$.

papers.title: Frobenius Profiles of Polynomial-Multiple MRD Codes
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius intersection profiles of maximum rank distance (MRD) codes arising from ordinary polynomial multiples over finite fields. We prove that every numerically admissible profile is realized within this family over every sufficiently large extension, using a root-exponent pattern independent of the extension degree. A factor-orbit gap formula provides the underlying structural description, while effective extension-degree bounds guarantee realization. We also establish a lower bound valid for all polynomial generators and show that the upper and lower bounds differ by only $O_q(\log n)$ along an infinite family of parameters. Finally, we characterize the generalized Gabidulin members and obtain non-generalized-Gabidulin realizations of every profile with initial loss at least two over infinitely many extensions.

papers.title: Iterative Truncated SVD for Inverse Scattering Problems
papers.authors: Zhinan Han, Ying Liang, Hongkai Zhao
papers.abstract: We propose an iterative truncated SVD (iTSVD) algorithm based on a nonlinear least squares formulation for Newton's method for inverse scattering problems. The key idea is to estimate the effective rank of the corresponding linearized operator (or the Jacobian matrix after discretization), which defines the dimension of the signal space of the associated forward operator. Once the effective rank is estimated, truncated SVD (TSVD) reconstruction in the signal space can be computed efficiently based on fast random SVD (RSVD) -- only requiring matrix-vector multiplication which can be implemented in a matrix-free formulation by solving multiple forward and adjoint problems of the same type. Our analysis and numerical experiments show that iTSVD can markedly improve computational efficiency by reducing the number of iterations and enhance stability by physics/information based inversion. Moreover, the effective rank estimate is naturally model- and data-based. Extensive experiments, including far- or near-field, limited aperture, and random measurement data without or with noise, are presented.

papers.title: Characteristic cycles and non-acyclicity classes for constructible \'etale sheaves
papers.authors: Kaicheng Bao, Jiangnan Xiong, Enlin Yang
papers.abstract: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism between smooth schemes over a perfect field $k$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible sheaf on $X$ and $Z$ a closed subscheme of $X$ such that $f$ is $SS(\mathcal F)$-transversal outside $Z$. We construct a class supported on the non-transversal locus $Z$ by using the characteristic cycle $CC(\mathcal F)$ defined by T. Saito. This class is a geometric counterpart of the non-acyclicity class introduced by the third author and Zhao in [Invent. Math. 240 (2025), 123-191]. Under certain conditions, the formation of this class is compatible with base change and proper pushforward. It also satisfies the Milnor formula and a conductor formula. We conjecture that the image of this geometric class under the cycle class map is the non-acyclicity class. This conjecture can be viewed as a (relative version of) Milnor-type formula for non-isolated singularities. We prove this conjecture when $k$ is algebraically closed, $X$ is quasi-affine and $Y=\mathbb A^1_k$.

papers.title: Linear Group Actions with Exactly One Regular Orbit
papers.authors: Thomas Michael Keller, Jeffrey M. Riedl
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $G$ a finite $p$-group, and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then $p=2^{n}-1$ is a Mersenne prime and $(G,V)$ embeds into $(P_m,V_m)$ for some $m\ge 1$, where $P_m$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the monomial group ${\rm GL}_1(2^{n})\wr S_{p^{m-1}}$ and $V_m$ is its natural module, regarded over ${\Bbb F}_2$. We determine the largest orbit size $p^{x_m}$ of $P_m$ on $V_m$ and the number of orbits of this size, and we construct subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ whose unique regular orbit is a largest orbit of $P_m$; for $p=3$ such subgroups exist for every $m$, whereas for Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ we prove that they exist only for $m\ge 3$. Finally, we classify the subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ with exactly one regular orbit for $m=2$ and, with the help of a computer, for $p=3$ and $m=3$, where there are $13$ such pairs up to isomorphism; for $p=3$ and $m=4$ we show that there are exactly $4914$ conjugacy classes of such subgroups in $P_4$. In particular, such a subgroup is in general not determined by its regular orbit.

papers.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
papers.authors: Jiakun Liu, Junqing Wang, Maolin Zhou
papers.abstract: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and V\'azquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.

papers.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning
papers.authors: Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, Giuseppe Caire
papers.abstract: Secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of users' gradients or model updates without revealing individual values. With user dropouts, correlated random keys protect local gradients while allowing recovery of the desired gradient sum. We consider three phases: key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask elimination. Users establish correlated keys, upload masked gradients, and provide additional messages to eliminate residual aggregate masks. Existing information-theoretic schemes typically design mask-elimination communication for a prescribed dropout threshold and evaluate its cost under worst-case dropouts across the masked-gradient upload and mask-elimination phases. Such designs cannot adjust communication to actual dropout scenarios. Moreover, the randomness and communication costs of establishing correlated keys remain largely unexplored. To address these limitations, we formulate an adaptive secure aggregation framework under the T-colluding security constraint and construct a single scheme that supports all feasible dropout scenarios by adapting its communication to the actual number of dropouts. We establish converse bounds on four resources: key randomness, key-distribution communication, masked-gradient communication, and mask-elimination communication. The latter two bounds are characterized for each realized dropout set in the masked-gradient upload phase. The proposed scheme achieves the optimal masked-gradient communication rate for every feasible dropout scenario and the optimal mask-elimination communication rate in almost all feasible regimes. Its key rate and key-distribution communication rate are each optimal or within a factor of two of their respective information-theoretic optima. These results characterize the fundamental randomness and communication costs of secure aggregation with user dropouts.

papers.title: Combinatorial Calabi flows on infinitely triangulated surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the combinatorial Calabi flow associated with vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces with piecewise Euclidean and piecewise hyperbolic metrics. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $\epsilon$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish short-time existence of smooth solutions and prove uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in the $L^\infty$ norm.

papers.title: Berry--Esseen Bounds for High-Temperature Ising Models
papers.abstract: We consider the nearest-neighbour Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and establish sharp results for the normal approximation of the magnetisation throughout the high-temperature regime. In particular, we establish optimal Berry--Esseen bounds between the magnetisation in an arbitrary finite region and a Gaussian with the corresponding finite-volume variance. These results hold for finite-volume Gibbs measures with arbitrary boundary conditions, as well as for the infinite-volume Gibbs measure. We also determine sharp rates of convergence of the magnetisation in a finite box to a Gaussian with variance given by the infinite-volume susceptibility. For this fixed Gaussian target, we show that, in dimensions $d\ge 3$, periodic boundary conditions yield strictly faster convergence than free boundary conditions. Our approach uses Stein's method to quantify the normal approximation error by analysing the semigroup of the continuous-time Ising heat-bath dynamics.

papers.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems
papers.abstract: We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.

papers.title: On one-dimensional pressureless Euler--Poisson systems: existence for non-semiconvex interaction potentials
papers.authors: Andrew Xie, Emmanuel Alayande, Christopher Chun, Yusen Li, Rohan Mawalkar, Adrian Tudorascu, Adam Van
papers.abstract: One-dimensional Euler-Poisson-type systems with interaction potentials that are repulsive at short range and attractive at long range are useful simplified models that describe biological aggregation. In the current work we employ new techniques to treat compactly supported solutions in the case where the potential is $C^1$ and satisfies certain coercivity growth conditions although it is not necessarily $c$-convex, as required in previous work. Central to this approach are uniform bounds on the positions and velocities of discrete sticky-particle solutions to such a system; these may be of independent interest and require less regularity of $W$, namely only $C^{0, 1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The tradeoff, just as in the case of repulsive Euler-Poisson, is that we cannot claim that the emerging solutions are sticky.

papers.title: A Benders decomposition approach for hierarchical k-medoids
papers.abstract: We study a hierarchical clustering problem formulated as a sum of k-medoids objectives. This problem is related to the multi-period p-median problem, but instead of having nested facilities, we consider a hierarchy of nested assignments. We present two Benders formulations from the p-median literature and show how the obtained nested p-median solutions can be converted into hierarchical k-medoids solutions. We validate our methods on various instances. First, we show on small-scale instances that a standard Benders decomposition approach achieves speedups of up to three orders of magnitude over an existing branch-and-price method, while producing hierarchical k-medoids solutions that are at most 5% away from optimality. Second, we present an aggregated Benders heuristic that can handle instances with more than 13,000 observations.

papers.title: Noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for convolution operators under $L_1$-H\"ormander conditions
papers.authors: Guixiang Hong, Liang Wang, Xumin Wang, Bang Xu
papers.abstract:
We prove weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for families of scalar convolution operators acting on operator-valued function spaces. A joint $L_1$-H\"ormander condition, together with a maximal strong type estimate at one exponent $1<r\leq\infty$, suffices. The kernels may be complex-valued and need not have uniformly bounded $L_1$ norms. Under a size condition, the result also yields a weak endpoint estimate for all sharp truncation radii of singular kernels. This resolves, for convolution kernels, the problem mentioned in \cite[Remark~5.5]{parcet09pseudo} and recalled in Parcet's recent survey \cite[Remark~1.3]{Parcet2026ICM}. The proof involves not only a simultaneous dyadic representation of the operators but also a noncommutative maximal weak type $(1,1)$ estimates of the resulting dyadic operators. This approach seems entirely new even in the commutative setting.
  Numerous applications are provided. On the one hand, it yields various maximal inequalities and pointwise convergence results for integrable kernels and dyadic approximations of the identity, monotone $L\log L$ majorants, and Poisson integrals on nilpotent groups and symmetric spaces. On the other hand, via various transference techniques, it implies maximal inequalities for Fourier multipliers, Schur multipliers and double operator integrals, together with bilateral almost uniform convergence of dyadic Fourier summation methods on $L_1$ of group von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Jumps and Iterated Jumps of Perfect Subtrees of Positive Trees
papers.abstract: An infinite (binary) tree is \emph{positive} iff its set of paths is non-null. As an elementary observation, positives trees always have positive perfect subtrees. Given a positive tree of certain complexity, here we present several theorems concerning the distribution of the Turing jumps or iterated Turing jumps of (positive) perfect subtrees of the given tree in the universe of Turing degrees.

papers.title: Lusztig's asymptotic algebra and a cell factorisation for the second lowest two-sided cell in type $\tilde{B}_n$
papers.abstract: We determine Lusztig's asymptotic algebra for the second lowest two-sided cell~$\Delta_1$ in the equal parameter extended affine Weyl group $\tilde{\mathsf{B}}_n$ for all $n\geq 2$, realising it as a full matrix algebra over the representation ring of $\mathsf{Sp}_{2n-2}(\CC)\times C_2$ with $C_2$ the group of order~$2$. Our result is an explicit isomorphism of based rings, determining the image of each basis element $\mathsf{t}_w$ of the asymptotic algebra. As a consequence we verify that Lusztig's original conjecture from 1989 on the structure of the asymptotic algebra holds for this cell. A key ingredient in our proof is a refinement of Shi's description of~$\Delta_1$, giving an explicit parametrisation of the elements of this cell (a \textit{cell factorisation}). This cell factorisation simultaneously describes all intersections of left and right cells, with uniqueness and length-additivity of expressions. Applications include a classification of the involutions in $\Delta_1$, and a calculation of the length generating functions for $\Delta_1$ and the right cells in~$\Delta_1$.

papers.title: A Fourier expansion principle for coherent cohomology of powers of Tate curves
papers.abstract: In the case of the totally degenerate split degenerations given by fibered powers of Tate curves over $\mathbf{Z}[[q^{1/w}]]$, this article proves a Fourier expansion principle that applies to higher coherent (equivariant) cohomology classes of rigidified line bundles on the $\mathbf{Z}((q^{1/w}))$-fiber. We do not require any ampleness hypotheses. This generalizes a previous Fourier expansion principle due to Faltings--Chai that applies only to sections of ample line bundles; that version was used as a key step in their proof of their classification of polarized degenerations and thus in the construction of toroidal compactifications of moduli spaces of polarized abelian varieties. This article can be considered as a theory of Fourier expansions for algebraic theta cocycles associated to possibly indefinite quadratic forms, and has application to arithmetic: in joint work with Venkatesh, we have used it to produce an algebraic theory of Kudla--Millson indefinite modular theta functions.

papers.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $\kappa$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-\kappa-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.

papers.title: Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
papers.authors: Yeoneung Kim, Donghyun Lee, Sung-Jun Son
papers.abstract: We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $\gamma \geq -2$ and the uncut case $\gamma=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.

papers.title: Self-Similar Solutions of the 2D Incompressible Euler Equations via a Lagrangian Construction
papers.authors: Thomas Y. Hou, Xiang Qin, Peicong Song, Wenhan Zhang
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of forward self-similar solutions of the $2$D incompressible Euler equation. For every $1<\alpha<2$ and every real $h\in L^{2/\alpha}(\mathbb{S}^1)$, the construction produces a flow with initial vorticity $|x|^{-\alpha}h(\arg x)$, without smallness or sign assumptions. The argument is based on a fixed-point formulation of backward particle transport from time $t=1$ to $t=0$. Mollifying the Biot--Savart velocity in self-similar variables preserves exact vorticity transport, while symmetrization yields the unforced Euler equation in velocity form even when the ordinary vorticity flux is not locally integrable. The limiting solution admits an almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flow from time zero, with strong local continuity and preservation of signed value distributions and absolutely integrable Casimirs.

papers.title: Computation of Free Boundary Minimal Tori via Extremal Steklov Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: Fraser and Schoen showed that the first Steklov eigenfunctions of a metric maximizing the length-normalized first eigenvalue of a surface with boundary define a free boundary minimal immersion into a Euclidean ball. We develop a method for this extremal problem on surfaces of genus one with $b$ boundary components and use it to compute free boundary minimal tori for $b \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8\}$. By uniformization, the problem is a nonsmooth maximization over the modulus of a flat torus, the centers and radii of $b$ removed disks, and a boundary weight. The eigenvalues are computed with doubly periodic layer potentials, all derivatives follow from a single formula for the underlying pencil of boundary integral operators, and the coalescence of eigenvalues at a maximizer is handled by a two-stage nonsmooth method. The Lagrange multiplier matrix that certifies first-order stationarity rescales the eigenfunctions into the free boundary minimal immersion. For $b=1$, the supremum is the Fraser--Schoen bound $4\pi$, attained by branched double covers of the disk; the embedded torus with connected boundary of Carlotto, Franz, and Schulz is a saddle point, which answers their question whether it maximizes the eigenvalue in the negative. For $b \geq 2$ the largest values correspond to free boundary minimal tori in \mathbb{B}^5 and \mathbb{B}^6; the surfaces of Folha, Pacard, and Zolotareva, two disks joined by a central neck and $b$ equatorial necks, are maximizers within their symmetry class but saddle points of the full problem, with values increasing toward $4\pi$ as $b \to \infty$.

papers.title: Asymptotic low slopes of toric exponential sums
papers.abstract: Let $\Delta$ be an integral Newton polytope containing the origin. We prove that the generic Newton slopes corresponding to Hodge slopes strictly smaller than one differ from their Hodge values by $O_\Delta(p^{-1})$. No hypothesis is imposed on the semigroup generated by the lattice points of $\Delta$. The proof combines an auxiliary prime and the Cartier operator to show that a coefficient of each required Dwork principal minor is nonzero. When the origin is interior to $\Delta$, duality gives the same estimate for the corresponding high slopes and, in dimension two, for all slopes.

papers.title: Orders in the Euclidean Court
papers.authors: Carlo Francisco Adajar, Kevin J. McGown, Paul Pollack, Enrique Trevi\~no
papers.abstract: Following Johnson, Queen, and Sevilla, we call an order $\mathcal{O}$ in a number field $K$ \textsf{generalized Euclidean} if for all $\alpha,\beta \in \mathcal{O}$ with $\beta\ne 0$ for which $\alpha\mathcal{O}+\beta\mathcal{O}$ is a principal ideal of $\mathcal{O}$, there are $\gamma, \rho \in \mathcal{O}$ with $\alpha =\beta \gamma + \rho$ and $|N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\rho)| < |N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\beta)|$. We prove that only finitely many quadratic orders are generalized Euclidean. Additionally, assuming GRH, we show that for each fixed $d > 1$ there are only finitely many integers $m$ for which $T^d-m$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{Z}[m^{1/d}] = \mathbb{Z}[T]/(T^d-m)$ is generalized Euclidean. When $d$ is even, we can remove the assumption of GRH.

papers.title: Finite BSC-Decomposition of Binary-Input Symmetric-Output Channels and Applications to Channel Simulation
papers.abstract: We propose a finite BSC-decomposition method for representing an arbitrary binary-input symmetric-output channel (BISOC) as a mixture of binary symmetric channels (BSCs) with at most $\ell+1$ distinct crossover probabilities. We show that the weighted average capacity of the component BSCs exceeds the capacity of the original BISOC by at most $(\pi^2\log e)/(48\ell^2)+O(\ell^{-5/2})$ bits, and the leading term is asymptotically optimal in the worst case. Based on the finite BSC-decomposition, we design a channel simulation scheme for arbitrary BISOCs. Combined with efficient channel simulation algorithms for BSCs, our scheme achieves a communication rate with $O((\log n / n)^{2/3})$ redundancy over the capacity for simulating $n$ copies of a BISOC.

papers.title: The Maximum Commute Time of Regular Graphs
papers.authors: Jing Huang, Xuezhu Liao, Jiaxin Tang
papers.abstract:
For a connected simple regular graph $G$, let $\tau(G)$ be the maximum commute time for simple random walk, and let $t_n$ be the maximum of $\tau(G)$ over all such graphs of order $n$. Aldous and Fill conjectured that $t_n\sim3n^2/2$. We determine $t_n$ exactly and classify all maximizers for every even $n\geq10$ and every odd $n\geq15$; both thresholds are best possible. The maximizers are cubic block chains joined by bridges at even orders and quartic block chains joined at cut vertices at odd orders. The exact formulas specify the linear corrections according to the order modulo four and five, respectively, and imply $
t_n\sim \begin{cases} \dfrac32 n^2, & n\text{ even},\\[1mm] n^2, & n\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \qquad n\to\infty. $
Thus the conjectured asymptotic formula holds along even orders but fails along odd orders. The proof combines unit-current potential orderings, cut-current inequalities, and sharp block resistance bounds, supplemented by finite computations in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Semi-similar Prandtl Flows near a Stagnation Point: Dynamical Selection and Nonlinear Stability
papers.authors: Chen Gao, Tao Tao, Zhouping Xin, Shing-Tung Yau, Chuankai Zhao
papers.abstract:
This paper studies time-dependent semi-similar Prandtl flows with outer flow $U(x)=x^m$, where $m\geq1$. The normal coordinate is scaled by the local boundary-layer thickness, and time by the associated diffusion scale. Every time-monotone solution in the Oleinik class extends globally in time. The Falkner--Skan boundary layer globally attracts every such unsteady semi-similar profile. The convergence rate is exponential for $m=1$ and algebraic for $m>1$. We also prove nonlinear stability of each admissible time-dependent semi-similar trajectory under small compatible perturbations that break the semi-similar ansatz. Together, these results provide a dynamical justification of the time-dependent semi-similar class within the full Prandtl theory.
  For semi-similar flows, the Crocco transformation reduces the problem to a one-dimensional degenerate parabolic equation. Combined with weighted barriers, comparison principles propagate time monotonicity and lead to global continuation. Zero-order convergence and a one-sided gradient estimate then produce uniform strict concavity after a transient period; this concavity supplies the damping needed for derivative decay. The same damping mechanism extends to the full ultraparabolic perturbation equation, allowing us to close the nonlinear stability estimates.

papers.title: 2-Local Derivations on Conformal Galilei Lie Algebras and Their Central Extensions
papers.abstract: We classify 2-local derivations on the finite-dimensional conformal Galilei Lie algebras in three natural settings: the algebra without central extension, the mass central extension, and the exotic central extension. No additivity or linearity is assumed in the definition of a 2-local derivation. We prove that in every case each 2-local derivation is an ordinary derivation. For the unextended algebra, the proof combines characteristic-quotient normalization with separating vectors, invariant bilinear forms, rank-two mixed zero anchors, and a semisimple-perturbation argument for the standard module. For the mass central extension with $2\ell\ge3$, the residual map is first reduced to the center and then eliminated by a symplectic-anchor construction on the Heisenberg radical; a dimension argument in the centralizer of a regular semisimple element simultaneously handles singular reductive actions and the additional central shear that occurs in spatial dimension two. The endpoint $\ell=\tfrac12$ is the Schr\"odinger algebra; a self-contained symplectic-anchor proof includes all spatial dimensions, with explicit treatment of dimensions one and two. For the exotic extension, after center normalization we use conjugate middle-weight positions and an affine middle anchor to eliminate every central translate, including the one-sided middle-weight configurations. Consequently the set of 2-local derivations coincides with the derivation algebra for all admissible parameters, and hence every 2-local derivation in these families is automatically linear.

papers.title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
papers.abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.

papers.title: Quantitative stratification and optimal regularity for stationary $J$-holomorphic maps
papers.authors: Chang-Yu Guo, Ming-Lun Liu, Chang-You Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give an alternate proof of the $\epsilon$-regularity theorem of Wang [Comm. Cont. Math. 2003] for weakly $J$-holomorphic maps by adapting the conservation law approach of Rivi\`ere [Invent. Math. 2007]. Then we adapt the powerful quantitative stratification method of Naber--Valtorta [Ann. Math. 2017] to obtain optimal volume estimates and rectifiability for the quantitative strata of stationary $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast with general harmonic maps, the almost complex equation gives rise to an additional symmetry improvement: Every odd-dimensional translation symmetry extends to an even-dimensional one. Consequently, consecutive even and odd strata coincide, and the $k$-th quantitative stratum satisfies a tubular-neighborhood estimate with exponent $2m-2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, where $2m$ is the real dimension of the domain. The corresponding strata are $2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$-rectifiable, with almost-everywhere unique complex planes of symmetry. Finally, we prove that every stationary $J$-holomorphic map is smooth if the target { manifold} admits no non-constant $J$-holomorphic sphere, improving the corresponding theorem of Wang.

papers.title: An intrinsic notion of visibility and classification of planar Denjoy-Wolff domains
papers.abstract:
In this article, we introduce an intrinsic notion of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance that does not require any boundary. We establish localization results for the Kobayashi distance on Kobayashi hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy this intrinsic visibility property. As an application of these localization results, we compare the Busemann horospheres of a domain with those of a subdomain.
  Recently, Benini and Bracci characterized simply connected planar domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property in terms of Busemann horospheres. More precisely, they proved that a proper simply connected planar domain has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of every Busemann horosphere meets the boundary of the domain in exactly one point. We introduce Condition (M$\star$), a condition of attaching a proper disk to the domain at a boundary point. Using our localization results together with this comparison of Busemann horospheres, we extend the characterization of Benini and Bracci to domains satisfying Condition (M$\star$) at every boundary point, and to domains satisfying it outside a totally disconnected subset of the boundary. In particular, we obtain a characterization for finitely connected domains and for a large class of infinitely connected domains having the Denjoy-Wolff property. These characterizations yield a variety of domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property, which we illustrate through example.

papers.title: The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality for chordal graphs
papers.authors: Shaohan Xu, Fengming Dong, Kexiang Xu
papers.abstract: For a connected graph $G$, let $\tau(G)$, $\alpha(G)$ and $\alpha^*(G)$ denote its numbers of spanning trees, acyclic orientations and totally cyclic orientations, respectively. We prove that $\alpha(G)\alpha^*(G)\geq\tau(G)^2$ for every connected bridgeless chordal graph.

papers.title: Global weak solutions for a two-species Riesz cross-attraction system with quadratic diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish global existence for a two-species cross-attraction system on $\mathbb R^3$, with quadratic diffusion and the common interaction operator $(-\Delta)^{-s}$, where $1/2<s<1$. Nonnegative initial data in $L^1\cap L^\infty$ with finite second moments require no smallness condition on the masses. A joint energy and second-moment estimate and a coupled $L^p$ iteration give uniform a priori estimates for the regularized solutions. Compactness then yields mass-conserving global weak solutions, bounded on every finite time interval and strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^2$. The energy inequality holds at every pair of time endpoints. Uniqueness and bounds uniform for all positive times are not asserted.

papers.title: Classification of all non-split central extensions of naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the naturally graded 2-filiform non-Lie Leibniz algebras over the field of complex numbers. There are two finite series of such algebras, defined in every dimension starting from five, and two further algebras which occur only in dimension five. For each of these algebras we classify, up to isomorphism, all of its non-split central extensions, of every possible dimension. The one-dimensional central extensions are already known from an earlier work, so the main part of the paper is devoted to the extensions of dimension two and higher. As usual, the classification is reduced to the description of the orbits of the automorphism group of the algebra on the subspaces of its second cohomology space with trivial coefficients. For each algebra and each dimension we give the complete list of these orbits together with the multiplication tables of the corresponding algebras, and we point out the extensions whose annihilator coincides with the added central ideal. Among the algebras obtained there are 2-filiform Leibniz algebras which are not naturally graded; this class of algebras has not been systematically studied so far.

papers.title: Optimal Priors for Betting Tests with Bounded Payoffs: An Exact Efficiency Characterization
papers.abstract: Testing by betting is a powerful framework that recasts hypothesis testing as a betting game. A popular approach uses an $F$-weighted portfolio with a predefined prior $F$. For suitable priors, this approach has recently been shown to achieve the optimal expected rejection time as the error probability goes to zero at a fixed alternative. Yet, the prior $F$ changes how the portfolio test behaves near the null. This motivates the question: Which prior should we use in testing-by-betting algorithms? We study bounded scalar payoffs and introduce an efficiency measure that allows the error probability and alternative to vary jointly. Under mild assumptions, we prove that efficiency equals a logarithmic decay index of the prior near zero. This gives a necessary and sufficient condition for optimality: Beta priors have infinite efficiency, whereas suitable Robbins-type priors attain efficiency 1. As an application, we consider testing a specified mean of a bounded random variable and describe an implementation of the portfolio algorithm with almost-linear computational complexity.

papers.title: Cohomological Milnor Fibrations of Landau--Ginzburg Models
papers.abstract: We study the global topology of \emph{fundamentally tame} Landau--Ginzburg (LG) models on complete K\"ahler manifolds. We first show that the superpotential $f$ is surjective onto $\mathbb{C}$, then prove that $f$ restricts to a locally trivial fibration over the set of its regular values, which yields a global generalization of the classical Milnor fibration and provides an Ehresmann-type fibration in the non-proper setting. Assuming that $f$ has finitely many critical points, we use a Morse-theoretic argument to show that the relative homology of $\bigl(M,f^{-1}(c)\bigr)$, for a regular value $c$, is concentrated in the middle degree and has rank equal to the global Milnor number $\mu_f$. We further identify the relative homotopy type of the fibers with that of the sublevel sets of $f$ at infinity.Finally, for deformations satisfying a uniform tameness condition on a Stein manifold, we construct the relative cohomology bundles at positive and negative infinity, each equipped with a natural flat Gauss--Manin connection.

papers.title: Piercing spanned lines and hyperplanes
papers.abstract: Motzkin, Gr\"unbaum, and Erd\H{o}s and Purdy asked how many noncollinear blue points can coexist with $t$ red points in the real plane if every blue-spanned line contains a red point. We prove that there are at most $2.35t-3$ blue points, even over the complex numbers. For the complex higher-dimensional problem of Campbell, Kroeker, and Lund, we prove $b_k(t)\le1.40k^2t$. Colorings of cyclic Dowling geometries give a matching lower bound in order of magnitude for all $k\ge2$ and $t\ge3$. The planar proof uses frame normalization and a second-moment estimate; the higher-dimensional proof combines the degree bound of Kroeker and Lund with principal truncation.

papers.title: A classification of the Nim-sequences for the two-element subtraction game with a single pass
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a complete description of the preperiods, periodic lengths, and the Grundy-value sequences of two-element subtraction games with a single pass option.

papers.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers
papers.abstract: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.

papers.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-expanders
papers.abstract: We describe the self-expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$. Apart from the Clifford minimal cone, every such hypersurface is complete, proper and noncompact, and belongs to one of three families: two one-parameter families of embedded hypersurfaces diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$ or to $\mathbb{R}^{q+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}$, whose profile curves leave an axis, and a two-parameter family diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$, parametrized by the point of the profile curve closest to the origin, which is the generic family: its set of initial conditions is open and of full measure in the phase space. Every end is asymptotically conical, with explicit decay rates, and every such hypersurface has Euclidean volume growth. A profile curve of the third family has at most one loop, and the point of the curve closest to the origin lies on that loop.

papers.title: A New Proof of Wei's Theorem
papers.authors: Zhiqaing Wei, Mengyan Xing, Xingya Zhao
papers.abstract: In the paper \emph{Structure and realizability for rational maps}, Wei proved the following. Let \(k\) nontrivial partitions of an integer \(d\ge 3\) be given, satisfying the Riemann--Hurwitz formula for the case of maps between two spheres. If \(k>\ell+1\), where \[ \ell=\min_i|\pi_i| \] is the shortest partition length, then there exists a rational map whose branch datum is given by these partitions. In this paper we give a new proof of Wei's theorem on realizing a tuple of partitions as the ramification data of a rational function. The proof is inductive on the shortest partition length. Two auxiliary results are established: a two-cut partition theorem and a gluing theorem for marked spherical coverings. These reduce any counterexample with shortest length \(\ell\ge3\) to auxiliary data with either fewer factors or smaller shortest length, while preserving the total defect and the marked conditions. The base case \(\ell\le2\) is quoted from the literature.

papers.title: Embedding into quotient
papers.abstract:
We study Bass's finiteness problem for embeddings into proper quotients. Given a commutative ring R, a reduced finitely generated R-algebra A, and an ideal $J\triangleleft A$, we ask whether an R-algebra monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow_R A/J$ forces J=0. We give affirmative answers by presenting two arguments. Also, we discuss not only in the reduced case, but also in several non-reduced cases: when R is artinian and A is finite over R; when R is zero-dimensional and A is finite projective over R; and in a series of Cohen--Macaulay settings. In the module-theoretic direction, for a noetherian reduced ring, and a finitely generated, and torsion-free A-module M, we show that $M\hookrightarrow_R M/JM$ implies that J is contained in a minimal prime of A; if M is faithful, then J=0. Also, dual versions investigated.
  Examples illustrate the necessity of hypotheses.

papers.title: Left tail asymptotics for the density of supercritical branching processes in random environment
papers.abstract: Let $(Z_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a supercritical branching process in a random environment in which every individual produces at least one offspring, and let $W$ be the almost sure limit of the normalized $Z_n$. Write $p_1$ for the (random) probability that an individual has exactly one child and $m_0$ for the mean offspring number in a given environment. Assume that $p_1$ is positive almost surely and bounded away from $1$, that $m_0$ is bounded away from $1$ and from infinity together with a mild moment condition, and that $\log m_0$ is non-lattice. Let $a_0>0$ be the unique solution of the equation $\mathbb{E}[p_1 m_0^{a_0}]=1$. Under these assumptions, we determine the precise left tail asymptotics of the annealed law of $W$: the distribution function $F(x)=\mathbb{P}(W\leq x)$ satisfies $F(x)\sim D x^{a_0}$ as $x\downarrow 0$ with a constant $D\in(0,\infty)$ admitting an explicit representation, and the annealed density $w$ of $W$, which we show exists and can be chosen continuous on $(0,\infty)$, satisfies $w(x)\sim G x^{a_0-1}$ as $x\downarrow 0$ with $G=a_0 D>0$. These results extend the classical power-law left tail behavior of the martingale limit of a Galton--Watson process in the literature to the random environment setting, where the exponent $a_0$ is determined by the averaged environmental law rather than by a fixed offspring distribution.

papers.title: Weak Limits of Parameter Estimation in Strongly Identifiable Mixture Models
papers.authors: Dung Le, Trang Pham, Alessandro Rinaldo, Nhat Ho
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of global maximum likelihood estimation in finite mixtures with an unknown number of components bounded by \(k\). Although convergence rates are well understood under strong identifiability, they do not determine the limiting distribution of mixing-measure loss. Under second-order strong identifiability, we establish two geometric results that connect density asymptotics to uncertainty about the mixing measure. First, we characterize the exact attainable density tangent set, accounting for the component budget shared by nonlocal vanishing components and local splitting directions. Second, we derive a sequential first-order expansion of squared Wasserstein loss, showing that its leading transportation cost is uniquely determined by the relative-density direction. Together with a Gaussian likelihood argmax theorem, these results yield joint weak convergence of the relative-density maximum likelihood estimator and \(\sqrt n W_2^2(\widehat G_n,G_*)\). The density limit maximizes a Gaussian likelihood process over the attainable tangent set, and the induced limit of \(n^{1/4}W_2(\widehat G_n,G_*)\) is generally non-Gaussian. We establish consistency of an \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) parametric bootstrap when \(m\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to0\). Numerical studies assess the approximation and distinguish bootstrap and optimization errors; a flow-cytometry application illustrates uncertainty summaries invariant to component labeling under a working mixture model.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
