papers.abstract: The birational Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem (KVV for short) is known to hold in considerable generality in equal characteristic zero, but fails in general in positive characteristic. We study a vanishing conjecture of Lipman for sequences of blow-ups at closed points of the spectrum of a regular local ring. We prove the conjecture when the ring has dimension at most three. We also establish a relative Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem for exceptional nef Q-divisors when all blow-up centers are rational over the residue field and the positive residue characteristic is at least the dimension of the ring minus one. Both results allow mixed characteristic.

papers.title: Invariance of logarithmic plurigenera and adjoint volumes in K\"ahler families
papers.abstract: We consider smooth proper families of compact complex manifolds over a disk whose total space is K\"ahler, together with a boundary divisor with relative simple normal crossings. We prove that, if the boundary is a rational divisor with coefficients in $[0,1)$, every logarithmic pluricanonical form on a fiber extends to a neighborhood of that fiber, and hence that the logarithmic plurigenera are constant. No positivity of the log canonical class is assumed. We prove further that, for real boundary coefficients in $[0,1]$, a log-adjoint class twisted by a smooth semipositive form has the same volume on every fiber, and that it is pseudoeffective either on every fiber or on none. When the log-adjoint class is nef on every fiber, we give a second proof of the extension theorem, which does not use the minimal model program.

papers.title: Distributional Lifting for Discrete Optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce a framework that transforms discrete optimization into continuous optimization over parameterized probability distributions. The framework reveals a common distributional structure behind several methods that have largely developed independently, including continuous reformulations for multilinear binary optimization, Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning, the cross-entropy method, mean-field variational optimization, and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm. It enables flexible and modular algorithm design, for example, by using neural networks to incorporate contextual information or by enforcing convexity of the lifted problem. We establish two theoretical results: a link between the lifted optimality gap and sampling quality in the original discrete problem, and a convergence guarantee for the lifted optimization problem under suitable conditions. These results lead to a unified algorithmic template based on batched sampling and stochastic gradient updates that is naturally compatible with GPU computation. We demonstrate the framework through three case studies spanning multidimensional knapsack, covering-constrained three-dimensional assignment, and a stochastic mixed-integer location-allocation problem, showing that it can accommodate distinct combinatorial structures and scale to large discrete and mixed-integer settings.

papers.title: Geometric parameter sequences for $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graphs
papers.authors: Jae-Ho Lee, Jongyook Park, Ian Seong
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a distance-regular graph with diameter $D \geq 3$, and let $\theta$ be a nonzero eigenvalue of $\Gamma$ distinct from its valency. Motivated by the geometric parameter sequences of geometric distance-regular graphs, we introduce analogous sequences defined recursively from the intersection numbers of $\Gamma$ and $\theta$, without assuming a geometric structure. We show that the recursion is well defined if and only if all terms of the standard sequence corresponding to $\theta$ are nonzero and consecutive terms are distinct. In particular, the geometric parameter sequences associated with the smallest eigenvalue always exist. Suppose that $\Gamma$ is $Q$-polynomial with respect to an eigenvalue ordering $\theta_0,\theta_1, \ldots,\theta_D$. Let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i=1}^{D}$ and $\{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^{D}$ be the first and second split sequences of the primary Leonard system, respectively, and let $\beta$ denote its fundamental parameter. We prove that the geometric parameter sequences associated with $\theta_D$ exist if and only if $\varphi_i\neq\phi_i$ for every $1\leq i\leq D$, and if and only if $\beta\neq-2$ or $D$ is even. When the sequences exist, we obtain closed formulas in terms of the primary parameter array. We introduce the split ratio sequence $\rho_i=\varphi_i/\phi_i$. Using this sequence, we obtain a bidiagonal factorization of $B-\theta_D I$, where $B$ is the intersection matrix of $\Gamma$. This factorization remains valid even when the geometric parameter sequences associated with $\theta_D$ do not exist. If $\Gamma$ is geometric and $\theta_D$ is its smallest eigenvalue, then the geometric parameter sequences associated with $\theta_D$ coincide with those of $\Gamma$.

papers.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
papers.abstract: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.

papers.title: On Exact Dihedral Angle Sum Ranges for Orthocentric and Isogonic Tetrahedra
papers.abstract: For a nondegenerate Euclidean tetrahedron T, let {\Sigma}(T) denote the sum of its six interior dihedral angles. We establish the exact range [6 arccos(1/3), 3{\pi}) for the orthocentric and isogonic classes. The orthocentric part gives a short alternative proof of the sharp lower bound; the main new result is the corresponding isogonic theorem. Starting from classical insphere-contact geometry, we derive a reciprocal half-angle identity and a sharp defect inequality controlled by the scale-invariant dispersion of the reciprocal tangent-length parameters. This quantitative refinement shows that any nonzero dispersion forces a positive dihedral-angle-sum gap, and that near equality forces the normalized reciprocal parameters to be close to equality. Finally, the common kite subfamily realizes every value in the interval and proves sharpness of both endpoints.

papers.title: Saturation degree of powers of graded ideals
papers.authors: Le Tuan Hoa, Hop Dang Nguyen, Ngo Viet Trung
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a non-nilpotent graded ideal of a standard graded algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring. We show that the saturation degree sdeg $I^n$ is asymptotically a constant function or a linear function whose slope is one of the generating degrees of $I$. Furthermore, we give sufficient (and necessary) conditions for a numerical functions to be the function sdeg $I^n$ of an ideal $I$ generated by forms of the same degree. Our results may provide a better understanding of the initial behavior of the regularity function reg $I^n$.

papers.title: The Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary
papers.abstract: We establish local existence for the nonlinear Israel--Stewart equations describing a relativistic viscous fluid with a physical vacuum free boundary. Compared with ideal fluids with a physical vacuum, the relaxation equation for the bulk viscosity introduces further derivative loss. The problem is compounded by the degenerate nature of the equations of motion on the free boundary. In this work, we construct solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces via a Nash--Moser iteration. Since the domain moves, the iteration is carried out in Lagrangian coordinates, while the linearized operator at each iterate is inverted on the Eulerian domain with the local well-posedness of the linearized equations established in our earlier work.

papers.title: The irrationality exponent of the lemniscate period: A determinant proof with a Lean 4 formalization
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega=2\int_0^1(1-t^4)^{-1/2}dt$. We prove that, for every real $\nu>2$, there is $Q\geq2$ such that $q^{-\nu}<|\Omega-p/q|$ for every integer $p$ and every integer $q\geq Q$. Consequently $\Omega$ is irrational and its irrationality exponent is two. The proof combines elliptic separated-weight interpolation, arithmetic denominator estimates, and an analytic determinant bound on a square complex-multiplication grid. The determinant comparison uses the same selected source columns on both sides. We give the integral-to-lattice normalization, the exact local-coordinate and common-multiplier transport, and the parameter order that makes the two bounds incompatible. The accompanying Lean 4 development proves the endpoint without additional hypotheses. Numbered formal references link the mathematical argument to exact declarations in the complete source distribution; an appendix gives the pinned build environment and the dependency audit.

papers.title: Lightning Algorithm for Inhomogeneous Modified Helmholtz Equations on Cornered Domains and Their Applications
papers.abstract: We develop in this paper an efficient solver for the inhomogeneous modified Helmholtz equations in two-dimensional complex domains with particular attention to resolving corner singularities. We represent the solution as a summation of a particular solution and the solution of the modified Helmholtz equation. Built upon suitable domain embedding methods, we compute the particular solution using the Fourier spectral method and/or Legendre--Fourier spectral method. To treat the corner singularities, we develop a lightning algorithm by employing an expansion of the modified Bessel functions of the second kind, coupled with tapered exponentially clustering poles, to approximate the corner singularities, and using an expansion of the modified Bessel functions of the first kind to approximate the smooth part of the solution. Finally, we determine the unknown expansion coefficients by solving a least-squares problem to satisfy the boundary conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that root-exponential convergence can be achieved for the modified Helmholtz equation with corner singularities. To further demonstrate the applicability of the proposed algorithm, it has been successfully applied to solve some typical linear and nonlinear parabolic equations. We have also made a first attempt in extending the lightning algorithm to a three-dimensional modified Helmholtz equation.

papers.title: On multilinear forms for mod $p$ representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
papers.authors: Hao Liu, Haoran Wang, Yuting Yang
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, for any prime $p$, and let $L/F$ be a ramified quadratic extension. We compute the spaces of $\mathcal O_L^\times$-equivariant linear forms on the representation $\operatorname{ind}^G_{KZ}\sigma/(\Phi-\lambda)$. The only nonzero cases arise from one-dimensional quotients. Consequently, the restriction of an infinite-dimensional irreducible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ with a central character to $\mathcal O_L^\times$ has no character quotient. We apply this vanishing result to show that a finite tensor product of smooth mod $p$ representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2(F)$ admits no nonzero invariant linear form whenever at least one factor is infinite-dimensional and irreducible with a central character.

papers.title: The binomial distribution maximises entropy among sums of negatively related indicators with fixed mean and support
papers.abstract: We show that the binomial distribution supported on $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ and with mean $np$ for some $0<p<1$ maximises entropy within the class of sums of negatively related indicator random variables with this mean and support. Our results generalise the main result of Yu (2008), who showed that this binomial distribution maximises entropy within the smaller class of ultra-log-concave random variables of order $n$. Our proof makes use of a Markov chain construction of Yu (2008), together with a stochastic ordering argument.

papers.title: On the Nonoccurrence of Gradient Restart in Nesterov Accelerated Gradient Method
papers.authors: Chenglong Bao, Liang Chen, Jiahong Li, Defeng Sun
papers.abstract: Gradient restarting often improves the practical performance of accelerated gradient methods for unconstrained convex optimization problems, but a general theoretical guarantee of such improvement remains unclear. In this paper, we construct smooth, strongly convex objectives with Lipschitz-continuous gradients and corresponding initial points for which gradient restart never occurs, both for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and for its ordinary differential equation model. From these examples, we conclude that strong convexity and smoothness alone do not guarantee that gradient restart improves the convergence behavior of the accelerated method or its continuous-time model. In particular, for the continuous-time example, the objective gap is asymptotic to $1/(\pi t^3)$. We therefore obtain a negative answer to the open problem raised by Su, Boyd, and Cand{\`e}s [\textit{J. Mach. Learn. Res.}, 2016, 17(153), 1--43] of whether gradient restart guarantees linear convergence of the continuous dynamics for smooth strongly convex objectives.

papers.title: Global strong solutions to the aligned 2.5D non-resistive full MHD system with high temperature and a strong magnetic field
papers.authors: Yachun Li, Zixuan Qu, Zhaoyang Shang
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for an aligned vertical-field reduction of the full compressible non-resistive MHD equations in two space variables. The shear and bulk viscosities are proportional to $\theta^\alpha$, and the heat conductivity is proportional to $\theta^\beta$. For $2<\alpha<\beta<\alpha+2$, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the background temperature and the comparable magnetic background are sufficiently large, while the positive density background is fixed. The velocity and temperature perturbations belong initially to $H^2$, and the transported magnetic perturbation belongs to $H^1\cap D^{1,4}$; their absolute norms may be bounded by an arbitrary fixed constant. Alignment is essential and implies a small density perturbation relative to the magnetic background. Our proof combines relative energy estimates, uniform in the background temperature and magnetic field, with coupled estimates for the material derivatives of the velocity and temperature. These bounds control the source terms in the damped magnetic-gradient equation, allowing us to close the global a priori estimates without a separate large-time decay assumption. We construct the global strong solution by smooth approximation and Sobolev energy estimates for the approximating solutions, and prove uniqueness by an energy estimate for the difference of two solutions.

papers.title: On sharp stability of the BCC quantizer
papers.abstract: We prove sharp nonlinear stability estimates for the squared-distance quantization energy of the body-centered cubic lattice. The reference Hessian has optimal coercivity constant \(1/96\) relative to nearest-neighbor displacement differences, uniformly over all finite-index periods. We classify all equality modes and prove cubic cancellation on their span. This yields nonlinear stability in a neighborhood independent of the period, including volume-preserving strain. The loss in the sharp energy coefficient is at most quadratic for each fixed period and exactly linear when all periods are allowed. We also determine the transition between these regimes. Finally, we prove global optimality and uniqueness of BCC, up to rigid motions, among two-site configurations with rectangular period cells of fixed volume.

papers.title: Beyond Finite-Sum Optimization: A Primal-Dual Method for Decentralized Finite-Max Optimization
papers.authors: Zhouxing Luo, Lei Wang, Xin Liu
papers.abstract: Many decentralized systems are judged by their worst-performing agents rather than their average performance. We study finite-max optimization over a connected undirected network, where each agent knows only its own smooth, possibly nonconvex objective. Quadratic regularization yields a smooth finite-sum representation with a scalar dual variable and locally computable clipped weights. We develop an alternating primal-dual gradient tracking (APDGT) method, using neighbor communication without any global or centralized projections. Under smoothness and level-boundedness assumptions, a localized Lyapunov analysis with vanishing regularization establishes bounded primal iterates and Clarke stationarity of every accumulation point of their network average. The averaged sequence contains an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, measured by near-active gradients, within $O (\varepsilon^{-3})$ iterations. Synthetic tests and decentralized logistic regression on Fashion-MNIST illustrate convergence behavior and potential improvements in worst-agent performance.

papers.title: Commutative Counterexamples to Arveson's Hyperrigidity Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative $C^*$-algebras. In each example, every irreducible representation of the $C^*$-envelope is a boundary representation, but hyperrigidity fails. The first example is the operator system of continuous affine functions on an infinite-dimensional weighted $\ell^p$ ball. In the second infinite-dimensional example, we start with commuting operators and construct a nontrivial dilation. The final example comes from a compact truncated epigraph of a strictly convex function and yields a finite-dimensional operator system.

papers.title: Vorticity growth beyond bounded relative vorticity for axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl
papers.abstract: We establish upper bounds for vorticity and related quantities in axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl in $\mathbb{R}^3$, assuming that the initial relative vorticity $\omega_0/r$ belongs to $L^1\cap L^p$ with $3<p\le \infty$. For each fixed $p \in (3,\infty]$, we obtain polynomial-in-time upper bounds for the radial moments, the radial velocity, and the $L^p$ norm of vorticity. We then consider initial data with unbounded relative vorticity whose growth near the axis is controlled by $\Phi (\log \tfrac{1}{r})$ for a subexponential profile $\Phi$, so that $\omega_0/r$ belongs to $L^p$ for every $p<\infty$ but not to $L^{\infty}$. For such data, we derive profile dependent upper bounds for the vorticity maximum. In particular, for any polynomial function $\Phi (s)=s^k$ with $k\ge 0$, we show that $\|\omega (\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is bounded by $(1+t)^{\frac{4}{3}+k} (\log (2+t) )^{\frac{2k}{3}}$. Moreover, for initial data satisfying $\omega_0/r \in L^1\cap L^p$ with a fixed $p\in (3,\infty)$, under additional symmetry and vertical confinement assumptions, we obtain a subexponential-in-time upper bound for the vorticity maximum, thereby improving the classical exponential bound for such data.

papers.title: Simultaneous Matrix Multiplication by Tensor Contraction Aggregation
papers.abstract: We present an interpretation of the fast matrix multiplication algorithms of Coppersmith and Winograd as aggregations of tensor contractions. This point of view provides a direct connection to older constructions by Pan and to more recent work on bilinear algorithms for symmetric tensor contraction. Further, we provide a new simple approach for exact aggregation of tensor contractions, each one yielding an independent matrix-matrix product. These constructions and border rank adaptations thereof do not come close to improving the best known bounds on $\omega$ (the matrix multiplication exponent), but provide explicit moderate-size fast matrix multiplication algorithms that achieve a better exponent than Strassen's algorithm and have potential practical value. These results imply improvements to the best known bounds on the rank and border rank of a fixed number of independent square matrix products. In particular, using $\langle m,m,m\rangle$ to denote the matrix multiplication tensor for matrices of dimension $m$, we obtain constructions that give bounds such as the border rank bound \[ \underline R\!\left(\langle n^2,n^2,n^2\rangle^{\oplus9}\right) \le (n+1)^6+6(n+1)^5, \] and the exact rank bound \[ R\!\left(\langle n^3,n^3,n^3\rangle^{\oplus14}\right)\le (n+1)^9. \] We quantify the accuracy of such constructions in finite precision, and provide border-rank constructions that reduce cost with limiting retained fractions of accuracy at least $1/2$, $1/3$, or $1/4$ relative to the classical matrix-multiplication approach under the stated error model.

papers.title: Powers and Functional Calculus for $m$-Selfadjoint and Skew $m$-Selfadjoint Operators
papers.authors: M. Faghih-Ahmadi, T. Berm\'udez, K. Hedayatian, H. Zaway
papers.abstract: We study powers and functional calculi of higher-order selfadjoint and skew higher-order selfadjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces. First, we compare the behavior of their powers with the corresponding theory for $m$-isometries. We prove that if $T$ is invertible and two powers $T^r$ and $T^s$ are, respectively, $m$- and $\ell$-selfadjoint, then $T^{\gcd(r,s)}$ is $\min\{m,\ell\}$-selfadjoint. In particular, invertibility yields the expected converse for consecutive powers. We also show that two consecutive skew $m$-selfadjoint powers must be non-invertible; in fact, nilpotent. For polynomials, we obtain coefficient characterizations under a cardinality assumption on the spectrum. Finally, for holomorphic functions we give spectral characterizations according to whether the spectrum is finite, or the domain of analyticity is a region, and we derive consequences for M\"obius transformations and $m$-isometries. Several examples illustrate why the spectral hypotheses cannot be omitted.

papers.title: General Periodic Conservation Laws Motivated by Traffic Modeling
papers.authors: Rinaldo M. Colombo, Mauro Garavello, Claudia Nocita
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the well-posedness, in the spatially periodic setting, of a mixed system of nonlocal-local conservation laws modeling traffic flow where autonomous vehicles --- informed on traffic conditions over long distances --- interact with human-driven bulk traffic. We also provide a comprehensive well-posedness theory in the periodic framework separately for general local conservation laws and for systems of nonlocal conservation laws, together with a priori total variation bounds and stability estimates.

papers.title: Surfaces Associated to Zeros of Automorphic $L$-functions
papers.authors: Debmalya Basak, Cruz Castillo, Alexandru Zaharescu
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, Montgomery established results concerning pair correlation of zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Rudnick and Sarnak extended these results to automorphic $L$-functions and all level correlations. We discover additional geometric structures associated to the zeros of automorphic $L$-functions. In the case of pair correlation, these structures form certain surfaces which display Gaussian behavior. For triple correlation, these structures exhibit Laplace and Chi-squared distributions, revealing an unexpected phase transition.

papers.title: Asymptotic Enumeration of $F$-decompositions in Typical Hypergraphs and of Universal Cycles
papers.authors: Danni Li, Bin Wang, Junxue Zhang
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we determine the asymptotic number of $F$-decompositions in typical hypergraphs. More precisely, let $F$ be a non-trivial $f$-vertex $k$-graph. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $F$-divisible $(n^{-\zeta},h,p)$-typical $k$-graph $G$ has $n^{\frac{f-k+o_n(1)}{|F|}|G|}$ $F$-decompositions.
  As an application, we asymptotically enumerate universal cycles for $k$-subsets of $[n]$, or equivalently, tight Euler tours of the complete $k$-graph $K_n^k$. For every $k\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying $k\mid {n-1 \choose k-1}$, the number of such universal cycles is $n^{(1-\gamma(n)){{n \choose k}}}$, where $0<\gamma(n)=o_n(1)$. More generally, for $\ell\in[k-1]$, we show that a sufficiently typical $n$-vertex $k$-graph $G$ satisfying the corresponding divisibility condition has $n^{(k-\ell-\gamma'(n))|G|}$ Euler $\ell$-tours, where $0<\gamma'(n)=o_n(1)$.

papers.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
papers.abstract:
A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work:
  1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions.
  2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes.
  3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes.
  The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

papers.title: Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications
papers.abstract: Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older bound for the map sending a H\"older potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.

papers.title: Reduction of structure groups for noncommutative principal bundles
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact group and let $H \subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup. We study reduction of the structure group for noncommutative principal bundles, modelled by free C${}^*$-dynamical systems in the sense of Ellwood. We first describe how induction from $H$ to $G$ behaves on associated correspondences and their tensor structure. Using reconstruction, this leads to a Tannakian characterization of reduction of the structure group in terms of the associated tensor functor. For normal subgroups, we characterize reduction in terms of central equivariant homomorphisms and derive module- and $K$-theoretic obstructions. We conclude with a noncommutative $O(n)$-example which admits no reduction to $SO(n)$.

papers.title: Uniform lower bounds for the average length of finite Pierce expansions
papers.abstract: For integers $1\leq a\leq b$, the length of the finite Pierce expansion of $a/b$ is the number of steps of the iteration $r\mapsto b\bmod r$ which starts at $a$ and ends at zero. Erd\H{o}s and Shallit (1991) proved that the average of these lengths over $1\leq a\leq b$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log b$, and suggested that it is at least of order $\log b$. In this paper, we prove that the average length is at least $\sqrt{2\log b}-3(\log b)^{1/4}-11$ for every $b\geq2$. We also show that, for each $0<c<\sqrt2$, the proportion of numerators $a$ for which the length is less than $c\sqrt{\log b}$ tends to zero exponentially fast in $\sqrt{\log b}$, with an explicit rate. Our approach refines the interval-counting argument of Erd\H{o}s and Shallit by restricting the product of the initial digits. As applications, we obtain similar bounds for reduced fractions and for numerators in a fixed congruence class.

papers.title: Rational Dyck Excursion Counts as Sums of Generalized Fuss-Catalan Products
papers.authors: Brecht Verbeken, Arne Vanhoyweghen, Vincent Ginis
papers.abstract: For walks with jumps +p and -q, where p,q are coprime positive integers, we express the weak and strict rational Dyck excursion counts as finite weighted sums of generalized Fuss-Catalan products. Both sums run over the same partitions of q for every path size. Reversing the order of the steps and changing their signs transforms a returning walk with jumps +p and -q into one with jumps +q and -p, with the same heights in reverse order. This preserves both weak and strict excursions. Applying the formulas with p and q exchanged therefore gives sums over partitions of p, so we can choose the smaller of the two jump magnitudes. The indices of the Fuss-Catalan factors satisfy certain divisibility conditions that are determined by the jump magnitudes and the partition parts. The weak formula alternates in sign with the number of parts, whereas every term in the strict formula is positive. We prove both formulas by cutting unrestricted walks at their first and last visits to their lowest height. Expanding the resulting factors produces the partitions of q and the different signs. We also give equivalent binomial convolutions. Multiplying each Fuss-Catalan factor by q in the weak formula or p in the strict formula gives a positive integer. For q=1, the weak and strict counts reduce to Fuss-Catalan and shifted Raney numbers, respectively; for q=2 and q=3, the formulas yield explicit convolution identities.

papers.title: Pointwise Wave--Damping for Linearized Vlasov--Poisson: Compactly Supported Radial Equilibria and Relativistic Applications
papers.authors: Haina Li, Quoc-Hung Nguyen, Zhilong Xue
papers.abstract: We establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response Green function and the complete electric field of the linearized Vlasov--Poisson system in $\mathbb{R}_x^3\times\mathbb{R}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. Both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $L_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying Landau-damped component. The wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. The equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. The proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. The electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. An exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.

papers.title: A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4\pi$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.

papers.title: A robust finite element method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics using Whitney forms
papers.abstract: A stabilized semi-discrete finite element scheme for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system is presented. The scheme uses the Whitney $2$-form and $1$-form for the fluid velocity and magnetic induction, respectively. The key ingredient is a magnetic curl-jump penalty term, which allows us to prove a pre-asymptotic error estimate of order $O(h^{1/2})$ with a constant depending on solution norms but not explicitly on the fluid viscosity and magnetic diffusivity.

papers.title: On a problem of Ma and Chen concerning minimal additive complements
papers.abstract: Let $m\geq1$ be an integer and let $W=(m\mathbb N_0+X)\cup U\cup V\subseteq\mathbb Z$ be bounded below, where $X\ne\varnothing$, $[U]_m\subseteq[X]_m$, $[X]_m\cap[V]_m=\varnothing$, and $V$ contains no infinite arithmetic progression with common difference $m$. Here $[S]_m$ denotes the set of residue classes modulo $m$ represented by $S$. Suppose that $W$ satisfies the $\mathcal C$-condition modulo $m$. For $0\leq r<m$, let $V_r=V\cap(r+m\mathbb Z)$, and put $V'=\bigcup_{|V_r|=\infty}V_r$, where the union is over $0\leq r<m$. We prove that $W$ has a minimal additive complement if $V'$ satisfies the big-hole property modulo $m$. This answers a problem posed by Ma and Chen.

papers.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
papers.abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=w\lambda$ for real or octonion $\lambda$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(w\lambda_1)\lambda_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $\lambda_2\lambda_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.

papers.title: Bootstrap percolation on the hypercube
papers.abstract: In this paper we obtain the critical probability $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ for bootstrap percolation with the infection threshold $r=f(n)n^a$ on the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_{n}$, where $0<a<1$ and $f(n)=n^{o(1)}$. More precisely, we obtain the exact first-order and second-order terms of $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ by extending the main theorem of Balogh, Bollob{\'a}s, and Morris (2009).

papers.title: On the denominators of signed harmonic sums
papers.abstract: Let $\eps=(\eps_i)_{i\ge1}$ be a sequence with $\eps_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $v_n(\eps)$ be the positive denominator of $\sum_{i=1}^n\eps_i/i$ in lowest terms. We prove that $|\{1\le n\le x:v_n(\eps)\ne v_{n+1}(\eps)\}|=o(x)$ uniformly in $\eps$. In particular, the set of positive integers $n$ with $v_n(\eps)=v_{n+1}(\eps)$ has asymptotic density one for every sequence of signs. This answers a problem of Wu and Chen, \emph{J. Number Theory} \textbf{200} (2019), 397--406.

papers.title: Rigidity of algebraic sets with small distortion
papers.abstract: We prove that for positive integers $k$, $n$, and $d>1$, there is a maximal $c(k,n,d)>1$ such that if $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a connected $k$-dimensional complex algebraic set with degree at most $d$ and $dist(X) < c(k,n,d)$, then $X$ must be a complex affine linear subspace, where $dist(X)$ denotes the distortion of $X$ and is given by the supremum of the ratios $d_{inner}(p, q)/d_{outer}(p, q)$ for all $p,q\in X$ with $p\not= q$. We also prove that $c(1,n,d)=\sqrt{2}$ for any positive integers $k$ and $n$. This result provides a sharp rigidity phenomenon for curves in the $c$-LNE category, showing that near-isometric behavior of the inner and outer metrics forces the curve to be as simple as possible.

papers.title: Average lower bound on magnetic double-well tunneling with asymptotically large well separation
papers.authors: Charles L. Fefferman, Say-Yeon Kwon, Jacob Shapiro, Michael I. Weinstein
papers.abstract: We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by $2d_1$ and the magnetic field strength is $b\lambda$, the lower bounds have the form $e^{-b\lambda d_1^2-Cd_1^{1+\delta}}$ for every fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$. No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.

papers.title: Deviation probabilities for global events in two dimensions (I): independent excursions
papers.abstract: We consider the field of local times generated by independent excursions of the two-dimensional simple random walk between the boundaries of two concentric disks, and study global events: informally, these are the events that have to occur everywhere (i.e., if such an event occurs on a set, then it also occurs on all its subsets). Examples include ``the set is completely covered'', ``the maximal local time on the set does not exceed a given level'', or ``the set does not contain a covered disk of a given radius''. For monotone global events, we show that the deviation probabilities (i.e., the probabilities that the event occurs with atypically few excursions, or does not occur with atypically many of them, or vice versa) can be obtained from the typical behaviour on different scales only, via a general decoupling argument based on soft local times.

papers.title: An Extension of Galvin's Theorem Related to the Banach-Mazur Game
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a topological space. Galvin's theorem on the Banach-Mazur game states that if $X$ has a $\pi$-base $\mathcal{B}$ satisfying the following condition:
  \textit{For any $U \in \mathcal{B}$, there exists a disjoint family $\mathcal{A}_U$ of nonempty open subsets of $U$ such that} \[ |\mathcal{A}_U| \geq |\{ B \in \mathcal{B} : U \subseteq B \}|, \]
  then, in the Banach-Mazur game on $X$, the second player, denoted NONEMPTY, has a 2-tactic if NONEMPTY has a winning strategy in this game. In this paper, we extend the disjointness condition of this family by replacing it with the condition of being open finite family. With this extension of the family $\mathcal{A}_U$, we showed that, the theorem is also true.

papers.title: A study of the $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances with a special emphasis on $C_{ab}$ curves
papers.authors: Eduardo Camps-Moreno, Olav Geil, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e
papers.abstract: In the seminal paper [13], Farr\'an and Munuera introduced a method to establish generic information on the $m$th Feng-Rao distance via a function on arbitrary numerical semigroups that serves as a lower bound on the generalized Hamming weights of dual one-point algebraic geometry codes whenever the semigroup is Weierstrass. In the present paper, we study what we shall call the primary and dual, respectively, $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances, which serve as lower bounds on relative generalized Hamming weights of nested primary and dual, respectively, one-point codes under similar condition. A unified method for establishing generic formulas for $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances of general numerical semigroups is developed and for a large variety of numerical semigroups generated by two elements, closed formula expressions are established complementing Delgado et al.s work [8] on the $m$th Feng-Rao distances of such semigroups. Finally, for non-singular $C_{ab}$ curves, we develop a method to estimate the $m$th relative generalized Hamming weight of dual and primary one-point codes in those regions where the generic methods may fail to provide best possible results.

papers.title: Direct Sample-Average Learning for Queueing Control: Gradient-Free Top-$K$ Coarse-to-Fine Optimization
papers.authors: Mehrdad Nozohour Yazdi, Yiqiang Q. Zhao
papers.abstract: We study steady-state queueing control when decisions must be learned from a single persistent operating trajectory: only the implemented action produces data, and the queue is not reset when the action changes. Fixed-event-count cycles yield a direct ratio-of-totals sample-average approximation (SAA) of each action's steady-state cost rate. A Top-K coarse-to-fine search ranks these estimates, retains several promising refinement paths, and concentrates later operation on finer candidate sets, without requiring gradients, convexity, or differentiability. We decompose direct-SAA error into accumulated conditional transient bias and martingale fluctuation. For regenerative queues, a bias-function representation reduces transient effects within contiguous action blocks to boundary terms. Finite-sample stagewise bounds then link estimation accuracy to master-grid identification through guardian retention, and the required queueing and sampling conditions are verified for a persistent-workload M/M/1 implementation. At a common active set, Top-K has a weakly larger guardian margin than Top-1, and an exact-objective example shows Top-1 can discard the optimal refinement branch. Numerical experiments delineate scope rather than universal dominance: Top-K improves terminal identification in the reported LiQUAR and mixed staffing comparisons, while LiQUAR can have lower cumulative learning cost, and GOLiQ is markedly stronger on a smooth benchmark with reliable queueing sensitivities. Direct ranking is therefore best viewed as a complementary method when model-specific gradients are unavailable, inconvenient, or poorly matched to the decision space.

papers.title: Weighted potential and Green systems with Dini coefficients and primitive growth
papers.authors: Hongtao Hu, Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou
papers.abstract: We prove a nonexistence theorem for positive potential systems with continuous coefficients satisfying distributional Euler lower bounds and a uniform Dini modulus on normalized logarithmic dilations. The nonlinearities have positive lower logarithmic derivatives and positive primitive-to-endpoint ratios. The common radial kernel is comparable with a Riesz kernel. A localized transport identity, a primitive pressure estimate and implicit amplitude normalization give uniform local energy bounds and a dilation contradiction. And we treats the genuine Green kernel of $-\Delta+V$ for nonnegative potentials under annular and Newton composition budgets and a strict gap corrected by the relative Green dilation defect. Relative endpoint differences and an exact virtual-energy cancellation retain local nonlinear energy as the only initial energy hypothesis. Independent representation arguments give these consequences, including even integer orders without initial tails. A compact family of normalized responses also yields universal interior bounds without regular variation.

papers.title: Critical Growth for Stochastic Adaptive Stabilization with an Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: This paper studies adaptive stabilization of a class of scalar discrete-time nonlinear systems with unknown drift coefficients and an unknown nonzero input gain. Under iid Gaussian noise, we establish a necessary and sufficient polynomial criterion for global stabilizability, characterizing the admissible combinations of growth exponents. When the criterion holds, we construct a feedback combining finite calibration with adaptive control. The time average of the squared output converges almost surely to the noise variance, attaining the smallest possible value. If the criterion fails, then for every Borel causal feedback there exist fixed parameter values and an initial state for which the output magnitude diverges with positive probability.

papers.title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk
papers.abstract:
Let \((S_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a Bernoulli random walk with \(P(X_i=1)=p\) and \(P(X_i=-1)=q=1-p\), and let \(M_n=\max\{S_0,\ldots,S_n\}\). We consider the semi-best selection problem of maximizing \(P(M_N-S_	au\le1)\) over stopping times \(	au\le N\). Allaart showed that the optimal decision in the critical state \((n,1)\) is determined by a sequence of critical probabilities \(\{p_n\}\), and conjectured that \(p_n	o1/2\). We prove this conjecture. For every fixed \(p<1/2\), the stopping value converges to \(
u=1-(p/q)^2\), while the continuation value converges to \(2p
u\). Since \(2p
u<
u\), stopping is optimal in state \((n,1)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Together with the known bound \(p_n<1/2\) for \(n\ge4\), this yields \(\lim_{n	o\infty}p_n=1/2\).

papers.title: Bounds on the Service Rates of Linear Codes and their Connections to Combinatorial Designs
papers.authors: Monika Yadav, Priyanka Choudhary, Maheshanand Bhaintwal
papers.abstract: The service rate region of a distributed storage system describes the set of concurrent demand vectors that can be served without overloading any individual server, and is a fundamental measure of how effectively redundancy is used. In this paper, we investigate aggregate service rates in distributed data storage systems based on linear codes over arbitrary finite fields. We first derive an upper bound on the aggregate service rate for an arbitrary subset of $t$ data objects in terms of the dual distance and the sizes of their smallest recovery sets. For systematic generator matrices, this bound simplifies to an expression depending only on the code length, the dual distance, and the cardinality of the selected subset. This result extends existing bounds and provides a subset-wise formulation of the First Dual Distance Bound. We then establish conditions under which this upper bound is attained. We apply our results to several important families of linear codes, including MDS codes, Reed-Muller codes, constacyclic codes, and extended Golay codes, and obtain exact values of the maximum aggregate service rates for the corresponding subsets of data objects.

papers.title: Proof of the Erd\H{o}s-Szemer\'edi sunflower conjecture
papers.authors: Matija Buci\'c, Fankang He, Hyunwoo Lee
papers.abstract: In the 1970s, Erd\H{o}s and Szemer\'edi conjectured that for any $n \ge k-1\ge 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_k^n$ for some $c_k<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k \ge 3$.

papers.title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms.
  For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well.
  For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes.
  We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders.
  Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.

papers.title: Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups and Kneser neighbours
papers.authors: Manuel K. -H. M\"uller, Nils R. Scheithauer
papers.abstract: We study Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups of even unimodular lattices of signature $(n,2)$ which arise as lifts of elliptic modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on 1-dimensional cusps. When the weight is small they have to be defined by analytic continuation. In general, they will be smooth but non-holomorphic after regularization. We show exactly in which cases we obtain holomorphic modular forms by computing the intertwining factors appearing in Langlands' constant term formula in terms of standard parameters and Rankin-Selberg $L$-values. This is related to Kneser's neighbour theory of positive-definite even lattices, which also governs the eigenvalues of these Eisenstein series. In particular, we describe the space of singular weight modular forms and construct the function $\Phi_{12}$, the denominator function of the Fake Monster Algebra, as an Eisenstein series. We apply these results to show that the corresponding orthogonal modular varieties are of general type.

papers.title: Global Dynamics and Periodic-Annulus Bifurcations in a Reversible Quintic Li\'enard System
papers.authors: Chen Cao, Nasrin Sadri, Yilei Tang, Zhaoxia Wang
papers.abstract:
We study the global dynamics and bifurcations of the reversible quintic Li\'enard system $\dot{x}=y$, $\dot{y}=a_0x+a_1x^3+a_2x^5+y(b_0x+b_1x^3)$, with $a_2\ne0$. In the original five-parameter space we treat both signs of $a_2$ and determine all global phase-portrait types on the Poincar\'e disc with one, three, or five finite equilibria. The analysis covers generic and generalized pitchfork, saddle-node, Bogdanov--Takens, and Hopf bifurcations; nilpotent and Hamiltonian degeneracies; bifurcations at infinity; and homoclinic, heteroclinic, limit-cycle-breaking, and periodic-annulus-breaking transitions.
  For a parameterized class of generalized polynomial Li\'enard systems whose unique finite equilibrium is the nilpotent origin with exactly one elliptic and one hyperbolic sector we establish a unique critical value of the higher-order damping parameter in the intermediate-degree range, nonexistence of a large-scale periodic annulus in the critical-degree case, and its persistence when the restoring degree dominates. Here large-scale means that the annulus closure meets the boundary of the Poincar\'e disc. In the degree range relevant to the quintic system the critical value gives a large-scale periodic-annulus--homoclinic-orbit-family bifurcation marked by a unique separatrix connection to infinity. For the quintic system with multiple finite equilibria periodic-annulus-breaking bifurcations arise from finite separatrix connections or separatrices reaching equilibria at infinity.
  Using Poincar\'e compactification, local normal forms, rotated vector fields, and separatrix arguments we describe bifurcation sets algebraically or by uniquely characterized critical functions. We obtain complete fixed-coefficient parameter partitions outside $\Omega_{14}$ and determine the admissible critical-surface configurations and their phase portraits inside it.

papers.title: Geodesics in the continuous Hecke monoid
papers.abstract: A permuton is a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals, the limit shape of a sequence of permutations. The sticky product of permutons is a continuous analogue of the Demazure product in the $0$-Hecke monoid; on copulas, the distribution functions of permutons, it is given by the tropical $(\min,+)$ product $\odot$. We show that every absolutely continuous rotation-invariant probability measure $\rho$ on the plane, which we call the profile, generates a one-parameter family of copulas $C^\rho=\{C^\rho_\beta\}_{\beta\in[0,\pi]}$. A copula in this family is defined by a pair of projections of a $\rho$-distributed random vector onto directions at angle $\pi-\beta$. Along this family, the sticky product adds angles: $$C^\rho_{\beta_1}\odot C^\rho_{\beta_2}=C^\rho_{\min(\beta_1+\beta_2,\pi)}.$$ Hence every non-identity element of such a family is a sticky product of two others and has roots of every natural degree. The normalized inversion number of the copula $C^\rho_\beta$ equals $\beta/\pi$. For the Archimedean measure $\mathfrak{Arch}$ the family $C^{\mathfrak{Arch}}$ consists of the limit shapes of the permutations of the uniformly random sorting network, found by Angel et al. and Dauvergne. For the Gaussian measure $\mathcal{N}$ the family $C^{\mathcal{N}}$ consists of Gaussian copulas and contains $\mathit{Unif}$, the uniform measure on the square (the limit shape of the uniformly random permutation); its square root within this family is the Gaussian copula with correlation $-1/\sqrt2$. By the Herschel-Maxwell theorem the Gaussian measure is the only profile whose family contains $\mathit{Unif}$; nevertheless, $\mathit{Unif}$ has another, singular, sticky square root. A discrete analogue of the Gaussian family is the geometric sorting network generated by rotating independent Gaussian points: after rotation by $\pi/2$ its permutation is exactly uniform.

papers.title: Logarithmic corrections and interacting fronts in shifting environments and competition systems
papers.abstract: We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.

papers.title: The Riemann zeta function at the zeros of real-rooted trigonometric polynomials
papers.authors: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Bryce Kerr, Oleksiy Klurman, Guilherme Vedana

papers.title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
papers.authors: Davide Barilari, Eugenio Bellini, Tommaso Rossi
papers.abstract:
We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[
  \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3\alpha_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(\alpha_n+\beta_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly.
  The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.

papers.title: Upper tail probability estimates of suprema of Gaussian processes by matrices-A number theoretic example
papers.abstract: We prove new lower bounds for the upper tail probabilities of suprema of Gaussian processes. We introduce a proper matrix approach. This is continuing recent works of the author on deviations of suprema and decoupling inequalities for parametrized families of Gaussian processes. An application is given to a number theoretic example related to Wintner random M\"obius function.

papers.title: Symmetric Polynomials Method for the Multiple Loewner Chains
papers.authors: Sergio Andraus, Nicole Hufnagel, Jacek Ma{\l}ecki, Vlad Margarint
papers.abstract: We introduce the technique of Symmetric Polynomials in the study of Loewner chains driven by a family of stochastic particle systems including but not limited to Dyson Brownian motion. As a first application of this technique we obtain the phase transitions at the critical parameter $\kappa=4$ in terms of the behavior of a class of symmetric polynomials evolving in time. We obtain new proofs of the phase transitions, we also obtain new closed-form expressions relevant for the models. In addition, we apply this method for some initial deterministic multiple Loewner evolutions. Finally, as this is, to our knowledge, the first paper analyzing this method in the context of multiple Loewner chains driven by root-system based multivariate processes, we also give an overview of potential future applications of this technique in the study of these models.

papers.title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet
papers.abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.

papers.title: The Structure of the Ghost and Swapping Algebras
papers.abstract: The swapping algebras and the ghost algebras were introduced in the papers of Labourie and Bridgeman--Labourie to encode the Poisson structure on spaces of length functions and generalized cross-ratio functions associated to $\Theta$-Anosov representations. They used these algebras to show that correlation functions are stable under the Poisson bracket associated to Atiyah-Bott-Goldman's symplectic form and that length functions are convex along the Hamiltonian flow of other length functions. In this paper, we study the algebraic relationship between these two algebras. In particular, we show that the kernel of a natural surjection from the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra is generated by five families of relations. Consequently, we obtain an isomorphism from an explicit quotient of the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra.

papers.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
papers.abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $\delta \in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_\delta((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.

papers.title: A two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$
papers.authors: Rajeev Gupta, Arpita Mal, Gadadhar Misra, Samya Kumar Ray
papers.abstract: We show that a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ carries a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$; the ``if'' half is the And\^o's theorem. For each of the remaining spaces we exhibit an explicit non-normal $Y \in \mathcal{M}_2$, with $(I,Y)$ an extreme point of the associated matrix ball, for which the induced linear map is contractive but not completely contractive. Since every two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has the $2$-summing property, the $2$-summing property does not imply uniqueness of the operator space structure for two dimensional complex Banach spaces.

papers.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
papers.abstract: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.

papers.title: FOMTools: Development and AI-Assisted Code Generation for First-Order Methods
papers.authors: Vinit Ranjan, Daniel Deza, Anushka Acharya, Jisun Park, Bartolomeo Stellato
papers.abstract: We present FOMTools, an open-source Python package for developing, analyzing, and deploying first-order algorithms for parametric linear and convex quadratic optimization. The user specifies an iteration in Python, with syntax close to its mathematical description. The package represents the iteration as a computation graph of affine and piecewise affine operations. To analyze worst-case performance, FOMTools formulates a mixed-integer verification problem that maximizes a convergence residual over a specified set of problem instances and initial iterates. For probabilistic performance analysis, a batched GPU simulator collects algorithm trajectories and computes statistical bounds on the probability of exceeding a specified convergence tolerance. From the same algorithm description, FOMTools generates specialized solver code for embedded hardware, multicore CPUs, and GPUs. The package first generates the numerical data, factorizations, and matrix-vector routines without any agent. A coding agent then translates the iteration into C or CUDA code and iteratively optimizes the implementation. After each phase, the package runs the generated code on sampled inputs and compares it with a reference execution. FOMTools also serves as a CVXPYgen backend, generating and optimizing solvers for parametric CVXPY problems. We demonstrate FOMTools on sparse coding, network optimization, optimal control, and portfolio rebalancing. The verification bounds reveal worst-case behavior that sampling misses. The generated solvers run up to two orders of magnitude faster than NumPy implementations, and they outperform hand-written GPU code and the OSQP solvers generated by CVXPYgen.

papers.title: Finite convexification by Minkowski summation
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact set and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact convex set. We study the problem of when there exists $\lambda>0$ such that the Minkowski sum $A+\lambda K$ is convex. First, we show that this finite convexification is equivalent to a uniform covering condition on the exposed sets of $A$ and $K$. We then show that another characterization is possible in terms of the covering radii of the iterated exposed sets after translating each exposed face of $K$ so that its relative centroid is $0$. In the case of convex polytopes, we show that it suffices to check the exposed sets in the first level of the iteration. We also study several special cases, such as strictly convex convexifiers, lower-dimensional convexifiers, strongly isomorphic polytopes, and the planar case.

papers.title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments
papers.authors: Xuanzhao Gao, Malte R\"osner, Jason Kaye, Alex Barnett
papers.abstract: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nystr\"om method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO$_2$ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by $198$ $p_z$-like orbitals, retaining the $2613^2$ non-negligible entries of the $198^4$-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on $1.3$ million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of $0.004\%$, at a cost of $22$ node-hours.

papers.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression
papers.abstract:
We show that gradient descent (GD) with step size $\eta$ can achieve $\varepsilon$ optimality gap on the multiclass logistic regression loss in a number of iterations $T$ that is independent of $\varepsilon$. To do so, the step size $\eta$ must be chosen large enough as a function of $\varepsilon$ (and properties of the linearly separable dataset), while $T$ is a constant that only depends on the data. The relevant properties of the data include the number of points and their margin (for $T$), and one additional quantity (for $\eta$) that turns out to be necessary in dimension $d \geq 3$. The proofs build on the known fact that, as $\eta \to \infty$, suitably rescaled GD becomes the perceptron algorithm, and the latter finds a perfect classifier in $T$ iterations. A similar claim was shown for two classes in dimension $d = 2$ using other proof techniques.
  This result adds to previous works that showed GD on the logistic regression loss can be accelerated by taking large step sizes. Those provoke a wild, oscillatory initial phase, followed by a stable phase. We provide results of this (qualitatively different) nature, too.

papers.title: An Efficient Open-Source Framework for Thermohygromechanical Phase-Field Simulation of Drying Damage Refractory Castables
papers.authors: Murilo H. Moreira, Roberto F. Ausas, Stefano Dal Pont
papers.abstract: The water removal from refractory castables is a complex process involving heat and mass transport and thermohygromechanical stresses. In order to reduce the risk of explosive spalling by improving the heat-up curves, numerical models are critical to predict the castable behavior during drying. However, most of the existing models either neglect the thermomechanical stresses or consider them as an \textit{a posteriori} assessment of the likelihood of failure. The present work proposes an open-source thermohygromechanical phase-field model to simulate the drying of refractory castables and predict the occurrence of explosive spalling. The model is based on an adaptive two-scale time-stepping strategy that allows for a significant reduction of the computational cost associated with the simulation. The model was validated against literature results and qualitative comparisons with experimental data were carried out to assess its ability to predict the failure behavior of partially saturated porous media during heating. The numerical simulations were also applied to investigate the impact of different heating methods on the risk of failure during drying. It was found that even at the significantly lower heating rates typical of refractory castable drying - compared to the fire accidents that motivate most thermomechanical studies on concrete structures - thermomechanical stresses still play a significant role in the explosive spalling, a finding well established for concrete under fire but novel for refractory castables. As a consequence, it was also concluded that the use of heterogeneous heating methods can increase the likelihood of explosive spalling. Ultimately, feasible solutions to increase the drying efficiency and safety that are compatible with the industrial setting were proposed and a free, open-source implementation of the model is provided.

papers.title: Fourth moments of prime exponential sums and exceptional sets for sums and differences of primes
papers.abstract: We prove a square root bound for the exceptional sets in the binary Goldbach and prime difference problems under quasi Riemann Hypothesis. If every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most a fixed $1/2\leq\Theta<11/12$, then $E_+(N)\ll_\Theta N^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$ and $E_-(N)\ll_\Theta N^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$. Here $E_+(N)$ counts the even integers greater than $2$ and at most $N$ that are not sums of two primes, and $E_-(N)$ counts the positive even integers at most $N$ that are not differences of two primes. The common analytic estimate is a fourth moment bound of the minor arcs for a smoothed prime exponential sum.

papers.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
papers.abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

papers.title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
papers.authors: Zach Hunter, Barnab\'as Janzer, Oliver Janzer, Benny Sudakov
papers.abstract:
In 1991, Erd\H{o}s, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked to estimate the smallest $u=u(n,d,s)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with average degree at least $d$ has a subgraph on at most $u$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$. We resolve this problem up to polylogarithmic factors for all even values of $s$. More precisely, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $d\geq s$ has a subgraph on $O_s\left(\max\left\{\frac{n}{d^{s/(s-2)}}(\log n)^{180},\log n\right\}\right)$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$, whenever $s\ge 4$ is even. This improves a result of Janzer, Sudakov and Tomon, who obtained a similar conclusion for subgraphs of average degree at least $s$.
  We also prove that for every positive integer $s$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite family $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs with minimum degree $s$ such that $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})=O(n^{2-2/s+\varepsilon})$. This is tight and is the first result of similar kind that applies to odd values of $s$ greater than 3.

papers.title: Socle formulas for rigid irreducible components of Lusztig's nilpotent varieties in type $A$
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. For any irreducible component $C$ of a nilpotent variety of type $A$ let $\pi(C)$ be the irreducible representation of a general linear group over $F$ attached to it. We show that if the multisegment of $C$ is multiplicity free, $C$ is rigid if and only if $\pi(C)$ is $\square$-irreducible. In this case, \[
  \pi(C*D)=soc\bigl(\pi(C)\times\pi(D)\bigr),\qquad
  \pi(D*C)=soc\bigl(\pi(D)\times\pi(C)\bigr) \] for every irreducible component $D$, where $*$ is the binary operation defined by Aizenbud and Lapid, in accordance with a conjecture of Lapid and M\'inguez.
