For half-space exponential last passage percolation (LPP) and the half-space log-gamma polymer, we establish convergence of their respective rescaled last passage time and free energy to the directed landscape when the observation window is at distance $f(n)n^{2/3}$ from the boundary and the attractive boundary strength is $o(f(n)n^{-1/3})$, where $f(n)\to\infty$ may diverge arbitrarily slowly. We also show that this condition on the boundary strength is sharp at the level of scales: any boundary strength of order $f(n)n^{-1/3}$ changes the limiting behavior for sufficiently large temporal separations. For exponential LPP, we prove a phase transition in the point-to-point last passage time as the boundary attraction varies on the scale \(f(n)n^{-1/3}\). As the attraction increases, the fluctuations transition from a bulk-dominated KPZ regime to a boundary-dominated Gaussian regime, with a critical window governed by the positive part of a shifted Gaussian. The limiting law in the critical window manifests the competition between a Gaussian boundary contribution and a bulk contribution whose magnitude vanishes under the Gaussian scaling.

papers.title: "Game, Set, Match": Double Delight Watching a Grand Slam Tennis Match
papers.authors: Edsel A. Pena, Dip Das, Yuexuan Wu
papers.abstract: Probabilistic properties of tennis scoring systems are examined and compared with best-of-K systems. A model, where each player has his/her own probability of winning his/her service point and which remains invariant for the duration of the match, and where outcomes of points played are independent of each other, is assumed. Probabilities of winning a game tie-breaker, a game, a set tie-breaker, a set, and the match are obtained. Since tennis scoring systems are unique, probability calculations require decomposing big and complicated problems into smaller and simpler constituent problems, solving these sub-problems, then combining to obtain the solution to the big problem. The problems that arise from tennis scoring systems offer excellent pedagogical venues for teaching probability, in particular, the use of the Theorem of Total Probability and the Iterated Rules for Mean, Variance, and Covariance. There are also many interesting questions in tennis, foremost of which is whether a tennis match under this assumption will actually end with probability one; or whether when two players of `equal abilities' play a match, the first server possesses an advantage. These questions are addressed in this work. Tennis scoring systems are technically statistical decision systems to determine the better player. Since such a decision system is based on a finite number of points played, erroneous decisions could arise, such as the inferior player winning the match. We compare different systems in terms of the probability of the better player winning, as well as the duration of the match in terms of the number of points played.

papers.title: Genus $2$ pencils on surfaces with $p_g=K^2=1$, envelopes, and conics tangent to plane cubic curves
papers.authors: Fabrizio Catanese (Accademia dei Lincei), Noah Ruhland (Universit\"at Bayreuth)
papers.abstract:
We consider $(1,1)$-surfaces, namely, minimal compact complex surfaces $S$ with $p_g (S) =K_S^2=1$: for these the bicanonical map is a covering of degree $4$ of the plane $P^2$.
  And we answer a question posed by Meng Chen, whether they can contain a genus 2 pencil (this is the standard reason of failure of birationality of the bicanonical map).
  Our main theorem says that those which admit a genus 2 pencil form an irreducible subvariety of codimension $3$ in their moduli space $\frak M_{[1,1]}$; moreover, the general such surface admits exactly $24$ such pencils, corresponding to $12$ pencils of conics in $P^2$.
  The real fun is to relate this variety to the geometry of pencils of conics in the plane everywhere tangent to a cubic curve and a line. We investigate the corresponding variety $\cal{T}$ of triples and provide explicit equations using the classical theory of envelopes: among others, equations given in terms of the Weierstrass normal form of the cubic.

papers.title: Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate the Cauchy problem for Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular (less than continuous) coefficients. We prove $H^\infty$ well-posedness in the very weak sense under suitable assumptions of the distributional structure of the coefficients and decay on the lower order terms. Consistency is proven with the classical $H^\infty$-results when the equation coefficients are smooth.

papers.title: GKLO representations for shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs of split simply-laced type, and construct their GKLO representations, following similar recent developments in the case of shifted twisted Yangians. A full proof that our formulas yield a representation is given.

papers.title: Semialgebraic interior layers in root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
papers.abstract: Finite-degree root plots of bounded-height monic integer polynomials can exhibit gaps around interior points of their root closures. Outside the closed unit disk, these closures coincide with Mandelbrot sets for affine iterated function systems with collinear digits. We construct explicit semialgebraic interior layers, certified when finite inverse orbits enter canonical self-covering parallelograms. Such parallelograms exist exactly in the non-real lens, which contains the non-real locus precisely from twenty maps onward. Within the non-real lens, limits of each capture level are captured within two additional steps, optimally, and the layers recover the locus by closure. The layers expose persistent interior deficits: explicit quadratic parameters evade every finite level; sufficiently close distinct parameters have logarithmically growing capture depths; the underlying lattice obstruction yields degree-dependent root-free radii, explaining such gaps. For non-real parameters of modulus at least the square root of the number of maps, exact enclosure trees have sharp, alphabet-independent branching bounds.

papers.title: Extreme value theorem for geodesic flow on the quotient of the theta group
papers.authors: Jaelin Kim, Seul Bee Lee, Seonhee Lim
papers.abstract: We establish an extreme value theorem for the geodesic flow $g_t$ on the hyperbolic surface $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ associated with the theta group $\Theta$. To capture excursions into both cusps of this surface, we introduce a generalized continued fraction algorithm obtained by splicing the even and odd--odd continued fraction maps into a single dynamical system. We prove that the natural extension of this map is isomorphic to the first return map of the geodesic flow on a suitable cross-section. Using spectral properties of the associated transfer operator, we derive a Galambos-type extreme value law for the digits of the spliced continued fraction. This symbolic result is then translated into a geometric extreme value theorem describing maximal cusp excursions of geodesics on $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$.

papers.title: Forcing with random variables in bounded arithmetics and set theory
papers.abstract: We analyse the Boolean-valued random forcing $B_{M,\Omega}$ in bounded arithmetics developed in Krajicek (Forcing with random variables and proof complexity, vol. 382, Cambridge University Press, 2011) from the perspective of the forcing in set theory. We observe that under the assumption that $M$ is a non-standard $\omega_1$-saturated model of true arithmetics of size $\omega_1$, and $\Omega \in M$ is a non-standard number, $B_{M,\Omega}$ is isomorphic to the probability (random) algebra corresponding to the product measure space on $2^{\omega_1}$ (and hence does not depend on $M$ and $\Omega$). Thus, in a well-defined sense, the forcing $B_{M,\Omega}$ adds a "random integer" to the model $M$, using a non-separable algebra corresponding to $2^{\omega_1}$. If $G$ is a generic filter for $B_{M,\Omega}$ over a transitive model of set theory $V$, we naturally define in $V[G]$ two-valued generic extensions $M[G]^{R}$ of $M$ which correspond to Boolean-valued models in Krajicek's book (where $R$ ranges over collections of random variables which function as names for new integers). We study the relationship between the linear order $(M,<)$ and its extensions $(M[G]^R,<)$, proving several results on the extent of the mutual density of new integers in $M[G]^{R}$ and the "ground-model" integers in $M$. At the end, we discuss some advantages and limitations of interpreting forcing in bounded arithmetics (and other weak theories) in the framework of set-theoretic forcing, providing an alternative to an axiomatic approach to forcing in bounded arithmetics formulated by Atserias and M\"uller in Partially definable forcing and bounded arithmetic, Archive for Mathematical Logic 54 (2015), 1-33.

papers.title: Sublinear elliptic equations with a sharp change of sign in the nonlinearity
papers.authors: M\'onica Clapp, Alberto Salda\~na, Delia Schiera
papers.abstract: We study the semilinear indefinite elliptic problem \[ -\Delta u = Q_\Omega |u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \] where $Q_\Omega = \chi_\Omega - \chi_{\mathbb{R}^N \setminus \Omega}$, $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded smooth subset, $N \geq 3$, and $1 \leq p < 2$, with $p=1$ corresponding to the sign nonlinearity. Using a variational approach, we investigate the uniqueness or multiplicity of nonnegative solutions depending on the shape of $\Omega$ and the existence of different types of nodal solutions. We also show that all solutions have compact support and analyze how the support of the ground state depends on $p$, proving convergence to the whole space as $p\to 2^{-}$ and identifying some qualitative features such as starshapedness and Lipschitz regularity of the support. We also establish a link between these problems and a two-phase Serrin-type torsion overdetermined problem.

papers.title: Zonal states and improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish polynomially improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces in the critical energy regime. We also show that, below the critical energy, the H\"ormander bound is saturated by explicit eigenstates, which we call magnetic zonal states. These states resemble zonal harmonics on the sphere and equidistribute on Lagrangian tori in phase space.

papers.title: A zero-one law for the spectral gap property of pairs in SU(2)
papers.abstract: For $n \ge 2$, Gamburd, Jakobson, and Sarnak [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 1, 51-85 (1999)] conjectured that almost every $n$-tuple in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ has a spectral gap. Toward this conjecture, Fisher [Int. Math. Res. Not. (2006)] established a zero-one law for $n \ge 3$, but obtained only a partial result for $n=2$. In this paper, we prove that the zero-one law also holds for $n=2$. We also remark that a Baire categorical analogue of this result holds.

papers.title: Arbitrary order stationarity preserving stabilized finite elements for multidimensional nonlinear hyperbolic problems. Application to the Euler equations with gravity
papers.authors: Moussa Ziggaf, Davide Torlo, Mario Ricchiuto
papers.abstract: We develop arbitrarily high-order, stationarity-preserving stabilized finite element methods for multidimensional nonlinear hyperbolic balance laws on Cartesian grids. We aim at approximating all the steady states of the problem at hand, including non-trivial genuinely multidimensional equilibria, with a level of accuracy higher than the nominal one of the underlying scheme. We formalize more precisely the meaning of stationarity preservation, providing some technical conditions for its realizability. We then recast the multidimensional global-flux quadrature of Barsukow et al. (Num. Meth. PDEs, 2025) as a local preprocessing of the physical fluxes that maps continuous polynomial vector fields to a local space with Raviart--Thomas-type structure. Both the Galerkin and SUPG formulations are recast in this setting. The resulting methods extend the stationarity-preserving finite-volume approach of Barsukow et al. (J. Comput. Phys., 2026) to high-order continuous finite elements and Barsukow et al. (Num. Meth. PDEs, 2025) to nonlinear balance laws. We analyze key properties of the proposed schemes, including local conservation and nodal superconvergence of the discrete steady kernel, and we discuss their relation to low-Mach-compliant discretizations. We apply the framework to the compressible Euler equations with gravity. A simple source-term reformulation yields machine-precision preservation of isothermal hydrostatic equilibria. Extensive numerical benchmarks, including moving equilibrium, near-equilibrium, and instability-dominated regimes, demonstrate clear improvements in robustness and accuracy over standard SUPG and reference finite-volume methods.

papers.title: A second-order energy-stable sequential regularization scheme for the Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a second-order decoupled scheme for the Navier-Stokes equations based on the idea of the auxiliary variable and the sequential regularization method (SRM). The proposed scheme enjoys unconditional energy stability, which is generally unavailable for the existing SRM, while preserving its key advantage of avoiding artificial pressure boundary conditions and maintaining the original velocity boundary conditions. We establish a viscosity-independent low-order stability estimate and a higher-order stability estimate for the proposed scheme. Furthermore, we derive global-in-time second-order error estimates in two dimensions and corresponding local-in-time estimates in three dimensions, without imposing any time-step restrictions. A series of numerical experiments confirm the convergence and stability, and demonstrate improved accuracy and incompressibility control compared with the projection method and the conventional SRM. In particular, both high-Reynolds-number and three-dimensional numerical simulations further demonstrate the robustness and reliability of the proposed method for complex incompressible flows.

papers.title: Ultrahomogeneity of monounary algebras
papers.abstract: A structure is ultrahomogeneous if every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures can be extended to an automorphism of the structure. The aim of this paper is to provide an explicit description of ultrahomogeneous monounary algebras of arbitrary cardinalities. We also show that a monounary algebra is ultrahomogeneous if and only if it is 1-ultrahomogeneous. These results are then viewed in the context of a several related concepts, including $\omega$-categoricity, homomorphism-homogeneity, (partial-)homogeneity, and transitivity.

papers.title: Deligne's weight spectral sequence and tautological cohomology of the moduli space of curves
papers.abstract: We have written a computer program that implements Deligne's pullback and pushforward weight spectral sequences to compute the weight graded pieces of the rational cohomology of moduli spaces of pointed smooth curves (as well as curves of compact type and curves with rational tails) in cases where the cohomology groups appearing in the boundary stratification of the Deligne-Mumford compactification are generated by tautological classes (and when Pixton's relations are all relations). The weight graded pieces are computed together with the induced action of the symmetric group permuting the points on the curves. Using the computer program we have determined this information in the case of genus five as well as in the case of genus three with three marked points.

papers.title: Quasi-random splitting method for accurate and efficient multiphysics simulation
papers.authors: Lei Li, Yunxiao Liu, Chenchen Wan
papers.abstract: We propose a quasi-random operator splitting method for evolution equations driven by multiple mechanisms. The method uses a one-dimensional low-discrepancy sequence to determine the ordering of the subflows through a direct point-to-permutation construction, while applying each subflow exactly once per time step. Thus, for a decomposition into \(p\) operators, the proposed method requires only \(p\) subflow evaluations per step, compared with essentially \(2p-2\) evaluations for the classical multi-operator Strang splitting when \(p\geq 3\). In contrast to randomized splitting, the quasi-random ordering is deterministic once the underlying sequence is fixed and avoids the run-to-run fluctuations caused by random permutations. To analyze the resulting scheme, we develop a convergence framework that connects the discrepancy of the induced operator orderings with cancellation of the leading commutator errors accumulated over time. For an arbitrary fixed number of bounded linear operators, we establish a global error of order \(O(\tau^2\log N)\), equivalently \(O(\tau^2|\log\tau|)\) for fixed terminal time, which is essentially second order. We further extend the same cancellation mechanism to the nonlinear Allen--Cahn equation and obtain the same essentially second-order convergence behavior under suitable Sobolev regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments for bounded linear systems and the Allen--Cahn equation confirm the predicted convergence rates and show that the proposed quasi-random splitting strategy retains the low per-step computational cost of a Lie-type splitting method while achieving accuracy close to second order.

papers.title: A Gradient Sampling Algorithm for Noisy Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.authors: Albert S. Berahas, Frank E. Curtis, Lara Zebiane
papers.abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for minimizing locally Lipschitz objective functions that may be nonconvex and/or nonsmooth. The algorithm, which is built upon the gradient-sampling methodology, is designed specifically for cases when objective and generalized gradient values might be subject to bounded, uncontrollable errors. A novel assumption pertaining to such errors in nonsmooth settings is introduced that decouples the noise that may be present due to typical errors in derivative estimates with noise that may be due to misidentification of segments of differentiability of the objective. Similarly to state-of-the-art guarantees for noisy smooth optimization, it is proved for the algorithm that, with probability one, either the sequence of objective values will decrease without bound or the algorithm will generate an iterate at which a measure of stationarity is below a threshold that depends proportionally on the error bounds for the objective function and generalized gradient values. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the algorithm can indeed perform approximate optimization robustly despite errors in objective and generalized gradient values.

papers.title: When is cumulative dose response monotonic? Analysis of incoherent feedforward motifs
papers.authors: Moh Kamalul Wafi, Arthur C. B. de Oliveira, Eduardo D. Sontag
papers.abstract: We study the monotonicity of the cumulative dose response (cDR) for a class of incoherent feedforward motifs (IFFM) systems with linear intermediate dynamics and nonlinear output dynamics. While the instantaneous dose response (DR) may be nonmonotone with respect to the input, the cDR can still be monotone. To analyze this phenomenon, we derive an integral representation of the sensitivity of cDR with respect to the input and establish general sufficient conditions for both monotonicity and nonmonotonicity. These results reduce the problem to verifying qualitative sign properties along system trajectories. The structural conditions identify eight canonical IFFM models, four of which are analyzed in detail within the proposed framework. In particular, IFFM1 and IFFM3 exhibit monotone cDR despite potentially nonmonotone DR, while IFFM2 is monotone already at the level of DR, which implies monotonicity of cDR. In contrast, IFFM4 exhibits nonmonotone cDR. Numerical simulations indicate that these properties persist beyond the structured initial conditions used in the analysis. Overall, our results provide a unified framework for understanding how system structure shapes monotonicity in cumulative input--output responses.

papers.title: Tree-Adaptive Multiscale Kernel Lasso in Samplet Coordinates
papers.authors: Sara Avesani, Gaia Fumagalli, Michael Multerer, Chiara Segala
papers.abstract: We develop a novel framework for sparse multiscale kernel approximation of large scattered data problems based on a samplet representation. Samplets form a multiresolution analysis of localized discrete signed measures and enable quasi-sparse representations of kernel matrices associated to asymptotically smooth kernels as well as smoothness detection of scattered data. Building on the latter, we introduce an adaptive data site selection strategy based on the native reproducing kernel Hilbert space norm of the samplet expansion coefficients. The selection results in a small set of representative data sites, significantly reducing the effective problem size. On the corresponding reduced kernel subspace, we solve an $\ell^1$-regularized least-squares problem using a trust-region semismooth Newton method in a normal-map formulation, stabilized by an online low-rank SVD on the active set to handle the notorious ill-conditioning of kernel matrices. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, including multi-kernel models with varying lengthscales, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves accurate reconstructions with considerably sparser representations and good computational efficiency.

papers.title: The record statistic and forward stability of Schubert products
papers.authors: Andrew Hardt, Reuven Hodges, Hanzhang Yin
papers.abstract: We initiate a probabilistic study of forward stability for products of Schubert polynomials through the record statistic (left-to-right maxima) of permutations. Building on the explicit record formula for forward stability obtained by Hardt and Wallach, we study random pairs of permutations drawn from three natural families: uniform permutations, Grassmannian permutations, and Boolean permutations. For each family, we determine record probabilities and use them to analyze the asymptotic behavior of forward stability. For uniform and Grassmannian permutations, we obtain asymptotics for the mean together with limiting distribution results. For Boolean permutations, we prove linear-order growth of the mean, and our analysis also produces an explicit time-inhomogeneous Markov chain that yields an exact linear-time uniform sampler. Beyond these cases, we prove that the record-set statistic is equidistributed on the avoidance classes of $132$ and $231$, and consequently the corresponding forward stability distributions coincide. We conclude with conjectures for numerous further permutation classes and a conjectural recursive criterion for when two avoidance classes have the same record-set distribution.

papers.title: On $u$-Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concepts of the $u$-bracket, finite multiple harmonic $u$-series, and $u$-multiple zeta values via the Carlitz module. These objects serve as function field counterparts to the classical theory of $q$-analogs. We prove that the "limits" of finite multiple harmonic $u$-series at Carlitz torsion points yield Thakur's multiple zeta values and finite multiple zeta values over $\mathbb{F}_r(\theta)$ from analytic and algebraic perspectives, respectively. This can be regarded as a positive characteristic analog of the results by Bachmann, Takeyama, and Tasaka [BTT18]. Furthermore, we investigate the properties of $u$-multiple zeta values and their expansions, obtaining a family of explicit relations among Thakur's multiple zeta values at both positive and non-positive indices.

papers.title: Arithmetic volume of Shtukas and Langlands duality
papers.abstract: We extend the work of Feng--Yun--Zhang relating the arithmetic volume of Shtukas with derivatives of zeta functions by allowing arbitrary coweights for split semisimple algebraic groups. As in their original work, the formula involves some numbers called eigenweights. We obtain uniform formulas for the eigenweights in terms of the Langlands dual group, marking the first structural role for the dual group in such formulas governing derivatives of L-functions.

papers.title: Optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy
papers.authors: Junior da Silva Bessa, Jehan Oh
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy law and oblique boundary conditions. The approach developed here relies on first deriving uniform boundary H\"older estimates for perturbed models with oblique boundary data in ``almost $C^{1}$-flat'' domains. Building upon these estimates, the desired regularity is obtained through a compactness and stability framework for viscosity solutions. As a byproduct of our analysis, we determine the optimal H\"older exponent for solutions when the governing operator is quasiconvex or quasiconcave. In addition, we establish an improved regularity result along vanishing points of the source term.

papers.title: An infinite series of Gorenstein local algebras failing the affine homogeneity property
papers.abstract: We provide an infinite series of commutative finite-dimensional Gorenstein local algebras $A_n$ for $n \ge 2$. We give an elementary proof that the maximal ideal of every algebra $A_n$ possesses a one-dimensional subspace that is different from the socle and invariant under the automorphism group of $A_n$. The latter implies that the algebras $A_n$ fail the affine homogeneity property. We also discuss some consequences concerning additive actions on projective hypersurfaces, related to the generalized Hassett-Tschinkel correspondence for these algebras.

papers.title: Muon Dynamics as a Spectral Wasserstein Flow
papers.abstract: Gradient normalization can stabilize deep-learning optimization, and spectral normalizations are especially natural for matrix-shaped parameter blocks; Muon is the motivating example. We study an idealized deterministic, continuous-time, vanishing-momentum version of this idea in the mean-field regime, where wide models are represented by probability measures on parameter space. Starting from normalized matrix flows, we introduce Spectral Wasserstein distances indexed by norms $\gamma$ on positive semidefinite matrices: the trace norm recovers the classical $W_2$ distance, the operator norm gives the Muon geometry, and Schatten norms interpolate between them. We develop a static Kantorovich formulation, a max--min robust-cost representation, and Gaussian reductions extending the Bures formula. For monotone norms, we prove equivalence with a Benamou--Brenier formulation and obtain a gradient-flow interpretation of normalized mean-field training dynamics. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting flows for MMD objectives, Gaussian reductions, two-layer ReLU models, and shallow attention.

papers.title: Simultaneous avoidance of length-4 patterns in ascent sequences
papers.authors: Qi Liu, Sergey Kitaev, Philip B. Zhang
papers.abstract:
Ascent sequences form a central class of combinatorial objects, as they are in bijection with several important families such as (2+2)-free posets, Stoimenow matchings, and other Fishburn objects, and are enumerated by the Fishburn numbers.
  We study pattern avoidance in ascent sequences for the five patterns of length 4: $0101$, $0102$, $0112$, $0120$, and $0121$. These patterns arise naturally from recent work on pattern avoidance in related families of Fishburn objects, including Stoimenow matchings and (2+2)-free posets. We enumerate ascent sequences avoiding any subset of these patterns, with the exception of the sets $\{0120\}$, $\{0121\}$, and $\{0120,0121\}$, for which the enumeration remains open.
  Our results reveal that the corresponding avoidance classes fall into $16$ Wilf equivalence classes and exhibit a wide range of enumerative behaviour, including connections to classical sequences such as the Catalan and Fibonacci numbers, as well as polynomial formulas and rational generating functions; several of the sequences we obtain appear to be new. Our methods combine structural decompositions with generating-tree techniques and, in several cases, rely on reductions to shorter patterns via restricted growth functions. This work contributes to the broader study of pattern avoidance across Fishburn families and highlights further connections between ascent sequences and other combinatorial structures.

papers.title: The Asymmetric Hamming Bidistance and Distributions over Binary Asymmetric Channels
papers.authors: Shukai Wang, Cuiling Fan, Chunming Tang, Zhengchun Zhou
papers.abstract: The binary asymmetric channel is a model for practical communication systems where the error probabilities for symbol transitions $0\rightarrow 1$ and $1\rightarrow0$ differ substantially. In this paper, we introduce the notion of asymmetric Hamming bidistance (AHB) and its two-dimensional distribution, which separately captures directional discrepancies between codewords. This finer characterization enables a more discriminative analysis of decoding the error probabilities for maximum-likelihood decoding (MLD), particularly when conventional measures, such as weight distributions and existing discrepancy-based bounds, fail to distinguish code performance. Building on this concept, we derive a new upper bound on the average error probability for binary codes under MLD and show that, in general, it is incomparable with the two existing bounds derived by Cotardo and Ravagnani (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 68 (5), 2022). To demonstrate its applicability, we compute the complete AHB distributions for several families of codes, including two-weight and three-weight projective codes (with the zero codeword removed) via strongly regular graphs and 3-class association schemes, as well as nonlinear codes constructed from symmetric balanced incomplete block designs (SBIBDs).

papers.title: Convergence of $k$-point functions in high dimensional percolation
papers.authors: Shirshendu Chatterjee, Pranav Chinmay, Jack Hanson, Philippe Sosoe
papers.abstract:
We establish first-order asymptotics for the $k$-point connectivity function in critical Bernoulli percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ assuming $d>6$ and Hara's two-point asymptotic. For every $k\ge 3$ and distinct macroscopically separated locations, the probability that the corresponding lattice points lie in the same open cluster, rescaled by $n^{(4-d)(k-1)-2}$, converges as $n \to \infty$ to an explicit sum of integrals indexed by trees. This confirms a conjecture of Aizenman and Newman.
  We also establish convergence of chemical-distance-decorated $k$-point functions. Conditionally on a set of $k$ point lying in the same cluster, this identifies the joint limiting distribution of all pairwise chemical distances after quadratic rescaling. It is described by binary trees with explicit laws along the edges. The decorated expansion also gives $k$ point asymptotics in the near-critical window.
  Our proof uses our previous results on convergence to the incipient infinite clusters to decouple macroscopic connections, as well as distributional convergence of the chemical distance.

papers.title: Non-Autonomous Return Dynamics for Nested Convex Bodies:\\ Cubic Tangency, Summable Geometric Variation, and Critical Regimes
papers.abstract:
We study a non-autonomous geometric dynamics generated by successive normal transitions between nested convex boundaries sharing a common tangency point. For \(C_{k+1}\subset C_k\subset\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(\mathcal G_k:\partial C_k\to\partial C_{k+1}\) be the first intersection of the inward normal ray with the next boundary. In signed arclength coordinates, the induced scalar map \(G_k\) is tangent to the identity to second order. Writing the boundaries locally as graphs \(f_k\), we prove the uniform defect estimate \[ |G_k(s)-s|\leq C\|f_{k+1}-f_k\|_{C^2}|s|^3. \] The first nonlinear term is cubic: \[ G_k(s)=s+\beta_k s^3+O(s^4), \qquad \beta_k= \frac{(\kappa_{k+1}-\kappa_k)(\kappa_{k+1}-2\kappa_k)}{6}, \] where \(\kappa_k=-f_k''(0)\). Higher coefficients satisfy a diagonal-vanishing principle: they vanish when the corresponding boundary jets coincide.
  If the geometric variation is summable, \(\sum_{k\geq0}\|f_{k+1}-f_k\|_{C^2}<\infty\), then the full transition defect is summable. Every sufficiently small nonzero orbit has finite total drift and converges to a nonzero limit; hence the common tangency point is Lyapunov stable but not locally attractive. The non-autonomous composition defines a limiting displacement map tangent to the identity.
  We also study abstract parabolic recurrences with nonsummable nonlinear drift. A weighted comparison principle yields polynomial and logarithmic asymptotic laws, including critical quartic and quintic regimes: \[ s_k\sim(3c\log k)^{-1/3}, \qquad s_k\sim(4c\log k)^{-1/4}. \] These abstract regimes are kept separate from the geometric theory. The main open problem is to determine which critical parabolic behaviors can actually be realized by nested convex boundaries.

papers.title: Sofic measures
papers.authors: Marie-Pierre B\'eal, Vincent Jug\'e, Eugene Gilburg, Jean Mairesse, Dominique Perrin
papers.abstract: Sofic measures, also known as hidden Markov measures, have been extensively studied. In this paper, we survey some equivalent definitions of this notion and improve a bound for deciding whether a sofic measure is~$k$-step Markov. We prove that if an invariant sofic measure with a linear representation of dimension~$n$ is a~$k$-step Markov chain, then~$k$ can be chosen at most equal to~$\binom{n}{2}$ and that this bound is tight for sofic measures over an alphabet of size $3$.

papers.title: Lyapunov exponents for uniformly hyperbolic random matrix products
papers.abstract: We consider a finite family of invertible $2 \times 2$ real matrices and a transitive Markov shift on the index set. Let $\lambda$ be the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products driven by the Markov shift. We prove that, if the matrices are projectively uniformly hyperbolic with respect to the Markov shift, then $\lambda$ admits an explicit representation in terms of an infinite matrix. This rapidly convergent representation yields a polynomial-time algorithm for approximating $\lambda$: only $O\big( (\log(1/\varepsilon))^3 \big)$ arithmetic operations are needed to achieve error $\varepsilon$. Furthermore, $\lambda$ depends real analytically on the matrix entries and the transition probabilities near a projectively uniformly hyperbolic system, and each Taylor coefficient can be approximated in polynomial time.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of Landau solutions to the MHD system and energy decay
papers.authors: Nicola De Nitti, Yun Wang, Shaoheng Zhang
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional incompressible MHD system. Any weak solution satisfying a strong energy inequality is $L^2$-asymptotically stable around a Landau solution. Under an additional integrability assumption on the initial perturbation, we also obtain an explicit algebraic decay rate for the $L^2$-norm of the velocity and magnetic perturbations.

papers.title: A Weak Solution of Inverse Treblecross
papers.abstract: We study Inverse Treblecross, the impartial avoidance version of the game Treblecross, in which completing a line of three X's is prohibited. We give a weak solution of the game: an empty board of $n$ cells is a $\mathscr{P}$-position (Sprague--Grundy value $0$) if and only if $n\equiv 0,2,3,6,9\pmod{10}$, and has value $1$ if $n\equiv 1,4,5,7,8\pmod{10}$. In particular the empty-board Sprague--Grundy sequence is the purely periodic sequence of period $10$ with values in $\{0,1\}$. The proof introduces two characteristic functions on $\mathbb Z/10\mathbb Z$ and a family of regular positions, and shows by induction that such a position splits, under a reduction move, into a disjunctive sum of regular positions whose sign product is preserved or inverted.

papers.title: Cyclic Equalizability Characterized by Parikh Vectors
papers.authors: Sarunyu Thongjarast, Sarit Pasiphol, Suthee Ruangwises
papers.abstract: Cyclic equalizability is a notion introduced by Shinagawa and Nuida in 2025, in the study of card-based cryptography. Informally, a collection of words is cyclically equalizable if, by inserting the same letters at the same positions in all words, they can be transformed into words that are cyclic shifts of one another. Shinagawa and Nuida showed that two binary words of equal length are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Hamming weight. They also posed the problem of characterizing cyclic equalizability over larger alphabets. In this paper, we completely characterize cyclic equalizability for two words over an arbitrary finite alphabet by proving that two words are cyclically equalizable if and only if they have the same Parikh vector.

papers.title: Koszul Duality for Quadratic Monomial Algebras
papers.abstract: Let \(\Lambda\) be a quadratic monomial algebra and let \(\Lambda^{!}\) denote its Koszul dual. We study finitely presented and finitely copresented graded modules over \(\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda^{!}\), and use this structure to obtain explicit forms of derived and singular Koszul duality. We prove that quadratic monomial algebras are both graded coherent and graded cocoherent. Applying this to the Koszul dual \(\Lambda^{!}\), which is again quadratic monomial, we show that finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules coincide with perfect and coperfect modules, respectively. It follows that the corresponding tails and cotails categories are hereditary abelian categories, and their objects are described in terms of linear and colinear modules. We also prove that quadratic monomial algebras are absolutely Koszul and have global linearity defect at most two. Consequently, finite-dimensional graded \(\Lambda\)-modules have rational Poincar\'e series, while finitely presented and finitely copresented graded \(\Lambda^{!}\)-modules have rational Hilbert series. As applications, we refine graded and ungraded derived Koszul dualities, singular Koszul dualities, and Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand correspondences for quadratic monomial algebras. We further describe the induced nonstandard \(t\)-structures on bounded derived and singularity categories and derive bounds for the finitistic dimension of \(\Lambda\) in terms of finite paths in the Koszul dual algebra.

papers.title: Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Nonlinear Control
papers.authors: Eray Unsal Atay, Venkat Chandrasekaran, Victoria Kostina
papers.abstract: We study finite-horizon rate-cost tradeoffs for general stochastic control systems, including nonlinear systems. Under an average control cost constraint, we show that the minimum expected communication rate lies within an additive logarithmic gap above the normalized directed information minimized over causal control policies. This establishes directed information as the operationally relevant quantity governing rate-limited control, extending its previously established roles in causal source coding and linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control to general nonlinear control systems.

papers.title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry
papers.authors: Luca Fanelli, Yilin Song, Ying Wang, Jiqiang Zheng, Ruihan Zhou
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations.
  Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schr\"odinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.

papers.title: Second-order geometry of optimal transport: cost identifiability and stability
papers.authors: Gabriel Peyr\'e, Clarice Poon, Oscar Tron
papers.abstract:
We study the optimal transport value as a functional of the ground cost. Although this functional is an infimum of linear functionals and is therefore polyhedral for finitely supported marginals, it develops genuine second-order geometry in the smooth continuous setting. Under twist, nondegeneracy, and regularity assumptions, we prove twice differentiability with respect to the cost in H\"older spaces, derive a variational formula for the Hessian, and characterize its null space. The resulting curvature is strict transverse to the cost perturbations that preserve the observed optimal plan.
  This structure yields identifiability and quantitative stability for inverse optimal transport. For bilinear costs $c_A(x,y)=-x^\top Ay$, a full spanning condition on the Hessians of the Kantorovich potential implies that every nonzero matrix compatible with a single optimal coupling is a positive multiple of the true matrix. We show that this condition can be attained by arbitrarily small compactly supported smooth perturbations of the transport potential that preserve the target marginal's support and density class. For $d\ge2$, uniquely optimal discrete plans and same-base elliptical models, including Gaussians, retain nontrivial degeneracies. Finally, we quantify the regularization bias and sampling error of entropic inverse optimal transport as the regularization parameter vanishes. Thus the second-order geometry of the forward transport problem provides a means towards identifiability, stability, and statistical cost recovery.

papers.title: Finite-Gap Solutions of the Pohlmeyer--Lund--Regge Equation and the Associated Lund-Regge Surfaces
papers.abstract: We develop a finite-gap construction for the Pohlmeyer-Lund-Regge (PLR) equation and the associated Lund-Regge surfaces. From the hyperelliptic spectral data we build a Baker-Akhiezer function and an SU(2)-frame, yielding an explicit theta-quotient formula for the PLR solution. We then derive criteria for s-periodicity and t-periodicity: under the stated theta-period assumptions, s-periodicity and t-periodicity are each equivalent to a critical-point condition for the corresponding normalized differential together with a phase condition at the reconstruction point. This provides a PLR analogue of the periodicity mechanism of Calini-Ivey.

papers.title: Hyper-Operations and Coherent Plasmas over $\mathbb{F}_1$
papers.abstract: The additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules (in the sense of Segal's $\Gamma$-sets) differs fundamentally from that of abelian groups: addition is encoded through a family of $n$-ary hyper-operations that are multivalued and need not satisfy classical associativity. We establish a \emph{law of generalized associativity} showing that, despite this failure of strict associativity, every $n$-ary sum is contained in the iterated hypersum associated with any partition of its inputs. This enables us to give a hyper-additive description on $\pi_0$ of Schwede's linearization functor $-\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_1} \mathbb{Z}: \mathbb{F}_1\mathbf{Mod} \to \mathbf{Ab}$ that universally strictifies the hyper-additive structure of $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules into classical abelian group addition. We then introduce coherent plasmas, whose algebraic structure encodes the coherence condition inherent in $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules. We construct fully faithful nerves for these structures and their finite-arity truncations, yielding a compatible tower of adjunctions, as well as a coherent Segal condition that characterizes the essential image. The levels of these nerves are represented by powerset plasmas $P_n$, which arise as algebraic realizations of representable $\Gamma$-sets, analogous to standard simplices in geometric realization.

papers.title: Acylindrical hyperbolicity of automorphism groups and property $R_\infty$ for generalized Higman groups
papers.abstract: We consider the Higman groups $H_k$ ($k\ge 4$) and their generalizations studied by Martin and Horbez--Huang. We prove that the automorphism groups of the Horbez--Huang groups on at least five generators, as well as those of Martin's $4$-generated Higman-like groups, are acylindrically hyperbolic. It follows that the groups themselves are acylindrically hyperbolic, admit infinite-dimensional spaces of automorphism-invariant homogeneous quasimorphisms, have infinite $2$-generated simple characteristic quotients, and satisfy property $R_\infty$. We also prove, using Delzant's lemma, a general criterion ensuring that an individual automorphism has infinite Reidemeister number: if $G$ is a group, $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, the group $\Gamma_\varphi=\langle\operatorname{Inn}(G),\varphi\rangle$ acts by isometries on a Gromov-hyperbolic space, and the restricted action of $\operatorname{Inn}(G)$ has two independent loxodromic elements, then $R(\varphi)=\infty$.

papers.title: Optimization and complexity of inertia-type bounds on the independence and chromatic numbers of graph powers
papers.authors: Aida Abiad, Stan van Hoesel, Valentin Michaux
papers.abstract:
The inertia bound, introduced by Cvetkovi\'c in 1971, is a fundamental result in spectral graph theory that provides an upper bound for the independence number of a graph in terms of spectral information about a weighted adjacency matrix of the graph. Recently, this bound has been extended to the so-called inertia-type bounds for estimating the independence and chromatic numbers of graph powers ($k$-independence number and distance-$k$ chromatic number of a graph). These bounds have recently found applications in coding theory and quantum information theory.
  The inertia-type bounds depend on the choice of a polynomial of degree $k$ and on the eigenvalues of the graph. Currently, optimizing these bounds requires solving several MILPs, which quickly becomes computationally demanding as the graph size or $k$ grows. This computational barrier is a major obstacle to the practical use of these bounds. Moreover, we have a limited theoretical understanding of their performance, even for small $k$. In this paper, we investigate their optimization and complexity. In particular, we improve the MILP formulations, reducing their computational burden and significantly decreasing the running time. Furthermore, we show that the optimization problems associated with the bounds are solvable in polynomial arithmetic time for every fixed $k$, given exact spectral input.

papers.title: Invariant metrics of model domains near pseudoconcave points
papers.abstract: We give precise estimates of some holomorphically invariant infinitesimal metrics near a pseudoconcave points in a wide family of ``model'' domains for that situation in $\mathbb C^2$. This extends to metrics (rather distances) the authors' previous results from arXiv:2503.19754 and also takes into account defining functions more general than just power functions.

papers.title: Exponential sums over singular binary quintics
papers.abstract: We give a characteristic-free explicit formula for exponential sums over singular binary quintic forms, based on the Waring decomposition of binary forms. This extends the method used in our previous work on the space of binary quartics to a non-coregular space.

papers.title: Nielsen coincidence theory of $(n,m)$-valued pairs of maps
papers.authors: Grzegorz Graff, P. Christopher Staecker, Alan \.Zeromski
papers.abstract:
We consider pairs of maps $(f,g)$, where $f$ is an $n$-valued map and
  $g$ is an $m$-valued map, defined on connected finite polyhedra.
  A point $x$ such that $f(x)\cap g(x)\neq \emptyset$ is called a coincidence point of $f$ and $g$.
  A useful device for studying coincidence points would be a Nielsen-type invariant which provides a lower bound for the number of coincidence points of all $(n, m)$-valued pairs of maps homotopic to $(f,g)$. The construction of such an invariant $N(f:g)$ was proposed in [J. Fixed Point Theory Appl. 14, 309--324 (2013)]. Unfortunately, this approach has some flaws. In this paper, we present a modified construction that yields a corrected form of the invariant, defined in terms of the intersection points of the graphs of $f$ and $g$. In the case of $(n, m)$-valued pairs of maps of the circle our invariant provides a sharp lower bound, which we precisely determine.

papers.title: Scalable Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Bidirectional Compression: Beyond Pessimistic Limits
papers.abstract: In centralized, distributed, and federated learning with stochastic gradients and $n$ workers, it was recently shown that it is infeasible to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point faster than $\tilde{\Omega}\left(\min\left\{\frac{d \kappa L \Delta}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h L \Delta}{\varepsilon} + \frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{n \varepsilon^2},\; \frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{h L \Delta}{\varepsilon}\right\}\right)$ seconds in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings under standard assumptions: $L$-smoothness, $\sigma^2$-bounded unbiased stochastic gradients, and lower boundedness of the function, i.e., $f(x) \geq f^*$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, where $\Delta = f(x^0) - f^*$, $h$ is the computation time, $\kappa$ is the communication speed between the workers and the server, and $d$ is the dimension of the iterates and gradients. This result is pessimistic since it does not allow a complexity in which both $\frac{d \kappa L \Delta}{\varepsilon}$ and $\frac{h \sigma^2 L \Delta}{\varepsilon^2}$ improve with $n$, even when using random sparsification techniques; moreover, this lower bound can be matched by either non-distributed SGD or vanilla Synchronous SGD, which reduces the impact of recent progress in the design of compression-based methods. In this work, we challenge this limitation and propose new compressed methods, Inkheart SGD and M4, and show that under an additional structural assumption, which is necessary due to the lower bound and which does not restrict the class of considered problems, we achieve new state-of-the-art time complexities that break this pessimistic barrier and allow scaling with the number of workers $n$.

papers.title: Galerkin Approximation of the Fractional Sobolev Constant
papers.abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the discrete optimal constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality in dimension $N\geq 1$, with fractional exponent $s\in (0,\min\{1,N/2\})$. The convergence rates that we establish take place for the Galerkin approximation with piecewise linear elements, when the problem is posed in the unit ball, for which we employ a quasi-uniform and regular mesh. Since the infimum defining the fractional Sobolev constant is not attained on bounded domains, these estimates quantify how far a piecewise affine mesh of size $h$ can resolve the concentration of the optimizers: the discrete minimizers are close to bubbles concentrated at the scale $h^{2(2-s)/(N+4(1-s))}$, and the energy gap is exactly of order $h^{2(2-s)(N-2s)/(N+4(1-s))}$.

papers.title: A nonlinear version of the $\alpha$-Kakutani equidistribution problem
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend results of Kakutani; Adler and Flatto; Smilansky; Pollicott and Sewell on the equidistribution of endpoints generated by interval-splitting procedures. We study a nonlinear version of the problem generated by a finite or countable family of $\mathcal{C}^{1+ \varepsilon}$ contractions and prove Lebesgue equidistribution under suitable nonlattice and thermodynamic regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network
papers.abstract: In this work we consider a dynamical cellular communication network in which mobile base stations (BSs) are modeled as a homogeneous Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Each base station moves at a constant speed in a random direction. A typical user connects to the nearest base station and it experiences variable signal and interference powers depending on the distance of all the stations. Along the motion of the stations, the user swaps its serving station, and such an event is called a {\em handover}. We are interested in the performance evaluation of the system under some classical and tropical metrics of interest at different time of events, inducing handovers, maximal proximity of serving station, nearest interferer at closest or farthest distance with respect to the user or at any typical time epoch. The main results of the paper are closed or integral form expressions for the basic metrics of interest, in particular coverage probability and Shannon rate at these epochs. We can make an analogy with ``seasons'' based on the fluctuations of signal and interference power. Strong or mild signal or interference power correspond to different seasons of Shannon rate along the evolution of the system. We also provide a complete comparison study of the metrics at interest at these epochs. We also provide a recipe to lift our results for a 3D wireless communication model for UAVs and HAPS.

papers.title: Motion-Enabled Tomography of Gaussian-Mixture Particles under Unknown Rigid-Body Motion with Parabolic Trajectories
papers.authors: Daniel Burrows, Ozan \"Oktem, Can Evren Yarman
papers.abstract: Reconstructing objects with unknown position and/or orientation arises in applications spanning geology to cryo-ET. When the relative motion between the object and the sensing apparatus provides sufficient angular coverage, computerized tomography offers a powerful means of reconstruction. For such scenarios, we propose a parametric spatiotemporal model applied to Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), in which each constituent Gaussian is parameterized by its own angular velocity, parabolic trajectory, and morphology. GMM are a suitable means of reconstruction because they (i) admit accurate approximations in object space and (ii) have a closed form expression under the ray transform; enabling efficient forward predictions and analysis in data space. By decoupling the projectile motion from the rotation and morphology, the full optimization problem can be reduced to two lower-dimensional sub-problems that are easier to optimize. The corresponding algorithm --- which is applicable to objects in Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension --- is validated on an extensive set of noisy 2D simulations. Its performance provides promise for further experimentation in more complex scenarios, such as higher dimensions, objects with deformable body mechanics, and on physical datasets.

papers.title: Solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere Equations with Low Codimensional singularities
papers.abstract: We construct solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere equations whose Monge-Amp\`ere measures contain singular components supported on low codimensional sets. We also study the regularity of such solutions. To motivate our construction, we present examples arising from optimal transport where the potential of optimal transport maps satisfy Monge-Amp\`ere equations similar to the ones we study.

papers.title: Isotropy Groups of $\sigma$-Derivations on the Quantum Plane
papers.abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal A_q=\Bbbk_q[x,y]$ be the quantum plane, with $q\in\Bbbk^\ast\setminus\{1\}$. For a fixed automorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathcal A_q$, we study $\sigma$-derivations and their isotropy groups under the conjugation action of the centralizer of $\sigma$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal A_q)$. For $q\neq\pm1$, we use Jordan's classification of skew derivations for toric automorphisms, which generalizes the description of Almulhem and Brzezi\'nski for the quantum plane, to describe these groups by character equations on the torus $(\Bbbk^\ast)^2$, obtaining an arithmetic criterion for finiteness. In this case, we also prove that, for every fixed $\sigma$, every finite subgroup of the torus occurs, up to isomorphism, as the isotropy group of a $\sigma$-derivation, including when $q$ is a root of unity. For $q=-1$, we classify the $\sigma$-derivations for both toric and flip automorphisms $\sigma$ and describe their isotropy groups. In particular, we explicitly determine the isotropy groups of ordinary derivations of $\mathcal A_{-1}$.

papers.title: The Closure of LCD-to-GI Reductions via Generalized Inner Products
papers.abstract: The Permutation Equivalence Problem (PEP) for linear complementary dual (LCD) codes reduces to Graph Isomorphism (GI) through the orthogonal projector onto the code, but this requires a trivial hull. We ask whether the reduction extends when the standard inner product is replaced by a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form \(M\). We make precise what it means for \(M\) to yield a valid reduction to GI and prove that, for length \(n \geq 3\) and every field size, this holds if and only if \(M\) is permutation-invariant. The reduction then reaches, beyond LCD codes, a class of codes with one-dimensional hull: exactly those whose hull is spanned by a vector with nonzero coordinate sum. We count these codes exactly; for odd \(q\), asymptotically the method covers a fraction \(\prod_{i \geq 2}(1+q^{-i})^{-1}\) of all codes, \(1 + q^{-1}\) times the fraction of LCD codes. A polynomial-time reduction algorithm is given.

papers.title: Stability of optimal transport maps and second variation of the 2-Monge-Kantorovich distance
papers.authors: F. -U. Caja-Lopez, Matias G. Delgadino, Jun Kitagawa
papers.abstract: We establish several quantitative stability estimates for optimal transport maps between non-degenerate densities on uniformly convex domains for the quadratic cost. Under H\"older regularity assumptions, we prove Lipschitz $L^{2}$ (respectively $C^{0,\alpha}$) stability estimates for optimal transport maps in terms of the $2$-Monge--Kantorovich distance (respectively $L^{p}$ distances) between pairs of source and target densities. When the continuity assumption is removed, we obtain a Lipschitz $L^{2}$ stability estimate for the Brenier potentials in terms of the $L^{2}$ distance between the source and target densities. The proofs rely on a precise characterization of the linear response of the Brenier potential along smooth interpolations of the data, obtained by linearizing the Monge--Amp\`ere equation in divergence form. As a further application of this approach, we derive an explicit formula for the second variation of the quadratic Monge--Kantorovich distance.

papers.title: An Infeasible Method with Feasibility Safeguard for Nonsmooth Composite Optimization Over Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study nonsmooth composite optimization over embedded submanifolds defined by nonlinear equality constraints. We propose a feasibility-safeguarded inexact proximal linearized method whose iterations require neither projection nor retraction onto the manifold. A computable smooth-dual residual certifies the approximate tangential step and controls the errors in both tangency and composite linearization consistency. The step is followed by a normal correction evaluated at the displaced trial point. To coordinate the resulting optimality and feasibility errors, a nonmonotone backtracking procedure reduces the tangential stepsize faster than the normal stepsize and accepts only corrected points within a prescribed constraint-violation region. Under the stated regularity and level-boundedness assumptions, we establish a uniform backtracking bound, positive lower bounds on the accepted stepsizes, boundedness of the primal and multiplier sequences, stationarity of all cluster points, and an $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ outer iteration complexity bound. The analysis does not assume compactness of the manifold or a separate global distance-to-manifold error bound. For a specified parameter regime guaranteeing full tangential steps, a KL assumption on an auxiliary function yields full-sequence convergence. Numerical experiments on sparse principal component analysis and sparse spectral clustering illustrate the performance of the method.

papers.title: On the complexity of two-stage stochastic linear optimization with small second stage
papers.abstract: Two-stage stochastic linear optimization is known to be #P-hard when all involved random variables are independently and uniformly distributed over intervals, even with fixed recourse. We show that this problem is in fact #P-hard in the strong sense. More surprisingly, #P-hardness persists even when the random vector is one-dimensional, i.e., uniformly distributed over a single interval. To obtain this result, we show that computing the area of a two-dimensional polytope given by a compact extended formulation is #P-hard. Furthermore, for a problem in standard form, we prove strong #P-hardness in case the number of second-stage constraints is fixed, while fixing the number of second-stage variables leads to a weakly #P-hard problem. Finally, if both the dimension of the random vector and the number of second-stage constraints are fixed, the problem turns out to be tractable.

papers.title: Computing statistical solutions of a Mach 2000 astrophysical jet
papers.abstract: The multi-dimensional compressible Euler equations admit non-unique entropy solutions in turbulent regimes, and extreme-Mach astrophysical flows are a natural setting in which this breakdown of deterministic well-posedness becomes computationally visible. We compute statistical solutions of a Mach~2000 astrophysical jet, defined as the pushforward of an initial probability measure through a vectorial lattice Boltzmann method, by Monte Carlo sampling with $M=1000$ realizations on grids of up to $12.8$ million cells. Under mesh refinement the individual realizations diverge pathwise, while the statistical solution converges: Wasserstein distances of the one- and two-point marginals, the ensemble mean, and the ensemble standard deviation all exhibit stable positive convergence rates. A spatially resolved analysis along the jet axis traces this dichotomy to the structure of the one-point laws, which are numerically Dirac in the undisturbed core, skewed in the sheared turbulent regions, and intermittent two-state mixtures at the random leading front. We conclude that the computed statistical solution is non-Dirac and remains stable in the extreme compressible regime, in which no strong solution is expected to exist.

papers.title: Resonant Microstructures as Dirac-type Sources for Acoustic Wave Control
papers.abstract: We study finite-time acoustic wave tracking using effective interior Dirac-type actuators generated by clusters of subwavelength resonant bubbles driven from exterior transducers. Starting from a time-domain point-interaction approximation, the full scattering problem is reduced to a finite-dimensional delayed system of interacting retarded monopoles. After localization to a bounded observation domain, we formulate the tracking problem on a prescribed finite-dimensional Dirichlet spectral subspace. At the ideal level, a full-rank spatial coupling condition yields exact tracking of arbitrary sufficiently smooth compatible trajectories in this subspace by interior point sources. These ideal actuators are realized using small, high-contrast bubbles, whose Laplace-domain transfer operator encodes the Minnaert resonances and collective attenuation. The principal mode of each cluster is isolated by the Perron--Frobenius structure and the intra-cluster spectral gap. Clusters tuned to the same band are then treated as a collective resonant block. The selected Dirichlet bands are matched with the corresponding Minnaert bands. For prescribed slowly time-modulated resonant pressure profiles, with sufficiently flat initialization, we construct causal exterior controls and obtain a quantitative tracking estimate on every fixed time interval $[0,T]$. In contrast, on frequency ranges uniformly separated from the Minnaert resonances, the actuator gain is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the corresponding realization cost is asymptotically unbounded as $\varepsilon \ll 1$, $\varepsilon$ being the maximum radius of the bubbles. Thus the Minnaert resonances convert accessible exterior excitations into robust effective interior controls.

papers.title: Topological and Diophantine properties of lattice subset projections
papers.abstract: This paper uses the Baire category theorem, the Riemannian manifold structure of Grassmannians, and the Khintchine Groshev theorem in Diophantine analysis, to relate properties of lattice subsets to those of associated subset of a Grassmannian.

papers.title: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
papers.authors: Ali Mohammadian, Sina Rezaie Zareie, Behruz Tayfeh-Rezaie
papers.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices whose activation eventually spreads to all vertices of $G$. Let \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\) be the odd graph and the bipartite odd graph, respectively, both defined on a ground set of size \(2k+1\). In this article, among other results, we prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The former result confirms a conjecture posed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.

papers.title: Local increment inference for time-inhomogeneous drift in Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for deterministic drifts in Gaussian process models under high-frequency observations over an expanding time horizon. Using a least squares-type contrast based on first-order increments, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality under conditions on drift accumulation and increment dependence.A key feature is that the convergence rate is determined jointly by the deterministic signal and the full covariance structure of the weighted Gaussian increments, rather than by local noise roughness alone.For power and fixed-frequency periodic drifts under Gaussian and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck covariance kernels, we derive explicit convergence rates and limiting variances, revealing distinct regimes depending on the drift structure and, for periodic drifts, the noise spectrum. These results clarify the respective roles of sampling frequency and observation horizon.

papers.title: On special perfect polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$
papers.abstract: We give some necessary conditions satisfied by special perfect polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

papers.title: Bridging Scales: Asymptotic Analysis and AI-Assisted Formalization
papers.abstract: Asymptotic analysis is one of the classical tools for bridging models across scales. Behind many such derivations lies a common symbolic structure: an ansatz, a substitution, an order-by-order matching procedure, and the extraction of effective equations or interface conditions. This article revisits that structure through two representative bridges: the kinetic-to-fluid limit, illustrated by radiative transfer with interface layers and by neural-network approximations of Boltzmann equations, and the quantum-to-classical limit, illustrated by the Frozen Gaussian Approximation and its Dirac extension. We then explain why such derivations are natural candidates for AI-assisted formalization: their recurring symbolic structures can be organized, verified, and reused. In this sense, a carefully structured expository paper may serve not only as a review, but also as a mathematical seed for future AI-assisted environments.

papers.title: On the class-breadth conjecture for $p$-groups
papers.abstract: The class-breadth conjecture of Leedham-Green, Neumann and Wiegold states that the nilpotency class of any $p$-group is at most $b(G) + 1$, where $\displaystyle{b(G) = \max_{g\in G}\log_p[G:Z_G(g)]}$ denotes the breadth of a group $G$. While several counter-examples to this conjecture have been found for $p = 2$, it is still open in general for $p > 2$. This article is dedicated to the general case $p > 2$ of the conjecture.

papers.title: A Betchov-Type Hydrodynamic Formulation of the Ivancevic Option-Pricing Equation
papers.abstract: We show that, under constant-coefficient assumptions, the Ivancevic option-pricing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation admits a Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation analogous to the one arising in the context of the vortex filament equation. Along with this structural correspondence, known Ivancevic solutions are interpreted in terms of density--velocity variables. As an illustration of the financial interpretation, we compare the normalized one-soliton density with the Black--Scholes risk-neutral density, obtaining an explicit relation between the Ivancevic coefficient ratio and standard market quantities. We further show that the probability current can be reconstructed from the temporal evolution of the density and demonstrate this reconstruction for an interacting two-soliton solution. Together, these results illustrate how the Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation can be used to describe the evolution and transport of the Ivancevic density, while establishing a coefficient-explicit bridge between nonlinear wave models in mathematical finance and geometric fluid mechanics.

papers.title: Service-Induced Congestion in Memory-Constrained LLM Serving
papers.authors: Ruicheng Ao, Jing Dong, Gan Luo, David Simchi-Levi
papers.abstract: In large language model (LLM) serving, each request accumulates persistent graphics processing unit (GPU) memory during service as its key-value cache grows with every generated token. Under high concurrency, aggregate memory usage therefore increases endogenously over time: the service process itself creates future capacity pressure. When memory capacity is exceeded, systems evict active requests, discarding cached state and restarting them later, which wastes computation and reduces throughput. We develop a discrete-time dynamical model of memory-constrained LLM inference that captures admission, memory growth, and eviction under continuous batching. In the saturated-input regime, the system admits both eviction-free fixed points and limit cycles with evictions. For homogeneous workloads, we show that the eviction-free equilibrium is unstable and that, except for a Lebesgue-measure-zero exact-capture set, the system converges to a unique worst-case limit cycle that is asymptotically stable outside this exceptional set, with throughput losses as large as 50%. For heterogeneous workloads, we prove a stability criterion in the two-class common-input setting and explain how the survival-polynomial mechanism generalizes to multiple classes and heterogeneous-input lengths. Under an input-dominated scaling regime, coprime decoding lengths stabilize the eviction-free equilibrium, while non-coprime lengths create synchronized modes that drive instability. These results characterize when workload heterogeneity desynchronizes completions and helps stabilize memory-constrained serving. More broadly, we identify service-induced congestion as a structural instability mechanism and derive scheduling design principles for sustaining high throughput.

papers.title: The quantitative isoperimetric inequality: A calibration argument
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of the quantitative isoperimetric inequality. Our argument is based on a notion of quantitative calibrations which induce a natural distance controlling both the Fraenkel asymmetry and the tilt excess. The proof of our key result which can be viewed as a nonlinear, geometric version of Fuglede's result in $BV$ is direct and self-contained. In particular, we do not make any use of regularity theory for almost minimizers.

papers.title: Bregman-projected mirror methods for regularized stationary mean-field games
papers.authors: Hussain Al Abdulaziz, Yuri Ashrafyan, Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a Bregman-projected mirror iteration for low-order regularizations of stationary mean-field game (MFG) systems in their natural Banach space setting. For separable Hamiltonians of the form $H(x,p,m)=H_0(x,p)-g(m)$, with quadratic or super-quadratic Hamiltonian growth and linear or super-linear density couplings, we formulate a low-order $\bar\gamma$-Laplacian regularization of the stationary MFG system as a variational inequality on $L^{\bar\beta}(\mathbb T^d)\times W^{1,\bar\gamma}(\mathbb T^d)$. To approximate solutions of this regularized variational inequality, we introduce a Bregman geometry matched to the mixed Lebesgue-Sobolev exponents of the problem and analyze the exact constrained one-step mirror iteration and a frozen two-step variant. Under quantitative monotonicity of the coupling, both exact iterations converge strongly to the unique solution of the regularized variational inequality for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, under natural summability conditions on the step sizes. Along weakly convergent vanishing-regularization sequences, we also prove strong convergence in the full product space. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions show first-order accuracy on manufactured solutions and weak dependence of outer iteration counts on the tested grids. At matched effective step sizes, the frozen two-step and one-step implementations agree up to inner-solve accuracy, while the latter requires fewer mirror solves.

papers.title: Level totients for integer mosaics
papers.authors: The Anh Dao, Tim Kasian, Mostafa Mirabi
papers.abstract:
We study a level analog of Euler's totient function for integer mosaics. Let $P_i(n)$ be the set of primes appearing in the first $i$ levels of the mosaic of $n$, and let $\varphi_i(n)$ count the integers $m\leq n$ for which $P_i(m)\cap P_i(n)=\varnothing$. We prove a M\"obius divisor-sum formula for $\varphi_i(n)$ and reduce it to a sum over a set $\mathcal{V}_{i,S}$ of powerful integers. If $S\neq\varnothing$, $i\geq 2$, and $q=\min S$, then \[
  |\mathcal{V}_{i,S}\cap[1,x]|\sim C_{i,S}x^{1/q}, \] with $C_{i,S}$ an explicit positive Euler-product constant. For fixed $S$, the density $\delta_i(S)$ of integers whose first $i$ levels avoid $S$ exists and has an Euler product; for nonempty $S$, $i\ge2$, and $q=\min S$, the number of such integers up to $N$ is $\delta_i(S)N+O_{i,S}(N^{1/q})$. Taking $S=P_i(n)$ gives \[ \frac{\varphi_i(n)}{n}=\delta_i(P_i(n))+O_\varepsilon(n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}) \] uniformly in $n$.

papers.title: From smooth to discontinuous kernels: a variance transfer principle for hyperuniform processes
papers.abstract: We give a transfer principle for the fluctuations of linear statistics of finite particle systems around Lebesgue measure: if for a smooth kernel the variance decays polynomially with some exponent a compared to independent (non-interacting) particles, then the number variance over balls centred at almost every point decays with exponent min(1,a) times a log term if a=1, over a possibly reduced range of scales for non-periodic systems. We apply this principle to eigenvalues of random N*N Girko matrices, leveraging results of Cipolloni et al., and obtain the optimal perimeter-like number variance, on the microscopic and some mesoscopic scales range, after local averaging. We also apply the results to Coulomb gases, by transferring the results of Serfaty: we prove that 2D-Coulomb gases are 2-hyperuniform, i.e. they have surface order number variance, which is optimal, and that 3D Coulomb gases are 1-hyperuniform. In 2D, it allows to prove finite Coulomb energy and Wasserstein distance to Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: \'Etale Fundamental Groups: a geometric and topological approach to fundamental groups in algebraic geometry
papers.abstract: This thesis explores the notion of fundamental groups across three mathematical settings. We begin with the classical topological theory of covering spaces, highlighting its structural analogy with Galois theory. We then follow Grothendieck in transporting these ideas to algebraic geometry. The inadequacy of the Zariski topology motivates the \'etale topology, from which the \'etale fundamental group is constructed and compared to its topological counterpart via transcendental methods. Finally, we linearise the theory through Tannakian duality, where fundamental groups are recovered as automorphism groups of fibre functors on certain monoidal categories, a framework broad enough to encompass \'etale, topological, and motivic Galois groups alike.

papers.title: Weak and Strong Convergence of an Implicit Iteration for Hemi-Contractive Semigroups in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: We study an implicit iteration for approximating common fixed points of strongly continuous semigroups on closed convex subsets of real Banach spaces. Under a stepwise Lipschitz restriction and hemi-contractivity relative to the common fixed point set, we establish well-definedness and Fej% \'{e}r monotonicity of the iteration. In reflexive Banach spaces satisfying Opial's condition, we obtain a sufficient condition for weak convergence based on a normalized residual estimate, uniform continuity at zero along the generated sequence, and demiclosedness at fixed positive times. In general real Banach spaces, we prove strong convergence under a time-dependent directional contraction condition and a divergence condition coupling the iteration weights with the contraction strength. A linear example shows that vanishing time steps and a divergent sum of iteration weights alone do not ensure convergence to a common fixed point. A nonlinear planar evolution semigroup illustrates the applicability of the strong convergence theorem beyond the nonexpansive class.

papers.title: Three-Body Earth-Moon Transfers with Different Departure/Arrival Orbital Altitudes: New Phenomenon and Diffusion Model-Augmented Construction
papers.authors: Shuyue Fu, Wenxuan Zhang, Di Wu, Shengping Gong, Peng Shi
papers.abstract: Construction of Earth-Moon transfers is the basis of missions to explore the Moon and cislunar space.
