That condition fails for only four $b$ with $|b|\le3000$, and at one of them, $b=3$, the conclusion itself fails. In the order $\mathbb{Z}[\eta_b]$ generated by $\eta_b$, by contrast, $\eta_b$ is the fundamental unit for every $b$, so these exceptions are a phenomenon of the maximal order. As an application we construct infinitely many biquadratic fields whose $3$-class field tower has length greater than $1$.

papers.title: Mutual Information Constrained Chernoff Bottleneck
papers.abstract: The classical information bottleneck (IB) measures the relevance of a representation $U$ of $X$ to a target $Y$ by $I(U;Y)$, which does not directly characterize the error of downstream decisions. For a binary hypothesis $Y$ inferred from many separately encoded observations, the optimal error exponent is the Chernoff information between the two conditional distributions of $U$ given $Y$. We study the mutual information constrained Chernoff bottleneck, which seeks an encoder that maximizes this Chernoff information subject to a rate constraint $I(U;X) \leq R$. We show that its optimal value $C(R)$ increases strictly up to $R = H(V)$, where $V$ merges the symbols of $X$ with equal likelihood ratio, remains at the uncompressed exponent beyond, and, unlike the IB curve, need not be concave. We further show that $k+1$ outputs suffice to attain $C(R)$, where $k$ is the cardinality of $V$. We propose an alternating algorithm that updates the encoder via a generalized Blahut--Arimoto algorithm and the Chernoff parameter $s$ via a nonlinear equation, and prove that its iterates remain feasible, with nondecreasing and convergent Chernoff information. Comparing with the classical IB for $n$ samples, we show that, whenever the two objectives disagree, the IB encoder has the smaller equivocation $H(Y|U^{n})$ at $n = 1$, whereas the Chernoff bottleneck has the smaller error probability and equivocation for all large $n$. Numerical experiments confirm the theory, and on real topic-detection data from the 20 Newsgroups corpus, compressing each word to only $17\%$ of its entropy retains $90\%$ of the error exponent and nearly the accuracy of the uncompressed classifier.

papers.title: Reconsidering the Vacuum Energy of a Massive Scalar Field in a Spherical Cavity
papers.abstract: We reconsider the vacuum (Casimir) energy of a massive scalar field obeying Dirichlet boundary conditions inside a spherical cavity. Using zeta-function regularization, we carefully recalculate the analytic part of the zeta function via the uniform asymptotic expansion of the modified Bessel functions. We correct a sign error present in an earlier calculation (PR D56 (1997) 4896) that affected the large-mass behavior. The renormalized vacuum energy is shown to vanish for large mass, as required on physical grounds. Numerical results reveal that the energy changes sign several times as a function of the cavity radius.

papers.title: On a question of Jones on tracelike vectors, cusp forms, and von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: Using the theory of von Neumann algebras, Vaughan Jones showed abstractly that there is a bridge between holomorphic cusp forms and random matrices. This bridge is supplied by a distinguished function he called a {\it tracelike vector}. He posed the following problem: construct a tracelike vector to make this bridge explicit. We carry out Jones' vision for the full modular group. We construct holomorphic tracelike vectors for every finite-covolume Fuchsian group throughout the permissible Bergman range. For the modular group at the critical parameter $s=13$, we use the resulting unit tracelike vector to assign explicit group coefficients to cusp form multiplication operators, and form positive finite random matrices from a shared Haar-distributed unitary matrix. Almost surely, their normalised traces recover all joint operator moments, first as the matrix size tends to infinity, and then as the group-word cutoff tends to infinity. We also identify the limiting mixed second moment with a series of Petersson norms that involve Maass-Shimura operators of cusp forms. The exact nature of our use of AI is detailed in the introduction.

papers.title: Spectra of Random Polynomial Matrices: the Petaloid Law
papers.abstract:
We study the distribution of the zeros of $\det P_N(z)$ where $P_N(z)$ is a random monic polynomial matrix, i.e., $P_N(z)=z^dI-\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}A_{j,N}z^j$ for possibly coupled random matrices $A_{j,N}$, scaled to have entrywise variance $O(1/N)$. We provide general conditions under which this distribution almost-surely weakly converges as $N\to\infty$ to a deterministic measure, depending on just the variance and covariance of the entries of the $A_j$.
  This generalizes the circular, elliptic, and semicircle laws, which concern the special case of this question where $d=1$. Unlike those classical laws, these measures can combine nonuniform two-dimensional densities with singular components supported on curves, producing a variety of petal-shaped regions, inspiring our name ``the petaloid law''. We give explicit formulas for the limiting densities and supports. Under a Gaussianity assumption, we also show that there are almost surely no eigenvalues outside small neighborhoods of the limiting support.

papers.title: Gradient-Only Online Convex Optimization with a Single Quadratic Leader
papers.abstract: We study online convex optimization on a bounded Euclidean domain when the learner receives only one subgradient at its prediction and knows neither the horizon, a gradient bound, nor the losses' strong-convexity parameters. We present a scale-invariant algorithm that couples projected adaptive gradient descent to one cone-constrained quadratic leader through a positive wealth process. The algorithm maintains $O(d)$ state, without a learning-rate grid or restarts. For a domain of diameter at most $D$, it guarantees regret at most $\sqrt{2}D(\sum_t\|\widehat g_t\|^2)^{1/2}+2D\max_t\|\widehat g_t\|$, with no logarithmic factor. A simultaneous quadratic-distance bound yields explicit improvements for unknown strong convexity, including a refinement governed by jumps in the observed gradient scale. For varying per-round curvature, the bound depends on the total shortfall below a reference level selected in hindsight. The proof uses a clipping-compatible surrogate and a potential involving the quadratic minimum, log wealth, and two scalar curvature statistics. The resulting strongly convex bound is not uniform at the classical logarithmic rate over all curvature-to-gradient ratios; the exact parameter dependence is stated. The contribution is a single-leader construction and its analysis, within an established literature on universal and scale-free online learning.

papers.title: Sharp Fresh-Gradient Complexity of Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We characterize the fresh-gradient oracle complexity of smooth nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, with matching upper and lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. Let $\Phi(x)=\max_y f(x,y)$, where $f$ is jointly $L$-smooth and $\mu$-strongly concave in $y$ on unconstrained Euclidean domains, and set $\kappa=L/\mu$. Each query returns a fresh unbiased joint gradient with conditional variance at most $\sigma^2$. Given initial primal gap at most $\Delta$ and dual residual $\|\nabla_y f(x_0,y_0)\|\le G$, the fixed-budget complexity of finding $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|\le\epsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$ is $\widetilde{\Theta}(\sqrt{\kappa}L\Delta/\epsilon^2+\kappa L\Delta\sigma^2/\epsilon^4+\kappa^2\sigma^2/\epsilon^2+\sqrt{\kappa}\log_+(G/(\epsilon\sqrt{\kappa})))$, where $\log_+u=\log\max\{1,u\}$. This characterization holds when $\kappa$ and $L\Delta/\epsilon^2$ exceed universal constants, uniformly over finite dimensions, and the suppressed logarithms are independent of $G$. It establishes the necessity of linear condition-number dependence in the global stochastic cost and identifies a separate statistical refinement cost. A proximal method separates coarse primal progress from one final refinement, while the lower bounds apply to arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms. Dual initialization contributes only an additive logarithmic cost, yet removing its control eliminates every finite dimension-free complexity bound, even with exact gradients.

papers.title: Matching Lower Bounds for Randomized First-Order Methods in Hessian-Lipschitz Nonconvex Optimization
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish a randomized first-order lower bound for finding an $\epsilon$-stationary point, $\|\nabla f(x)\|\le \epsilon$, of a nonconvex function with initial gap at most $\Delta$, $L_1$-Lipschitz gradient, and $L_2$-Lipschitz Hessian. Each oracle call returns the exact function value and gradient. Let $Q_{\mathrm{rand},\mathrm{FO}}^{\infty}(\epsilon;\Delta,L_1,L_2)$ denote the minimax number of calls, maximized over finite dimensions, for arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms with per-instance success probability at least $2/3$. In the regime $\epsilon\lesssim L_1^2/L_2$ and $\Delta L_2^{1/2}\epsilon^{-3/2}\gtrsim 1$, we prove $ Q_{\mathrm{rand},\mathrm{FO}}^{\infty}(\epsilon;\Delta,L_1,L_2) \ge c\,\Delta L_1^{1/2}L_2^{1/4}\epsilon^{-7/4}, $ where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. This matches the deterministic restarted accelerated-gradient upper bound of Li and Lin (2023) and extends the sharp deterministic lower bound of Zhou (2026) to unrestricted randomized algorithms. Thus, randomization does not improve the high-dimensional worst-case query rate. The construction keeps quadratic curvature visible while revealing the forcing directions sequentially. Large eigenspaces limit preprocessing, and a scheduled-disclosure coupling makes each fresh direction incur a separate cost.

papers.title: Sharp High-Probability Statistical Rates for Heavy-Tailed Nonsmooth Convex Optimization
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish sharp high-probability statistical rates for nonsmooth stochastic convex optimization under heavy-tailed noise, closing the confidence-dependence gap in both general convex and strongly convex settings. We consider composite objectives with a Lipschitz convex loss and a known proximal regularizer, accessed through fresh unbiased stochastic subgradients. The centered noise has conditional norm and directional $p$th moments bounded by $L^p$ and $s^p$, respectively, where $1<p\le2$ and $0<s\le L$. For $T$ oracle calls and failure probability $0<\delta<1/10$, set $q=1-1/p$, $\ell=\log(3/\delta)$, and $A=s(L^2/s^2)^q$. With initial distance bound $D$, the minimax objective error is $\Theta(D(A+s\ell^q)/T^q)$ in the nonsaturated statistical regime. For a $\mu$-strongly convex regularizer, the corresponding quadratic-regime rate is $\Theta((A^2+s^2\ell^{2q})/(\mu T^{2q}))$. These rates require domination of the deterministic and finite-variance terms; matching lower bounds require $d\ge\lceil L^2/s^2\rceil$, while the upper bounds hold in every finite dimension. The new upper bounds attain known statistical lower-bound orders, replacing the previous confidence coefficient $s^{1/p}L^{1-1/p}$ by $s$, and its square by $s^2$ under strong convexity. The key is an online inequality that separates directional fluctuations from the total second moment created by rejection sampling. Localization preserves this separation under strong convexity without additional horizon logarithms. The results characterize oracle complexity with unrestricted internal computation.

papers.title: Joint Lower Bounds for Zeroth-Order Nonconvex Optimization on Euclidean Balls
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We prove a joint stochastic zeroth-order lower bound for Goldstein stationarity on a Euclidean query ball, even when the ball is guaranteed to contain a stationary point. In dimension $d$, let $f=\mathbb{E}[F(\cdot;\xi)]$, assume $\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Lip}(F(\cdot;\xi))^2]\le L_0^2$, and bound the initial objective gap over the ball by $\Delta$. For neighborhood radius $\delta>0$ and residual tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, our smooth hard family requires $\Omega(dL_0^2\Delta/(\delta\varepsilon^3))$ scalar evaluations for success probability $1/2$, against randomized adaptive algorithms that may retain and repeatedly query each sampled function. The result holds for $\varepsilon\le cL_0$, $\Delta\ge C\delta\varepsilon$, and $d\ge C[1+\log(2+\Delta L_0^2/(\delta\varepsilon^3))]$, on a constructed ball of radius $\Theta(\Delta/\varepsilon)$. A sequence of localized regions forces repeated direction estimation, and an adaptive Gaussian posterior argument controls sample reuse. The result establishes a joint dimension and accuracy obstruction on solvable bounded-domain instances. The gap is local to the query ball; a matching minimax characterization at a common radius and the corresponding unrestricted global-gap lower bound remain open here.

papers.title: Sharp Minimax Rates for Highly Smooth Strongly Convex Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We determine the minimax dimension dependence of noisy zeroth-order optimization for globally strongly convex functions with higher-order smoothness in multilinear operator norm. Each query returns one function value with fresh independent Gaussian noise. For dimension $d$, query budget $T$, and any fixed finite smoothness order $\beta>2$, the minimax expected objective error satisfies $\mathcal{E}_{\beta}(T,d)=\Theta_{\beta}\left(\min\left\{1,(d^2/T)^{(\beta-1)/\beta}\right\}\right)$, with dimension-independent strong-convexity, gradient-smoothness, higher-order-smoothness, noise, and minimizer-radius bounds. Thus, for sufficiently small target error $\varepsilon$, the necessary and sufficient number of noisy values is $\Theta_{\beta}(d^2\varepsilon^{-\beta/(\beta-1)})$, with no logarithmic loss. The new lower bound matches the dimension and budget dependence of the upper bound of Akhavan et al. (2024), and holds for arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms with unrestricted query points. Its key step localizes a normalized hypercube with one radial cutoff: a query can emphasize one hidden coordinate, but the aggregate information about all coordinates remains small. A self-contained multiscale spherical estimator attains the matching upper bound by cancelling lower-order bias terms. Constants in the rates depend only on the fixed smoothness order under the stated normalization.

papers.title: Watkins's conjecture holds for all infinite groups
papers.abstract: We prove that at every infinite cardinality, every group which is neither abelian of exponent greater than two nor generalized dicyclic admits a graphical regular representation, settling the infinite-group part of Watkins's conjecture. We also determine the Cayley index of every infinite group: it is $1$, $2$, or $8$, according to its algebraic type, and in every case the index is attained by a connected Cayley graph. For every infinite group $G$ of cardinality $\kappa$, we construct $2^\kappa$ pairwise nonisomorphic Cayley graphs with exactly the unavoidable inverse-pair symmetries, diameter two, and $\kappa$ common neighbors at every distinct pair. The principal tool recovers a continuous ordinal hierarchy from an alternating adjacency baseline with bounded-degree errors: robust finite patterns identify the initial classes, successive twin quotients recover the layers, and their finite exception packets determine the translation action. The reconstruction applies without a group action and is stable under additional layerwise bounded-degree edits. Further results give closed Cantor-cube families with prescribed finite data in the regular cases, sharp cofinality-dependent graph properties, and optimal three-valued shortest-path metrics.

papers.title: Parabolic Monge-Amp\`ere equations on a family of Calabi-Yau manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform $L^\infty$-estimate for the parabolic Monge--Amp\`ere equation under uniform H\"ormander-Tian type estimates with respect to the initial and prescribed measures. We apply this estimate to rescaled K\"ahler--Ricci flows on a family of polarized Calabi--Yau manifolds over the punctured disk. An interpolation argument gives uniform H\"ormander-Tian type estimates along the flows. We also establish uniform diameter bounds and Gromov--Hausdorff precompactness for this family of flows. In particular, we obtain an alternative proof of the diameter estimate by Li-Tosatti.

papers.title: An elliptic Calabi-Yau threefold of Mordell-Weil rank twelve
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi-Yau threefold with a flat elliptic fibration of Mordell-Weil rank twelve and Hodge numbers $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(25,1)$. The construction starts from the Kummer surfaces associated with the products of a fixed elliptic curve and the level-four modular family. The threefold is birational to an anticanonical quartic in $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(3)^{\oplus2}\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(4)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1})$. We give twelve independent sections and construct a projective crepant resolution of the associated Weierstrass model. Varying the fixed elliptic curve gives a family of quartic resolutions that is locally complete at the original member. The resulting fourfold is birational over $\mathbb{C}$ to a diagonal order-four quotient of a product of four elliptic curves with $j$-invariant $1728$, and every smooth projective model has Kodaira dimension zero. An algebraic correspondence identifies the third cohomology of the original quartic resolution with the tensor product of the first cohomology of the fixed elliptic curve and the transcendental cohomology of the modular K3 surface. The Galois representation on the latter factor is associated with a weight-three CM newform.

papers.title: Global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form with applications to dual semigeostrophic equations and periodic homogenization
papers.authors: Guoqing Cui, Chong Gu, Nam Q. Le, Ling Wang, Bin Zhou
papers.abstract: We establish interior and global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Amp\`ere potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. The estimates use the $L^p$ norm of the solution for any $p>1$. A key ingredient is an $L^1$ estimate, with appropriate decay rates, for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Amp\`ere operator in small sections, uniform with respect to the pole. As applications, we obtain uniform H\"older estimates for the time derivatives of the primal and dual potentials in the three-dimensional periodic dual semigeostrophic system when the initial density is bounded away from zero and infinity, and establish a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation.

papers.title: Randomized Matvec Lower Bounds for Simplex-Based Matrix Games
papers.abstract: We prove randomized matrix-vector query lower bounds for two normalized matrix-game geometries: a Euclidean unit ball against a probability simplex, with row norms at most one, and two probability simplices, with entries of absolute value at most one. Each query returns $(Ax,A^\top y)$ for arbitrary real vectors. The algorithm must return a feasible pair with full saddle-point gap at most $\varepsilon$, with probability at least $2/3$ on every admissible matrix. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the worst-case query complexities are $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-2/3}/(\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\log\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ for ball-simplex games and $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-2/3}/(\log^{7/3}(1/\varepsilon)\log\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ for simplex-simplex games. The hard instances have dimensions of order $\varepsilon^{-2/3}$ and $\varepsilon^{-2/3}/\log^{1/3}(1/\varepsilon)$, respectively, and the bounds extend to larger dimensions. These lower bounds match the deterministic upper bounds of Karmarkar, O'Carroll, and Sidford up to logarithmic factors. The proof extracts a fresh Gaussian core after adaptive two-sided queries and uses uncertainty in its smallest singular value to establish linear-system solve hardness. Two reductions transfer this hardness to matrix games by converting a small full gap into a small residual, with an additional logarithmic normalization loss only for simplex-simplex games.

papers.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.

papers.title: Limit law for Brownian cover time of the two dimensional torus
papers.authors: Amir Dembo, Jay Rosen, Ofer Zeitouni
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_\varepsilon$ denote the time it takes a Brownian motion to come within distance $\varepsilon$ of every point in the two dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ of unit area. We prove that for an explicit non-random centering $m_\varepsilon$, the variables $\{\sqrt{\mathcal{C}_{\varepsilon}} - m_\varepsilon \}$ converge in distribution as $\varepsilon \to 0$, to a randomly shifted Gumbel law.

papers.title: Closing the Accuracy Gap in Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We characterize the optimal accuracy dependence for smooth nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with stochastic first-order oracles. For globally unbiased fresh-gradient observations with bounded variance, we prove an $\Omega(\epsilon^{-6})$ lower bound matching the accuracy exponent of existing upper bounds. We consider globally Lipschitz gradients, a bounded upper gradient in the lower variable, and Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks, with target $\mathbb{E}|\nabla F(\widehat{x})|\le\epsilon$. Let $L$ be the common first-order scale, $\mu$ the lower strong-convexity modulus, $\rho$ the lower Hessian-variation budget, $\kappa=L/\mu$, and $\chi=1+\rho/\mu$. For $\rho\gtrsim\mu$, $\chi\lesssim\kappa$, sufficiently high accuracy, and sufficiently large dimension, we establish $\Omega\left(L\kappa^2\Delta\epsilon^{-2}+L^3\chi^2\kappa^8\sigma_g^2\Delta\epsilon^{-6}\right)$, where $\Delta$ is the initial gap budget and $\sigma_g^2$ is the lower-gradient variance budget. The bound holds over full Euclidean spaces against arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms, even when every sample is the gradient of a scalar function. In the common-scale regime $\rho=\Theta(L)$, the leading stochastic term has condition-number dependence $\kappa^{10}$, compared with the achievable $\kappa^{11}$ dependence. The proof embeds a sequential hard objective into an exact lower response while preserving global regularity and finite gap. A multiscale decomposition limits the gradient signal carrying each new direction, yielding the required sample complexity. We complement this lower bound with a frozen-linear-tilt estimator whose bias is proportional to lower Hessian variation. Its analysis makes this structural dependence explicit and yields matching leading rates in the specified curvature-controlled and small-gap regimes.

papers.title: The Minimax Cost of Smoothness in Fully First-Order Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We study the sample complexity of finding a point with expected hypergradient norm at most $\epsilon>0$ in nonconvex--strongly-convex stochastic bilevel optimization using fresh, globally unbiased first-order samples with bounded variance. For lower-variable smoothness order $p\ge1$, F$^2$SA-$p$ achieves $\widetilde O(p\epsilon^{-4-2/p})$ (Chen et al., 2026), but necessity of the exponent $4+2/p$ was open. We prove matching upper and lower bounds $\Theta_p(\epsilon^{-4-2/p})$ under fixed nondegenerate regularity budgets, with constants allowed to depend on $p$. The lower bound holds for unrestricted randomized algorithms under a fixed sample budget, allows dimension to grow with accuracy, and preserves global unbiasedness and all prescribed lower-variable smoothness bounds, even with a scalar lower variable and exact upper gradients. We further characterize the minimax fixed-budget complexity under $L_j=M\Lambda^j(j!)^\beta$ for $j\ge3$: $Q_{p,\beta}^*(\epsilon)=\Theta\left(\epsilon^{-4}\left[\inf_{1\le r\le p,,r\in\mathbb N} r^\beta\epsilon^{-1/r}\right]^2\right)$, for $p\in\mathbb N\cup{\infty}$, with constants independent of $p$. At infinite order, this gives $\Theta(\epsilon^{-4})$ for $\beta=0$ and $\Theta(\epsilon^{-4}\log^2(1/\epsilon))$ for $\beta=1$. A gradient-difference method with weighted independent batches attains these bounds uniformly in order. Thus quantitative smoothness yields precise gains, whereas qualitative analyticity alone still permits $\Theta(\epsilon^{-6})$ complexity.

papers.title: Forcing in bounded arithmetic and set theory: analogies and differences
papers.authors: Radek Honzik, Ondrej Je\v{z}il, Mykyta Narusevych
papers.abstract: We provide a modern overview of several forcing methods in bounded arithmetic and compare them with forcing in set theory. We specifically discuss the countable forcing framework of Atserias and Muller, the restricted ultrapowers of Bydzovsky and Muller, and forcing with random variables developed by Krajicek. We illustrate these forcing arguments by reviewing the Paris--Wilkie forcing and by giving a self-contained construction of the shallow PHP model constructed by Krajicek. We observe that, from a formal point of view, Krajicek's forcing with uncountable structures can be interpreted in the framework of Atserias and Muller after a countable collapse using an LS argument. We further observe that the countable restricted ultrapowers of Bydzovsky and Muller, used to obtain models of the theory $T_{PV}$, can also be interpreted in this framework. This part serves as a primer on modern forcing methods in bounded arithmetic. In the next part, we discuss the analogies and differences between forcing in arithmetic and set theory. We embed Krajicek's Boolean-valued models into generic extensions of models of set theory, observing that the set-theoretic forcing framework can be used to interpret forcing in arithmetics. In our interpretation, set theory offers a convenient method for formalizing forcing arguments with uncountable structures. We end with a question whether analogies with set theory can facilitate the discovery of new uncountable partial orders for arithmetic.

papers.title: Moments and Large Geometric Monodromy for Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$, and $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ for a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb F_p$. For $n\ge2$ we study $\Sigma_n(h)=\sum_{u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n,\sum_i h_i u_i=-\lambda}\psi_q(\sum_i u_i^{-1})$. On $\mathbb G_m^n$ we construct a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$, pure of weight $n+1$ and rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, whose Frobenius traces equal $(-1)^{n-1}q\Sigma_n(h)$ minus an explicit polynomial in $q$, for $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$. For odd $p$, its geometric monodromy has identity component $\mathrm{SL}_{r(n)}$ and cyclic component group of order divisible by $p$. The full group is $\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$ for $n=2$, and for $n\ge3$ using boundary unipotence from the companion preprint arXiv:2610.03081. For $p=2$, the sheaf is self-dual and its geometric monodromy is $\mathrm{SO}_{r(n)}$ for odd $n$ and $\mathrm{Sp}_{r(n)}$ for even $n$. After normalization to weight zero, the arithmetic and geometric groups coincide, using the same companion input for odd $p$ and $n\ge3$. As $q\to\infty$ with $p$ fixed, we obtain Sato-Tate laws for centered, normalized sums with error $O(q^{-1/2})$ for polynomial tests and formulas for all power moments. For $p=2$, limiting moments are Gaussian through order $r(n)-1$, with an excess of one above the orthogonal value at order $r(n)$ for odd $n$; if $n+1$ is a power of two, every Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n$ has eigenvalue $q^{(n+1)/2}$. The proof uses $\sum_h|\Sigma_n(h)|^4=c_pq^{3n-2}+O(q^{3n-2-\delta(n)})$ for $n\ge3$, where $c_p=2$ for odd $p$, $c_2=3$ and $\delta(n)=\min(1,(n-2)/2)$, plane sections of the Cayley cubic, exact Frobenius-Schur identities, Laumon's local Fourier transforms and Artin-Schreier theory. For $n=2$ we identify twisted classical Kloosterman sums and compute the fourth moment exactly.

papers.title: BV rigidity for compact Lie groups and the integral string topology of the symplectic group
papers.authors: Mukilraj K (Indian Institute of Science Education,Research Kolkata, India)
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $\pi_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincar\'e duality. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. We compute, in Hepworth's presentation, the integral BV algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ with its Gerstenhaber bracket, open for $n\geq2$, the running example of the rigidity theorem.

papers.title: Unbounded log-concavity breaks in independence polynomials of spherically symmetric trees
papers.abstract: Using a dioid algebraic structure, we show that there exist spherically symmetric trees $T(2^m 1^n)$ whose independence polynomials exhibit multiple breaks in log-concavity, a result established by estimating the asymptotic growth of the coefficients of these polynomials. Provided the parameter $n$ is a sufficiently large odd integer, the number of breaks is bounded below by the Jacobsthal numbers. This result affirmatively answers a question raised by F. Bencs [D. Galvin, Trees with non log-concave independent set sequences, arXiv 2502.10654.v2].

papers.title: Sharp Truncated Difference Estimates for Nonlocal Nonconvex Functionals Defined by Superlevel Sets
papers.authors: Feng Dai, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao
papers.abstract: Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$. In this article, we consider a family $\{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ of nonlocal nonconvex functionals with a real parameter $\gamma$ and establish two truncated difference estimates bounded by these functionals with the sharp range of $\gamma$; that is, for any $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, any cube $Q\subset\mathbb R^N$, and any measurable function $g:Q\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\int_Q\int_Q\left[\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|-\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}{\ell(Q)^{1+\gamma/p}}\right]_+^p\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad\lesssim \lambda^p\mathop{\int_Q\int_Q}\limits_{\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}>\lambda}\left[\frac{|x-y|}{\ell(Q)}\right]^{\gamma-N}\,dx\,dy=:\frac{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}(g;Q)}{\ell(Q)^{\gamma-N}}, \end{align*} where the implicit positive constant depends only on $N$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, the above estimate holds with the left-most integrand replaced by $\frac{\min\{|g(x)-g(y)|^p,\lambda^p|x-y|^{p+\gamma}\}}{\ell(Q)^{p+\gamma}}$. As applications, these estimates yield related nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities with the sharp range of $\gamma$, and also recover the known $\Gamma$-liminf lower bounds and characterizations of Sobolev and BV spaces in terms of the liminf of the functionals $\{\Phi^\gamma_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\setminus(-1,0]$. We investigate further applications to compactness and variational problems as well as a new VMO criterion. Inspired by a recent work of R. L. Frank, we develop an elementary approach based on dyadic iteration of truncated differences along line segments, which allows us to treat the aforementioned problems in a unified way.

papers.title: Core Coordinates and Negative Support in A-Hypergeometric Systems
papers.abstract: For a homogeneous $A$-hypergeometric system, let $K_v$ be the intersection of the negative support family for a fake exponent $v$, and let $C_w$ be the set of indices of variables that do not occur in any minimal monomial generator of $\operatorname{in}_w(I_A)$. We prove that $K_v=\operatorname{nsupp}(v)\cap C_w$ holds for every parameter and every fake exponent if and only if $\operatorname{Cone}(A_{C_w})$ meets the interior of $\operatorname{Cone}(A)$. We give equivalent criteria using the reduced Gr\"obner basis and the associated regular triangulation. When the condition fails, we construct an infinite family of fake exponents for which the equality fails.

papers.title: Optimal Community Recovery by Spectrally Initialized Variational EM in General Stochastic Block Models
papers.authors: Binghui Liu, Jiangzhou Wang, Man-Chung Yue
papers.abstract: We prove a Chernoff-exponent guarantee for the output of spectrally initialized batch variational EM after a prescribed iteration budget, without assuming global maximization of its variational objective. The iteration repeatedly estimates the entire block probability matrix and community proportions from the same sparse graph. We consider a fixed number of communities with proportions bounded away from zero and fixed, positive, distinct connectivity profiles; neither assortativity nor full rank is required. The algorithm uses simultaneous softmax updates without sample splitting or posterior thresholding. Its analysis must control the feedback between estimated parameters, soft labels and reused edges at an exponentially small risk scale. We establish a uniform one-step bound over data-dependent soft assignments whose random remainder has exponentially small expectation. Combined with an exponentially reliable regularized spectral initializer, this yields an unconditional expected misclassification rate bounded by $\exp\{-(1-o(1))J_n\}$ throughout the sparse, diverging-degree regime, where $J_n$ is the minimum nodewise Chernoff information. Matching lower bounds establish first-order logarithmic minimax optimality on local parameter spaces allowing unknown connectivity and varying community counts. The algorithm also attains the sharp first-order exact-recovery threshold. Numerical experiments illustrate refinement gains and sensitivity to initialization and imbalance.

papers.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
papers.abstract: We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\ge\kappa>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,\kappa$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window.

papers.title: A relaxation to the post-composition approach to metric-valued Sobolev maps
papers.abstract: We establish that the definition of Sobolev mappings from metric measure spaces to metric spaces relying on the post-composition approach of Ambrosio-Reshetnyak admits, under certain transparent assumptions on the spaces, an equivalent reformulation that is substantially weaker than the principal version. In detail, the corresponding definition requires maps of this kind to meet two successive tests in order to be called Sobolev: first a ''qualitative'' one and then a ''quantitative'' one. At the same time, our result allows the relevant conclusion to be drawn based solely on the ''qualitative'' part. Remarkably, the conditions on the spaces sufficient for this to hold fit entirely into the singular flavor of the subject. More explicitly, such a phenomenon emerges if either the source space is of finite Hausdorff dimension and satisfies the Sobolev-to-Luzin-Lipschitz property or the target space is of finite Hausdorff dimension. All this provides a significant generalization of several earlier achievements on the topic.

papers.title: An improved result on Chern conjecture
papers.authors: Qing-Ming Cheng, Fengjiang Li, Guoxin Wei, Jiabin Yin
papers.abstract: Let $X: M^n\to \mathbb S^{n+1}(1)$ be a closed minimal hypersurface with constant scalar curvature. Chern conjecture says that a closed minimal hypersurface with constant scalar curvature, $S\geq 2n$ if $S>n$, where $S$ is the squared norm of the second fundamental form. As a partial result, Peng-Terng \cite{pt1, pt2}, Yang-Cheng \cite{yc1, yc2, yc3} and Suh-Yang \cite{sy} obtained that if $S>n$, then $S>n+ \dfrac{3}7n$. Recently, Chen \cite{c} has proved $S>n+\frac{26}{59}n$ if $S>n$. Since resolving Chern conjecture is a hard problem, as a midway for resolving Chern conjecture, one wants to prove $S>n+\frac12 n$ if $S>n$. In this paper, we give a positive solution for this midway problem. We should remark that our topological condition is complete which is weaker than closed in Chen \cite{c}.

papers.title: Remarks on the critical catenoid and an overdetermined eigenvalue problem in $\Bbb S^2$
papers.abstract: It was recently proved that an embedded minimal annulus with free boundary in the unit ball $\Bbb B^3$ of the Euclidean space is, up to a rotation, the critical catenoid. We prove that an immersed, possibly branched, free boundary minimal annulus in $\Bbb B^3$ with embedded boundary components is necessarily free of branch points and is embedded. This shows the uniqueness of the critical catenoid holds under these weaker hypotheses. We then apply these results to prove that if $\Omega$ is a sufficiently regular annulus in $\Bbb S^2$ for which there exists a smooth function satisfying the overdetermined eigenvalue problem \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} \Delta u+ 2u = 0 \quad \text{on} \quad \Omega\\ \qquad \quad u=0 \quad \text{in}\quad\partial\Omega\\ \quad\,\,\,\, |\nabla u|=1 \quad \text{in}\quad \partial\Omega. \end{cases} \end{equation*} then $\Omega$ is, up to rotation, a rotational annulus with equatorial symmetry.

papers.title: Low Mach number limit of the full Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions and large temperature variations
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Gu, Song Jiang, Qiangchang Ju, Yaobin Ou
papers.abstract: In this paper, we rigorously justify the low Mach number limit of the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional smooth bounded domain, subject to the no-slip boundary condition for the velocity and well-prepared initial data. In the presence of heat conduction and large temperature variations, we establish the uniform estimates for strong solutions on a time interval independent of the Mach number by constructing an energy functional in a Sobolev framework. The no-slip boundary condition cannot provide the vorticity boundary relation used in the slip-boundary setting. To overcome this difficulty, a divergence-free Stokes lifting of the boundary trace for the time derivative of the modified velocity is employed to define a test function vanishing on the boundary, which enables the transfer of a priori estimates from the velocity to the temperature.

papers.title: Uniform Bessel bounds for magnetization crossings in finite Ising chains
papers.abstract: We consider a finite Ising chain in zero field and ask when the all-up configuration is as likely as zero magnetization (magnetization one for an odd number of spins). For both free and periodic ends, the crossing coupling of a long chain is half the logarithm of its length minus half the logarithm of that logarithm, up to a term that vanishes as the length grows. We compute further terms with explicit constants and, for free ends, bound the crossing at every length. The second term is missing from an earlier approximation and explains why an earlier numerical fit gives a slope below one half. To locate the crossing, we compare the known magnetization law with its Bessel approximation. The Bessel approximation is above the exact weight, and we bound its relative error for every length, coupling and magnetization. At the crossing this bound tends to zero. The central bin still has about as many domain walls as the logarithm of the length on average, so the crossing has a coupling width of order the inverse logarithm. In a fixed positive dimensionless field the last crossing comes from near the edge of the row, at a coupling of about a quarter of the logarithm of the length. For long chains it is the one-spin crossing when the field exceeds half the logarithm of two. Below that value another bin crosses later.

papers.title: Graphic additive bases and graph flows
papers.abstract: The lattice-coset method of Alon, Buci\'c, and Davies gives real solutions with controlled coordinates. We combine it with integer rounding to prescribe outdegrees and flows from spanning-tree packing. For every integer $q\ge3$, $q$ edge-disjoint spanning trees suffice for every outdegree prescription modulo $q$ whose sum is compatible with the number of edges. The tree count is optimal even for simple graphs. A common interval theorem extends the argument to totally unimodular matrices; for graphs, its partition inequalities admit a sharp allowance of two. Fractional packing characterizes when every prescription has a strongly connected realization and gives circular-flow bounds. In particular, for every integer $k\ge1$, every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly below $2+1/k$, with optimal connectivity for this strict inequality. As a structural application, every four-edge-connected graph with no bond of size six, seven or eight has a nowhere-zero three-flow. Further consequences concern star decompositions, antisymmetric flows and contraction.

papers.title: Biquandle-Based Invariants of Virtual Knotoids and Connected Sum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the behavior of biquandle-based invariants of virtual knotoids under their connected sum. We first show that the fundamental biquandle of the connected sum of two virtual knotoids is the pushout of a span in the category of biquandles. By applying the Hom functor to this pushout description, we obtain the correspondence between biquandle colorings of $K_1 \# K_2$ and compatible pairs of colorings of summands. This provides a categorical explanation of a known matrix product formula for biquandle counting matrices under connected sum. We then study the behavior of biquandle virtual bracket invariants under connected sum. We introduce normalized multiset invariants derived from biquandle virtual brackets and show that they are strictly stronger than their unnormalized versions in certain cases by an explicit example. Furthermore, we show that for each coloring of the connected sum $K_1 \# K_2$ corresponding to a compatible pair of colorings of the summands $K_1$ and $K_2$, the normalized biquandle virtual bracket value factors as the product of the normalized values of the summands. Building on this, we obtain connected-sum formulas for the normalized multiset invariants defined by utilizing biquandle virtual brackets. When the coefficient ring is a number ring, the normalized bracket multisets can be encoded by polynomials and matrices with polynomial entries. We introduce an induced matrix product $\odot$ and show that the normalized biquandle virtual bracket matrices satisfy \begin{equation} \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1 \# K_2) = \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1) \odot \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_2). \end{equation}

papers.title: On the number of cokernel-closed additive subcategories for uniformly oriented $A_n$ quivers
papers.abstract: We study the integer sequence that enumerates cokernel-closed, idempotent split, full, additive subcategories of the category of finite dimensional complex representations of a uniformly oriented $A_n$ quiver. Using a combinatorial model, we describe a non-obvious connection of this sequence to Catalan numbers and derive an implicit recurrence. We also describe some basic properties of the lattice underlying the sequences, in particular, we give an explicit description of the meet irreducible elements of that lattice.

papers.title: On the Information Bottleneck for Stable Variables
papers.authors: Dongmin Park, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad
papers.abstract: We consider a generalization of the Gaussian information bottleneck problem to jointly stable variables $X$ and $Y$. Specifically, for $X = Y + A$, where $A$ is stable and independent of $Y$, we find optimal stable linear encoders of the form $T = kX + N$, with $N$ stable and independent of $X$. We characterize the linear stable information bottleneck in closed-form and its critical value. Furthermore, we show that, except for the Gaussian case, such stochastic linear encoders are strictly suboptimal, while becoming asymptotically optimal at large compression rates. Our linear solution recovers the Gaussian information bottleneck for jointly Gaussian variables as a special case.

papers.title: High-order entropy-stable isothermal wall boundary condition for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: Entropy-stable boundary conditions are critical for ensuring that the corresponding numerical scheme satisfies the discrete entropy inequality, thus mimicking the second law of thermodynamics for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations discretely. Provably entropy-stable adiabatic wall boundary conditions were introduced in Parsani 2014~\cite{parsani2014entropy}. These discrete wall boundary conditions were further generalized in Dalcin 2019~\cite{dalcin2019conservative} to a moving adiabatic solid wall or a wall with a prescribed heat flux for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations discretized by using summation-by-parts (SBP) and simultaneous-approximation-term (SAT) operators. Currently, no entropy-stable formulation using SBP-SAT operators for isothermal wall boundary conditions is available in the literature. This paper presents new isothermal no-slip wall boundary conditions that: 1) enforce the $T|_{y=0}=T^{wall}$ and $\vec{v}|_{y=0}=\vec{v}^{wall}$ conditions with the design order of accuracy while maintaining stability, 2) provide the correct sign of entropy production at the wall, and 3) mimic the entropy balance of the Navier-Stokes equations at the discrete level. The structure-preserving and design-order properties of the proposed methodology are demonstrated and verified on standard benchmark problems for compressible flows.

papers.title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization
papers.abstract: How can structured transformations of data improve regularizer design for inverse problems? We address this question through anisotropic dilation, a direction-preserving map that rescales each point along its Euclidean ray by a positive profile on the sphere. Our analysis builds on a characterization of optimal regularizers within a broad Gibbs class, where the regularizer best matched to a distribution $P$ is determined by a direction-dependent radial summary statistic $\rho_P$. We show that anisotropic dilation acts explicitly and transitively on the space of radial summary statistics: any prescribed optimal regularizer in this class can be obtained by transforming an admissible source distribution using a single explicit profile. We characterize the resulting distributional orbits and establish conditions under which this control of regularizer geometry yields a weakly convex denoising formulation even when the original objective is not weakly convex. We also derive in closed form the profile that optimally adapts a fixed base regularizer to data. Its improvement over isotropic rescaling with respect to KL divergence is governed by a Jensen gap, for which we establish strict positivity under explicit conditions for several natural families of distributions. For jointly learning the base regularizer and anisotropic profile from samples, we establish finite-sample generalization bounds, with explicit rates when the logarithm of the profile is parameterized by linear feature models or sparse ReLU networks. Experiments on a controlled two-dimensional family and on MNIST denoising demonstrate that learning the anisotropic profile can improve reconstruction performance for both handcrafted and learned base regularizers.

papers.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{\k{a}}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.

papers.title: Positive Lin-Lu-Yau curvature, planar graphs, and forbidden minors
papers.abstract:
Over the past few decades, several notions of graph curvature have been introduced. Among them, Ollivier curvature, defined through optimal transport, and its Lin--Lu--Yau variant provide notions of curvature for graphs which retain several features of their counterpart in Riemannian geometry. A classical problem in this context is to understand the global structure of positively curved spaces.
  Lu and Wang proved that there are only finitely many positively curved planar graphs of minimum degree at least 3. In this paper, we study two directions motivated by this result. We first show that for fixed $2\leq s\leq t$, there are only finitely many positively curved $K_{s,t}$-minor-free graphs with minimum degree at least $s$. In particular, this generalizes the result of Lu and Wang to graphs embeddable on any fixed surface. We then give a complete classification of positively curved 5-connected plane triangulations. In particular, we show that there are only five examples, on 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17 vertices.

papers.title: Cocycle Relations and Elliptic Gamma Values
papers.abstract: Recent work of Bergeron-Charollois-Garc\'ia proposed a conjectural analytic expression for elliptic units for complex cubic fields as the special values of smoothed quotients of elliptic Gamma functions. These values depend on the conductor ideal, ray class group element, smoothing ideal, and an admissible element $h$. If this analytic expression is to fit into the framework of explicit class field theory, then, as in the case of torsion points on CM elliptic curves, the resulting complex number should depend only on the congruence class of $h$ modulo a fractional ideal. This conjecture has been supported by much numerical evidence. In this paper, we use the cocycle relations of the smoothed elliptic Gamma function to prove that the construction is indeed independent of $h$.

papers.title: The packing spectrum: interpolation between Hausdorff and packing dimensions
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of metric outer measures whose critical exponents form a packing spectrum interpolating between Hausdorff and packing dimensions. For analytic sets, we characterize each spectral value as the supremum of the Hausdorff dimension of a product with a compact testing set minus the testing set's upper intermediate dimension at the complementary parameter. The associated product bounds refine the classical Hausdorff--packing inequalities and can give exact Hausdorff additivity when both factors have distinct endpoint dimensions. Below the packing endpoint, we prove a variational principle in terms of windowed local mass exponents and sharp parameter estimates implying local Lipschitz continuity; a jump at the endpoint is possible. We characterize all attainable profiles by monotonicity, continuity below the packing endpoint, and a sharp upper right Dini-derivative bound. Every admissible profile is realized by a compact binary digit set whose uniform measure attains the finite-window and classical packing variational suprema. Complementary digit positions yield reflected upper intermediate-dimension profiles and a single factor attaining the Hausdorff product bounds at every parameter, with an Ahlfors regular product measure.

papers.title: A Local Approximation Characterization of Oka Manifolds
papers.authors: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie
papers.abstract: We introduce the local approximation propert (LAP) and prove that it characterizes Oka manifolds. We prove that LAP yields convex approximation and, in an $n$-dimensional target, propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Consequently, strong dominability characterizes Oka manifolds, convex approximation in the target dimension suffices, the Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps. Local families of entire curves give geometric applications: smooth projective rationally connected manifolds are Oka, and deleting an algebraic subset of codimension at least two from any such manifold preserves the Oka property. Structure theorems further show that compact K\"ahler manifolds with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature or nef tangent bundle are Oka. Finally, the complement of a smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is Oka exactly when $d\leq n+1$.

papers.title: Oka manifolds are ubiquitous
papers.authors: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie
papers.abstract: We prove that a holomorphic family of connected complex Lie groups has Oka total space if and only if its base is Oka. Extension presentations and generating sections give Oka results for stable and parabolic bundle moduli and for holomorphic mapping and embedding spaces. Every nonempty degree component of maps from a compact Oka curve to projective space is Oka; rational-function spaces are also holomorphically elliptic. For a vector bundle on a smooth projective curve, the Oka property of its nested Quot scheme is equivalent to that of the symmetric powers determined by the length increments. Complete Hamiltonian flows give holomorphic ellipticity of irreducible \(\mathrm{SL}_2\)- and \(\mathrm{GL}_2\)-character and representation loci, for closed surfaces of genus at least two and for surfaces with fixed regular semisimple boundary classes. The Riemann--Hilbert correspondence yields Oka moduli spaces of nonresonant parabolic connections for arbitrary parabolic weights, and holomorphic ellipticity when reducible monodromy is absent. A proper holomorphic fibration over a Riemann surface, with a section and connected complex tori as smooth general fibres, has Oka total space exactly when its base is Oka. For a Schoen fibre product \(X\) of rational elliptic surfaces with disjoint singular values, we construct an entire local biholomorphism \(\mathbb C^3\to X\) whose image contains a dense Zariski-open subset. Further applications treat Hilbert schemes, compactified relative Jacobians, and logarithmic complements.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
papers.abstract: This is the first of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on stability. An observable is stable when the order in which the two systems are idealized never changes its expectation value, and this is Shelah's stability. Its classical characterizations, in model theory and in analysis, acquire a physical meaning: idealized preparations are simulated by finite mixtures of actual ones, and adaptive probes can tell apart only polynomially many preparations.

papers.title: Convexity preservation for first-order nonlinear evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We study preservation of spatial convexity for viscosity solutions of first order Hamilton-Jacobi evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions in bounded convex domains. Under a monotonicity assumption on the Hamiltonian in the outward normal direction, every viscosity supersolution of the Neumann problem is also a state-constraint supersolution. This reduces the boundary difficulty to a state-constraint problem and enables us to prove convexity preservation via the convex-envelope argument established by Alvarez, Lasry and Lions (1997). We also obtain propagation estimates for semiconvexity and strong convexity under similar structural assumptions.

papers.title: A rank bound for bases and circuits in binary matroids
papers.abstract:
Let \(b(M)\), \(d(M)\), and \(r(M)\) denote the number of bases, the number of circuits, and the rank of a matroid \(M\), respectively. We prove that every nonempty simple binary matroid with no coloops satisfies \[
  2b(M)\ge(r(M)+1)d(M), \] with equality if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to the Fano matroid. This confirms a conjecture recorded by Oxley in 1983. For the same class, we prove that deleting any element leaves at least as many bases as there are circuits in the original matroid: \(b(M\backslash e)\ge d(M)\) for every \(e\in E(M)\). We determine all equality cases and deduce a sharp linear lower bound for basis growth under successive series extensions. We also give a circuit-size exclusion condition guaranteeing distinct bases containing \(C-e\) for circuit-element pairs \((C,e)\) with prescribed circuit sizes.

papers.title: Geodesically Convex Optimization in Hyperbolic Space: Matching Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish matching lower bounds for deterministic first-order optimization of globally Lipschitz geodesically convex functions on hyperbolic space. A global minimizer lies within distance $r$ of a known point, each query returns an exact function value and a selected Riemannian subgradient, and the target objective gap is $\varepsilon Lr$, where $L$ is the Lipschitz constant. For sectional curvature $-k^2<0$, let $\rho=kr$ and $\zeta=\rho/\tanh\rho$. The optimal worst-case query complexity $Q^\star$, taken uniformly over dimensions, satisfies $Q^\star(\rho,\varepsilon)=\Theta(\zeta\varepsilon^{-2})$ for every $\rho>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/64$. The new lower bound covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries and arbitrary outputs, matching the projected-subgradient upper rate of Zhang and Sra (2016). It removes the geodesic-span and historical-halfspace restrictions of earlier matching lower bounds. The construction extends a radial source from a convex carrier with boundary. A small residual cut selects minimizer candidates while an exact hyperbolic persistence inequality keeps every historical contact valid under future carrier growth. One fixed globally convex objective and one fixed subgradient selection consequently realize all exact replies simultaneously. Each query consumes $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of a geometric potential whose available budget is $\Theta(\zeta)$, yielding the product lower bound in a dimension linear in the query horizon.

papers.title: Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves
papers.abstract: Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geometric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently established Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for weighted occupation times of supercritical superprocesses
papers.abstract: Suppose $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a supercritical superprocess with a non-local branching mechanism on a Lusin space $E$, whose mean semigroup admits a positive leading eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ with a bounded positive eigenfunction $\varphi$ and a finite eigenmeasure $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Let $Y_t:=\int_0^t X_s\mathrm{d}s$ be its occupation measure. We first prove a law of large numbers, that is, for every bounded measurable function $f$, $e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ converges in $L^2$ to $\lambda_1^{-1}\langle f,\widetilde{\varphi}\rangle W^\varphi_\infty$, where $W^\varphi_\infty$ is the limit of the martingale $W^\varphi_t:=e^{-\lambda_1 t}\langle\varphi,X_t\rangle$. We then establish functional central limit theorems for the fluctuations of $\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ around this random centering. We show that the normalisation and the limit are determined by the spectral decay rate of $f$ compared with the critical value $\lambda_1/2$, and there are three possible regimes: after suitable normalisation, the fluctuation process converges in distribution in $\mathcal{C}[0,+\infty)$ either to a mixed Gaussian process $\sqrt{W^{\varphi}_{\infty}}G(f)$, or to a constant Gaussian process with random variance depending on $W^{\varphi}_{\infty}$, or to a non-Gaussian limit given by the limit of a martingale associated with the spectral projection of $f$. These results are the occupation-time counterparts of the fluctuation theorems for instantaneous linear functionals of supercritical non-local branching superprocesses.

papers.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
papers.authors: Catalin Carstea, Matti Lassas, Tony Liimatainen, Leo Tzou
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the

papers.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
papers.abstract:
We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(\zeta(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(\Phi(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels.
  In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(\chi\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_\chi(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^\chi(x) = L(-n,\chi,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_\chi(t) = \chi(-1)A_\chi(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^\chi\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,\chi)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.

papers.title: Relaxed Centralized Circumcentered-Reflection Methods for Convex Feasibility: Convergence and Finite Termination
papers.authors: Vincent Guigues, Roger Behling, Adriana Henarejos
papers.abstract: Projection methods are among the most widely used techniques for solving convex feasibility problems due to their simplicity and robustness. However, classical projection-based algorithms and existing circumcentered-reflection methods generally provide only asymptotic convergence. In this paper, we introduce a relaxed version of the centralized circumcentered-reflection method (cCRM) obtained through an extrapolation of the circumcenter step. We first analyze the two-set case and then extend the proposed approach to the successive framework for multiple convex sets, including under- and over-relaxation and a backtracking strategy. The convergence analysis establishes Fej\'er monotonicity and global convergence under suitable conditions, while local error-bound assumptions yield linear convergence and standard regularity assumptions imply superlinear convergence. Motivated by finitely convergent projection methods based on perturbed feasible sets, we further investigate a perturbed relaxed formulation designed to achieve finite termination. Numerical experiments show good practical performance, comparable to and competitive with the finitely convergent PACA method. The results also provide clear numerical evidence of finite termination in the tested instances.

papers.title: A lower bound for additive complements to the primes
papers.abstract: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erd\H{o}s Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive.

papers.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.

papers.title: From almost tight $p$-group enumeration to $2$-group domination among finite groups
papers.abstract:
Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. The pioneering works of Higman (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) and Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965), with improvement by Newman and Seeley, establish that \[ \frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac{4}{9}m^2+\Omega(m)\leq \log_p f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^{5/2}). \] In the same paper in 1965, Sims speculated on improving the error term ($O(m^{8/3})$ at that time) in the upper bound. To show that $f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^2)$ is now known as Sims' conjecture.
  Our first main result proves Sims' conjecture in a strong form as follows: \[ \log_p f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac{4}{9}m^2+O(m). \]
  Techniques developed to prove the above lead to progress on some well-known open questions in group enumeration in affirmative, including:
  (1) 2-group domination in finite group enumeration (Pyber, \emph{Eur. Congr. Math.}, 1996): Let $F(n)$ be the number of groups of order $\leq n$, and $F_2(n)$ be the number of $2$-groups of order $\leq n$. Then $$ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{F_2(n)}{F(n)} =1. $$
  (2) A question attributed to Higman and Erd\H{o}s (see Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman, \emph{Cambridge Tracts in Maths.}, 2007) when $m$ is large enough: $$ \text{for } 1<n<2^m, f(n)<f(2^m). $$ Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalisation by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-\Omega(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bl\"aser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term.

papers.title: The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite Artin algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation-finite Artin algebra of finite global dimension has integral Cartan determinant one.

papers.title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
papers.authors: JiaJia Han, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang
papers.abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.

papers.title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
papers.authors: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Yanmei Hong, Wang Xi, Jinze Hu
papers.abstract:
For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number. Let $\mathcal K_k(F)$ be the expanded graph obtained by adding $k-2$ new vertices to each edge of $F$, with disjoint sets of new vertices for distinct edges.
  Mubayi proved that, for every clique $K_r$ with $r\ge4$ and fixed $ q>0$, $
  h_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,q)\ge qt_{\mathcal K_3(K_r)}(n,1)$ for every sufficiently large $n$. Pikhurko and Yilma later proved that, for every color-critical graph $F$, there is a constant $\epsilon_F>0$ such that $h_{F}(n,q)=t_{F}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon_F n$. We extend this equality to expanded color-critical graphs. Let $d>k\ge3$. For every color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F)=d+1$,
  there is a constant $\epsilon>0$ such that $ h_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)=t_{\mathcal K_k(F)}(n,q)$ for every sufficiently large $n$ and $1\le q\le\epsilon n^{k-1}$. Let $q_L(n)$ be the largest integer $q$ such that $h_L(n,s)=t_L(n,s)$ for every integer $1\le s\le q$. We give a sufficient condition for $q_L(n)=\Theta_L(n^{k-1})$ and an explicit family satisfying it. We also give a different sufficient condition under which $q_L(n)=\Omega_L(n^{k-1/2})$ and an explicit family satisfying it.
  \noindent
  \emph{Keywords.}
  Supersaturation; extremal graph; color-critical graph; chromatic number; expanded graph; hypergraph.

papers.title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
papers.authors: Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie
papers.abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative rough singular integrals
papers.authors: Junming Cao, Wei Li, Lian Wu
papers.abstract: We establish the weak type \((1,1)\) endpoint estimate for operator-valued rough singular integrals with kernels satisfying the classical \(L\log L\) integrability and cancellation conditions. This extends Seeger's endpoint theorem [{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{9} (1996)] to the noncommutative setting. A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.

papers.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
papers.abstract:
We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$.
  In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.

papers.title: Uniform Asymptotics for Andrews-Beck Partition Statistics
papers.abstract: Let $\NT(m,n)$ be the total number of parts in the partitions of $n$ with rank $m$, and let $\MW(m,n)$ be the total number of ones in the partitions of $n$ with crank $m$. Using the uniform generalized-rank estimate of Liu and Zhou, we establish asymptotic formulas for $NT(m,n)$ and $\MW(m,n)$. Put $\beta_n=\pi/\sqrt{6n}$ and $L_n=\log(1/\beta_n)$. For every fixed $A>0$, uniformly for $|m|\le A\sqrt n$, we prove \begin{align*} \NT(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)L_n}{4}\sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\log L_n\bigr) \intertext{ and} \MW(m,n)&=\frac{p(n)}4\log(1+e^{-\beta_nm}) \sech^2\!\left(\frac{\beta_nm}{2}\right) +O_A\!\bigl(p(n)\sqrt{\beta_nL_n}\bigr). \end{align*}

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and combine local boundary analysis with a global argument on an algebraic curve. We exclude Diagrams~1, 2, 4, 6 and~8 for complex germs, Diagram~7 on curves through real configurations, and Diagram~3 on curves with a positive arc. For Diagrams~5 and~9, direct order estimates show that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances tends to zero. On a hypothetical curve containing a positive arc, a first pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. On the completed curve, $\Delta$ must then have a pole elsewhere. The identity $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$ forces a four-product to have a pole there, contradicting the same vanishing conclusion. The computer-assisted inputs concern Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 and use exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).

papers.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
